# HTML on circles.

Orbit is a CSS layout system for things that grow around a center: gauges, dials, knobs, radial menus, donut charts, watch faces. You write plain HTML with a few classes. Orbit does the trigonometry.

[How Orbit thinks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/universe.html)
[See examples](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/index.html)
[Star on GitHub](https://github.com/zumerlab/orbit)

`npm install @zumer/orbit`

## A small solar system

Orbit borrows its words from the sky. It sounds like a gimmick for about a minute. After that it is the easiest way to remember what each piece does.

- `.bigbang` The universe. Its box is the only size you set.
- `.gravity-spot` The center. Its gravity reaches the edge of the universe.
- `.orbit-1` … `.orbit-12` Twelve lanes from the center out to that edge.
- `.satellite` Travels a lane. Orbit spreads them around it and keeps your content upright.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
      <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded" role="progressbar" aria-label="Upload" aria-valuenow="72"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 12">
      <div class="satellite at-center">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong>72%</strong><span>uploaded</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<label class="controls">Value <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72"></label>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
  height: 100vh;
  padding: 20px 16px 14px;
}
.bigbang { max-height: 100%; }
.controls { justify-content: center; }
/* cqmin: a share of the satellite, so the number scales with the ring. */
.readout strong { font-size: 22cqmin; }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
```

```js
const ring = document.querySelector('o-progress');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  ring.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  ring.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', e.target.value);
  document.querySelector('strong').textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

A whole Orbit: a progress ring and a label. Nothing in it has a size in pixels, so the same markup works as a badge or a full-screen dial. Move the slider, or open the code and change it.

## Start somewhere

- [How Orbit thinks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/universe.html): The model in one page, with live examples. Read this first.
- [Build a knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/guide.html): From an empty box to a control you can drag, step by step.
- [Examples](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/index.html): Full pages with live controls, and small layouts to copy: gauges, a radar, watches, depth in 3D.
- [Orbit Kit](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/index.html): Ready-made gauges, donuts, knobs and clocks, one tag each.
- [Coming from 1.x](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/migrating.html): What changed in 2.0, and one line to keep everything as it was.

Orbit is open source under the MIT license, made by [Zumerlab](https://github.com/zumerlab). If it saves you time, you can [sponsor its development](https://github.com/sponsors/tinchox5). Using Orbit 1.x? Its [documentation](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit-docs/) stays online.

# How Orbit thinks

Every Orbit layout is a tiny universe. Once the four words in this page click, the rest of Orbit is details.

## The universe

A `.bigbang` is the universe: the space your layout lives in. It is square by default, as wide as its parent, and a parent with a height keeps it from growing taller. Its box is the only size you ever set.

Inside it, a `.gravity-spot` is the center. Its gravity reaches as far as the shorter side of the universe, and that reach is split into 12 lanes. `orbit-12` touches the edge, `orbit-6` is halfway, `orbit-1` hugs the center.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-1"></div>
    <div class="orbit-2"></div>
    <div class="orbit-3"></div>
    <div class="orbit-4"></div>
    <div class="orbit-5"></div>
    <div class="orbit-6 half">
      <div class="satellite angle-90"><div class="capsule tag">orbit-6</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-7"></div>
    <div class="orbit-8"></div>
    <div class="orbit-9"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10"></div>
    <div class="orbit-11"></div>
    <div class="orbit-12 edge">
      <div class="satellite angle-90"><div class="capsule tag">orbit-12</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The universe, tinted so you can see it. */
.bigbang {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, var(--panel));
}
/* Rings are invisible; these borders only draw the lanes. */
[class*="orbit-"] {
  border: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--faint) 70%, transparent);
}
.half, .edge {
  border: 1.5px solid var(--accent);
}
.tag {
  padding: 2px 7px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--accent);
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  white-space: nowrap;
}
```

The light area is the universe. The preview is wider than it is tall, so the shorter side, 300px, sets the reach. There is also `orbit-0`, the center itself, and `orbit-13` to `orbit-24` past the edge, for things that should stick out.

## Things on the lanes

Rings hold things. A `.satellite` carries your content in a `.capsule`; Orbit spreads all the satellites of a ring evenly around it, and the capsule keeps the content upright wherever it ends up.

Every element on a ring is **one lane thick**. A satellite on `orbit-8` is a circle one lane across. To make things bigger or smaller, set `--o-size-ratio`, counted in lanes, on the element, on its ring or on the whole `.gravity-spot`:

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-3">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">1</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">1</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">1</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-7" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">2</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">2</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">2</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">2</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
[class*="orbit-"] {
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
.satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--bg);
  color: var(--bg);
  font: 600 12px/1 var(--mono);
}
/* The number is the thickness, in lanes. */
.orbit-7 .satellite { font-size: 14px; }
.orbit-10 .satellite { font-size: 18px; }
```

An element on `orbit-N` reaches half its thickness past lane N, so a band two lanes thick on `orbit-11` ends exactly at the edge.

## One box, any size

Because every ring, satellite and band is a fraction of the universe, a layout scales as one piece. You do not write breakpoints for it, and you do not call anything. Drag the corner of the dotted box:

```html
<div class="box">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-progress value="64" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-6" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 6">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>64</strong></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* Drag the corner: the system follows the box. */
.box {
  width: 220px;
  height: 220px;
  margin: 20px;
  resize: both;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
  border-radius: 10px;
}
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.orbit-6 .satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--amber);
}
```

If you need a fixed size instead, give the reach a length on the `.gravity-spot`: `--o-force: 400px`.

## Universes inside universes

A satellite is a universe too. Put a `.gravity-spot` inside one and its reach is the satellite's edge, like a moon system around a planet. Every `.gravity-spot` starts from the defaults, so the inner system does not inherit sizes or angles from the outer one.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
      <div class="satellite at-center sun"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-8 path" style="--o-size-ratio: 5">
      <div class="satellite system">
        <!-- A system inside a satellite: the planet and its moons. -->
        <div class="gravity-spot">
          <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 9">
            <div class="satellite at-center planet"></div>
          </div>
          <div class="orbit-10 moons" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
            <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            <div class="satellite moon"></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="satellite system">
        <div class="gravity-spot">
          <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 7">
            <div class="satellite at-center planet"></div>
          </div>
          <div class="orbit-10 moons" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
            <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            <div class="satellite moon"></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.satellite { border-radius: 50%; }
.sun {
  background: var(--amber);
  box-shadow: 0 0 24px color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 60%, transparent);
}
.path { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
.moons { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); }
.planet { background: var(--accent); }
.moon { background: var(--muted); }
/* Turning a ring turns everything on it, inner systems included. */
.path { animation: turn 40s linear infinite; }
.moons { animation: turn 6s linear infinite; }
@keyframes turn { to { rotate: 1turn; } }
```

Each planet is a satellite of the sun's `orbit-8`, five lanes thick. Inside it, a whole new system: the planet in its center and its moons on its own `orbit-10`, measured against the planet's satellite, not against the page.

## Angles

Angles start at the top and grow clockwise. `--o-range` is how much of the circle a ring uses and `--o-from` where it starts. A speedometer is a ring that uses 240° and starts at 240°, so its gap sits at the bottom:

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-10 whole"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-range: 240deg; --o-from: 240deg; --o-size-ratio: 2">
      <o-arc class="ok"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="ok"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="ok"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="warn"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="bad"></o-arc>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-8 fit-range" style="--o-range: 240deg; --o-from: 240deg">
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 8">
      <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>240°</strong><span>from 240°</span></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The full circle, for reference: the unused 120° is the gap. */
.whole { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
o-arc { --o-gap: 3; --o-stroke: none; }
.ok { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
.warn { --o-fill: var(--amber); }
.bad { --o-fill: var(--coral); }
.vector { height: 2px; background: var(--faint); }
.readout strong { font-size: 30px; }
```

Without `value`, sibling arcs share the ring equally. `fit-range` puts the first and last tick on the two ends of the range instead of leaving a step at the end. Classes like `range-240`, `from-240` and `ccw` cover the usual values.

## Which way is out

Each satellite also knows where it sits: `--o-dir-x` and `--o-dir-y` are its direction from the center, from `-1` to `1` (`y` grows down). Use them to hang labels outward, here above the satellites of the upper half and below the rest:

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.5">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Mercury</span></div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Venus</span></div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Earth</span></div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Mars</span></div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Jupiter</span></div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Saturn</span></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<label class="controls">Turn the ring <input type="range" min="0" max="360" value="0"> <output>0°</output></label>
```

```css
.orbit-8 { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
.capsule { aspect-ratio: 1; }
.dot {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
}
.label {
  /* -1 in the upper half, 1 in the lower half */
  --side: clamp(-1, var(--o-dir-y) * 1000, 1);
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  top: calc(50% + var(--side) * (50% + 4px));
  translate: -50% calc((var(--side) - 1) * 50%);
  font-size: 13px;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
.controls {
  position: fixed;
  left: 16px;
  bottom: 14px;
}
```

```js
// Move the ring's start angle: labels switch sides as they cross the middle.
const ring = document.querySelector('.orbit-8');
const input = document.querySelector('input');
input.addEventListener('input', () => {
  ring.style.setProperty('--o-from', input.value + 'deg');
  document.querySelector('output').value = input.value + '°';
});
```

## The whole map

```
.bigbang                          the universe: its box sets the size
└── .gravity-spot                 the center; reaches the shorter side
    ├── .orbit-N                  a lane, N twelfths of the way out
    │   ├── .satellite > .capsule ← your content
    │   ├── .vector · .side       rays and chords
    │   └── <o-arc> · <o-progress>
    └── .orbit-M …
```

- Rings are direct children of a `.gravity-spot`, never of another ring.
- A ring holds only `.satellite`, `.vector`, `.side`, `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`.
- Content goes in a `.capsule` inside a `.satellite`. Centered content goes in `.orbit-0 > .satellite.at-center > .capsule`.

Add `dev-orbit` to the `.bigbang` while you build: it draws the lanes, outlines anything in the wrong place and explains it in the console. More in [Visual aids](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/visual-aids.html).

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/install.html

# Install

Orbit is two files: a stylesheet and a small runtime. Load both. The CSS does the geometry and the look; the runtime registers `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`, numbers the rings and keeps everything drawn as your layout changes.

## From npm

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

Then, in the entry file of your app:

```js
import '@zumer/orbit/style';
import '@zumer/orbit';
```

The package is safe to import during server rendering. Import it in the browser entry too, so it can register the elements and watch the page. It exports `Orbit`, `OrbitArc`, `OrbitProgress` and `registerOrbit`; registration happens on import.

## From a CDN

Load it from unpkg. This always gets the latest release; add a version after the name (`@zumer/orbit@2`) if you want it to change only when you decide.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.min.css">
<script defer src="https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.min.js"></script>
```

The script puts the API on `window.Orbit`. To load it as an ES module instead: `import { Orbit } from 'https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.mjs'`.

## What is in the package

Everything lives in `dist/`. You can [browse it on unpkg](https://unpkg.com/browse/@zumer/orbit/dist/).

| File | Import as | What it is |
| `orbit.css`, `orbit.min.css` | `@zumer/orbit/style` | The stylesheet: geometry, reset, default theme, `theme-cyan`, the color palette and `dev-orbit`. About 18 kB gzipped. |
| `orbit.mjs` | `@zumer/orbit` (import) | The runtime as an ES module. |
| `orbit.js`, `orbit.min.js` | `@zumer/orbit` (require) | The runtime as a classic script that sets `window.Orbit`. About 9 kB gzipped. |
| `orbit.d.ts`, `style.d.ts` | | TypeScript types for the API, the elements and the stylesheet import. |
| `react.d.ts` | `@zumer/orbit/react` | JSX types for `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`. Types only, no code. See [React](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/react.html). |
| `custom-elements.json` | `@zumer/orbit/custom-elements.json` | A [Custom Elements Manifest](https://custom-elements-manifest.open-wc.org/) for tools that read one. |
| `vscode.html-custom-data.json` | `@zumer/orbit/vscode.html-custom-data.json` | Attribute completion for VS Code. |

To get that completion, add this to `.vscode/settings.json`:

```json
{ "html.customData": ["./node_modules/@zumer/orbit/dist/vscode.html-custom-data.json"] }
```

## Try it

A layout is a `.bigbang` with a `.gravity-spot` inside, and rings inside that. Put things on the rings: satellites with your content, arcs, progress, ticks. This one is a ring of eight satellites around a label. Edit it here, or press *Copy page* and save it as an `index.html`: it loads Orbit from unpkg and needs nothing else.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 8">
      <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule label">Orbit</div></div>
    </div>
    <!-- Eight satellites: Orbit spreads them around the ring. -->
    <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.5">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">1</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">2</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">3</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">4</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">5</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">6</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">7</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">8</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.orbit-8 {
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
.orbit-8 .satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 16%, var(--panel));
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent);
  color: var(--accent);
  font: 600 15px var(--mono);
  transition: background .2s, color .2s;
}
.orbit-8 .satellite:hover {
  background: var(--accent);
  color: var(--bg);
}
.label {
  font-size: 24px;
  font-weight: 650;
  letter-spacing: -.02em;
}
```

## When something looks wrong

Orbit explains common mistakes in the browser console, in messages that start with `[orbit]`. Messages about structure appear when `dev-orbit` is on the `.bigbang`; the others always appear. [Visual aids](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/visual-aids.html) shows what `dev-orbit` draws.

| You see | Because | Fix |
| Nothing, and the console says *has no size* | The `.bigbang` is 0px wide or tall, usually in a parent that shrinks to fit. | Give the `.bigbang` or its parent a width. |
| A layout as big as the window | The `.gravity-spot` is not inside a `.bigbang`, so it measures the viewport. | Wrap it in a `.bigbang`. |
| An empty arc or ring | `value` is not a number, or `max` is not positive. | Fix the attribute; the console names it. |
| Content overlapping or off the ring | It sits directly in a ring instead of a `.satellite`. | Add `dev-orbit` to see where, then wrap it. |
| Curved text cut off | The text is longer than its arc. | Shorten it, widen `--o-range`, use `range="auto"`, or `fit-range`. |
| Everything thin | Elements are one lane thick. | Raise `--o-size-ratio` on the ring or the system. |
| An arc that ignores clicks | Arcs are decorative by default. | Add `interactive`, and `hit-width` for a bigger target. |
| The console says *Orbit.resize() has nothing to do here* | The system already scales with its `.bigbang`. | Remove the call. See [Runtime and resizing](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html). |

## Browser support

Orbit needs CSS `sin()`, `cos()` and container query units, which current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari all have. In a browser without trigonometric functions, each `.bigbang` turns into a red box that asks for an update.

Without JavaScript, a CSS fallback still places simple layouts: up to 24 rings and 60 children of each kind per ring. The fallback also needs `:has()` and `:nth-child(… of …)`. `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>` always need the runtime.

- With a framework: [React](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/react.html), [Vue](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/vue.html), [Svelte](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/svelte.html), [Angular](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/angular.html), [Astro](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/astro.html).

# Build a knob

A volume knob: a ring of ticks, a band that shows the level, a body with a dot that turns, and the number under it. On the way you meet every piece of Orbit. Each step below is live: open its code and change it.

## 1. Make a universe

Everything starts with a [`.bigbang`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/bigbang.html). It is the space the knob lives in, and its box is the only size you set: the knob will be as big as this box. Here it is 260px wide and square by default. It is invisible; the dashed outline is only there so you can see it.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob"></div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
/* The only size you set. */
.knob {
  width: 260px;
  outline: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
```

## 2. Give it a center

A [`.gravity-spot`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html) is the center of the system. Its gravity reaches the shorter side of the universe, and that reach is split into 12 lanes: the rings you will place things on. It is invisible too. The circle drawn here is its reach, `--o-force`.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob">
  <div class="gravity-spot"></div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 260px;
  outline: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
/* Only to see it: the reach of the gravity spot. */
.gravity-spot::before {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  top: 0;
  translate: -50% -50%;
  width: var(--o-force);
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  border: 1px dashed var(--accent);
}
```

## 3. Draw the orbits

[Rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html) go straight inside the gravity spot. `orbit-N` sits N lanes from the center: `orbit-6` halfway, `orbit-12` at the edge. The knob needs three: `orbit-11` for the ticks, `orbit-10` for the band, and `orbit-0`, the center itself, for the body.

Rings are transparent. The dashed lines here come from a `border` in the example CSS.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-11"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10"></div>
    <div class="orbit-0"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 260px;
}
/* Only to see them. */
.orbit-11, .orbit-10 {
  border: 1px dashed var(--accent);
}
```

`orbit-11` outside, `orbit-10` just inside it. `orbit-0` is the center point, with no size of its own.

## 4. Put things on them

Rings hold [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html) carrying your content, [ticks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html), [chords](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html), [arcs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) and [progress bands](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html), and Orbit spreads them evenly around their ring. Here: 21 ticks on `orbit-11`, a progress band on `orbit-10` and the number in the middle. The ticks are the same element 21 times, so one line of JavaScript writes them.

Centered content goes in `.orbit-0 > .satellite.at-center > .capsule`. Every element on a ring is one lane thick, so the center satellite gets `--o-size-ratio: 6` to make room for the number.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-11 ticks"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10">
      <o-progress value="64"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 6">
      <div class="satellite at-center">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong>64</strong><span>volume</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 260px;
}
.orbit-11, .orbit-10 {
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
.ticks .vector {
  background: var(--muted);
}
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong {
  font-size: 26px;
}
```

```js
document.querySelector('.ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(21);
```

## 5. Shape it

Now the details. The ticks and the band use 270° of the circle starting at 225° (`range-270 from-225`), so the knob has a gap at the bottom, and `fit-range` puts the first and last tick on the two ends of the range. `--o-size-ratio` makes the ticks a little shorter and the band a little thinner than a lane, and `shape="rounded"` rounds the band's ends. The track behind the band is `--o-back-fill`.

The number moves into the gap: a satellite on `orbit-11` with `angle-180` sits straight down. The dashed guides are gone.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <!-- Ticks and band share range and start, so they line up. -->
    <div class="orbit-11 range-270 from-225 fit-range ticks" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10 range-270 from-225" style="--o-size-ratio: .9">
      <o-progress value="64" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-11">
      <div class="satellite angle-180">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong>64</strong><span>volume</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 260px;
}
.ticks .vector {
  background: #3a4757;
}
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: #1d2630;
}
.readout strong {
  font-size: 22px;
}
```

```js
document.querySelector('.ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(21);
```

## 6. A system inside a satellite

A satellite is a universe too: put a `.gravity-spot` inside it and its rings are measured against the satellite. The body of the knob is a satellite 15 lanes wide on `orbit-0`. Its capsule paints the body, and the system inside it carries the dot on its own `orbit-9`, with the same range as the dial.

With one satellite on a partial range, the dot sits at the start, 225°. Turning that inner ring with `rotate` moves it along: 64% of 270° is about 173°.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-11 range-270 from-225 fit-range ticks" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10 range-270 from-225" style="--o-size-ratio: .9">
      <o-progress value="64" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <!-- The body: a satellite 15 lanes wide, and a universe of its own. -->
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 15">
      <div class="satellite at-center">
        <div class="capsule body"></div>
        <div class="gravity-spot">
          <div class="orbit-9 range-270 from-225 turn" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.2">
            <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule dot"></div></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-11">
      <div class="satellite angle-180">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong>64</strong><span>volume</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 260px;
}
.ticks .vector {
  background: #3a4757;
}
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: #1d2630;
}
.body {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, #2b3542, #151b22 70%);
  box-shadow: 0 14px 30px -10px #000, inset 0 1px 0 #3b4655, inset 0 -6px 14px #0a0d11;
}
.dot {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
  box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent);
}
/* 64% of the 270° range. */
.turn {
  rotate: 173deg;
}
.readout strong {
  font-size: 22px;
}
```

```js
document.querySelector('.ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(21);
```

## 7. Make it turn

The drawing is done; the rest is a few lines of JavaScript. One function sets the value: it changes `value` on the `<o-progress>`, turns the inner ring through a `--turn` custom property, lights the ticks up to the value and keeps `aria-valuenow` in sync. The pointer, the wheel and the arrow keys all call it.

The `.bigbang` is the control: `role="slider"`, a name and `tabindex="0"`, so it works with a keyboard and a screen reader. Orbit draws; the behavior is yours.

```html
<div class="bigbang knob" tabindex="0" role="slider" aria-label="Volume" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="64">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-11 range-270 from-225 fit-range ticks" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"></div>
    <div class="orbit-10 range-270 from-225" style="--o-size-ratio: .9">
      <o-progress value="64" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 15">
      <div class="satellite at-center">
        <div class="capsule body"></div>
        <div class="gravity-spot">
          <div class="orbit-9 range-270 from-225 turn" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.2">
            <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule dot"></div></div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-11">
      <div class="satellite angle-180">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong id="level">64</strong><span>volume</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.knob {
  width: 300px;
  touch-action: none;
  cursor: grab;
}
.knob:active { cursor: grabbing; }
.knob:focus-visible { outline: none; }
.ticks .vector { background: #3a4757; }
.ticks .vector.lit { background: var(--accent); }
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: #1d2630;
}
.body {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, #2b3542, #151b22 70%);
  box-shadow: 0 14px 30px -10px #000, inset 0 1px 0 #3b4655, inset 0 -6px 14px #0a0d11;
}
.knob:focus-visible .body { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent), 0 14px 30px -10px #000; }
.dot {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
  box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent);
}
.turn {
  rotate: var(--turn, 0deg);
  transition: rotate .08s linear;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 24px; }
```

```js
const knob = document.querySelector('.knob');
const ticksRing = knob.querySelector('.ticks');
ticksRing.innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(21);
const ticks = [...ticksRing.children];
let value = 0;

const set = (v) => {
  value = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Math.round(v)));
  knob.querySelector('o-progress').setAttribute('value', value);
  knob.style.setProperty('--turn', value * 2.7 + 'deg');
  knob.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', value);
  document.getElementById('level').textContent = value;
  ticks.forEach((tick, i) => tick.classList.toggle('lit', value > 0 && i * 5 <= value));
};

// Pointer angle around the center, 0 at the start of the 270° range.
const fromPointer = (event) => {
  const box = knob.getBoundingClientRect();
  const x = event.clientX - (box.left + box.width / 2);
  const y = (box.top + box.height / 2) - event.clientY;
  const along = (Math.atan2(x, y) * 180 / Math.PI + 360 + 135) % 360;
  if (along <= 270) set(along / 2.7);
};

knob.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => { knob.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); fromPointer(e); });
knob.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => { if (knob.hasPointerCapture(e.pointerId)) fromPointer(e); });
knob.addEventListener('wheel', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); set(value - Math.sign(e.deltaY) * 2); }, { passive: false });
knob.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  const step = { ArrowUp: 1, ArrowRight: 1, ArrowDown: -1, ArrowLeft: -1, PageUp: 10, PageDown: -10 }[e.key];
  if (step) { e.preventDefault(); set(value + step); }
  if (e.key === 'Home') set(0);
  if (e.key === 'End') set(100);
});

set(64);
```

Drag around the knob, scroll over it, or focus it and use the arrow keys.

Change `width` on `.knob` and all of it scales together, ticks, band, body and dot. Every element has more options like these: the pages under Elements list them. The same knob is also a [full-page demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/05-knob.html), and [`<o-knob>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html) in Orbit Kit is a ready-made one.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/migrating.html

# Coming from 1.x

Orbit 2 changes one big thing: where size comes from. Everything else is smaller and mostly in your favor. You can move a layout over in a few minutes, or keep it exactly as it was with one line of CSS.

The [1.x documentation](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit-docs/) stays online.

## Size comes from the universe

In 1.x every system was 500px across, whatever the size of its `.bigbang`. `orbit-12` was always 500px wide, and to make a layout follow its container you called `Orbit.resize()`.

In 2.0 the `.bigbang` is the universe and its box sets the size. The `.gravity-spot` reaches the shorter side of it (`--o-force` defaults to `100cqmin`), so `orbit-12` touches the edge and every ring is a fraction of the box. Layouts follow their container with no code.

Both previews below are the same ring in a 300px-tall frame. The first keeps the 1.x size with a fixed reach; the second is written for 2.0.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-force: 500px">
    <div class="orbit-12 reach"></div>
    <div class="orbit-4" style="--o-size-ratio: 1">
      <o-progress value="70"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 6">
      <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>70%</strong><span>1.x size</span></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The reach of the system, drawn so you can compare. */
.reach {
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 26px; }
```

`--o-force: 500px`: the dashed `orbit-12` is 500px across, larger than the frame, as in 1.x.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-12 reach"></div>
    <div class="orbit-7" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.7">
      <o-progress value="70"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 10">
      <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>70%</strong><span>2.0 size</span></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The reach of the system, drawn so you can compare. */
.reach {
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
}
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 26px; }
```

No `--o-force`: the dashed `orbit-12` touches the edge of the frame, and `orbit-7` lands where 1.x put `orbit-4`.

## Two ways to move

**Keep the 1.x size.** Set the old reach back on your systems:

```css
.gravity-spot { --o-force: 500px; }
```

Your layouts look exactly as before. `Orbit.resize()` still scales systems with a fixed px reach, so code that used it keeps working.

**Adopt the new model.** Remove `--o-force` and `Orbit.resize()`, then pick rings by their share of the space. If your 1.x layout sat in a box `W` px wide:

- a ring `orbit-N` lands near `orbit-(N × 500 / W)`,
- a thickness ratio `r` lands near `--o-size-ratio: r × 500 / W`.

Round to the nearest lane; if that is visibly off, try the neighbor or nudge with `--o-alignment` in px. When every ring of a system scales the same way, set `--o-size-ratio` once on the `.gravity-spot`. Give auto-numbered `.orbit` rings an explicit number while you are at it, so the result does not depend on DOM order.

Text inside arcs keeps its font size, so on a smaller layout a label may no longer fit its arc. The console will tell you (`[orbit] <o-arc> text "…" overflows its arc`); widen the range, use `range="auto"`, or move the ring out a lane.

## Everything else

- **The universe.** A `.bigbang` is square by default and a size container, so it is the containing block of `position: fixed` descendants. Directly in `<body>` it is capped at the viewport height instead of forced to it, so your own `width` and `aspect-ratio` apply.
- **Thickness.** `.satellite` no longer resets `--o-size-ratio`, so a value set on its ring reaches it. `shrink-N` on a ring only changes how close it sits to the previous lane; it does not shrink what is on it.
- **Nested systems.** Every `.gravity-spot` starts from the defaults, including ring spacing, so a `shrink-N` around a satellite does not leak into the system inside it.
- **Gaps and alignment.** `--o-gap` cascades from the ring and the system. `--o-aligment` still works; `--o-alignment` is the right spelling.
- **Ranges.** `fit-range` on a ring of arcs no longer makes the arcs overflow the range.
- **Styling.** Satellites have no border by default. The reset, the default theme and `theme-cyan` count only their own class for specificity, so a single class of yours wins without `!important`, also inside a `.capsule`. `dev-orbit` combines with a theme.
- **Arcs and progress.** They are placed with `rotate` instead of `transform`, so a `transform` of yours adds to it. Endings (`rounded`, `arrow`…) scale with the band. `interactive` makes the whole band clickable, transparent or not, and `hit-width` adds touch area. `variant="stroke"` draws a 2px line over a gray track by default.
- **New.** `range="auto"` and `text-anchor` for arcs that fit their text, `--o-dir-x` / `--o-dir-y` on satellites, depth layers, `Orbit.ready()`, the `o-rendered` event, `value` and `max` as properties on arcs and progress (so `[value]` bindings redraw), and `[orbit]` messages in the console.
- **No `!important`.** Utility classes (`grow-*x`, `shrink-N`, `angle-N`, `ccw`, `fit-range`, `at-*`, `flip`…) no longer use it. An inline style or a more specific rule of yours wins over them. In 1.x some of them could only be beaten with another `!important`; those still work, but you can drop them.
- **Renamed.** `from-1x` … `from-12x` are now `core-1` … `core-12`, so they don't read like `from-N`. The old names still work.
- **Fixed.** `angle-N` on a `.side` points where it does on a satellite. Only real `angle-N` classes reset `--o-from`, not any class that contains "angle-". `--o-color` set on a ring or satellite gives it its own `--o-color-*` shades.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/bigbang.html

# Bigbang

Every Orbit layout starts with a big bang. The `.bigbang` creates the universe your system lives in, and its box is the only size you set: every ring, satellite and band inside is a fraction of it.

```html
<!-- The universe is the whole frame: wide and short, so the system takes its height. -->
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-12 edge">
      <div class="satellite angle-62"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-12</span></div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-6 half">
      <div class="satellite angle-135"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-6</span></div></div>
    </div>
    <!-- Two planets, each on a ring that turns. -->
    <div class="orbit-9 turn" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.2"><div class="satellite planet"></div></div>
    <div class="orbit-6 turn fast" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"><div class="satellite planet"></div></div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 3"><div class="satellite at-center sun"></div></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The universe box, tinted so you can see it. */
.bigbang {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 7%, transparent);
  outline: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent);
  outline-offset: -1px;
}
.edge { border-color: var(--accent); }
.half { border-color: var(--faint); }
.orbit-9 { border-color: var(--line); }
.label {
  white-space: nowrap;
  padding: 1px 6px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: var(--panel);
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  color: var(--muted);
}
.sun { background: var(--amber); box-shadow: 0 0 18px var(--amber); }
.planet { background: var(--text); }

.turn { animation: turn 40s linear infinite; }
.turn.fast { animation-duration: 16s; }
@keyframes turn { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
```

The tinted box is the universe. `orbit-12` touches its top and bottom, and `orbit-6` is halfway.

## How big it is

A `.bigbang` is as wide as its parent and square by default. A parent with a definite height caps it, so in a wide, short container it becomes a wide, short box, and the system inside takes the shorter side.

- To size it, give the `.bigbang` or its parent a width. Your own `width`, `height` or `aspect-ratio` always win, because the defaults have zero specificity.
- Directly inside `<body>` it is capped at the viewport height. The previews on this site are pages like that, which is why the universe above is as tall as the frame.
- It is a size container: the `.gravity-spot` inside measures it with container query units. It is also the containing block of `position: fixed` descendants.
- A `.bigbang` with no width or height draws nothing, and the console says so with an `[orbit]` message.

Drag the corner of the dotted box. The system follows with no JavaScript: make the box wide and short and it takes the height, tall and narrow and it takes the width.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <!-- Drag the corner: the universe fills the box, the system takes its shorter side. -->
  <div class="box">
    <div class="bigbang">
      <div class="gravity-spot">
        <div class="orbit-12"></div>
        <div class="orbit-9" id="dots" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <output class="size" id="size"></output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.box {
  position: relative;
  width: 320px;
  height: 180px;
  min-width: 60px;
  min-height: 60px;
  max-width: calc(100vw - 32px);
  max-height: calc(100vh - 32px);
  resize: both;
  overflow: hidden;
  border: 2px dotted var(--faint);
  border-radius: 4px;
}
.bigbang { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 7%, transparent); }
.orbit-12 { border-color: var(--accent); }
.orbit-9 { border-color: var(--line); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.size {
  position: absolute;
  left: 8px;
  bottom: 6px;
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
```

```js
document.getElementById('dots').innerHTML = '<div class="satellite"></div>'.repeat(8);
// Only to show the size of the box: the layout itself needs no script.
const box = document.querySelector('.box');
new ResizeObserver(() => {
  document.getElementById('size').value = `${box.clientWidth} × ${box.clientHeight}`;
}).observe(box);
```

## Moving the center

The universe centers its system. An alignment class on the `.bigbang` puts the center on an edge or a corner of the box instead, so only part of the system shows. It is the quick way to a quarter dial in a corner or a half gauge along an edge.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="grid" id="grid"></div>
</main>
```

```css
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 84px);
  justify-items: center;
  gap: 12px 44px;
}
.cell { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 6px; }
.cell span { font: 12px var(--mono); color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
.bigbang {
  width: 84px;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 7%, transparent);
  border-radius: 4px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.orbit-6, .orbit-12 { border-color: var(--accent); }
/* The center of the system. */
.center { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const places = ['at-top-left', 'at-top', 'at-top-right', 'at-center-left', 'at-center',
  'at-center-right', 'at-bottom-left', 'at-bottom', 'at-bottom-right'];
// The same system nine times; only the class on the .bigbang changes.
document.getElementById('grid').innerHTML = places.map(place => `
  <div class="cell">
    <div class="bigbang ${place}">
      <div class="gravity-spot">
        <div class="orbit-6"></div>
        <div class="orbit-12"></div>
        <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><div class="satellite at-center center"></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <span>${place}</span>
  </div>`).join('');
```

The amber dot is the center of the system. `.at-center` is the default.

## A universe inside a system

A `.bigbang` placed directly in a `.gravity-spot` takes the reach of that system instead of measuring its own box. That is how a whole system becomes one layer of a [depth stack](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html).

## Reference

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `.bigbang` | | Creates the universe. Holds one or more `.gravity-spot`. |
| `width` / `height` / `aspect-ratio` | `100%` / `auto` / `1` | The size of the universe. Capped by a parent with a definite height, and by the viewport directly in `<body>`. |
| `.at-top-left` … `.at-bottom-right` | `.at-center` | Puts the center of the system on an edge or a corner of the box. |
| `.dev-orbit` | | Draws the lanes and explains misplaced elements in the console. See [Visual aids](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/visual-aids.html). |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html

# Gravity spot

The `.gravity-spot` is the center of mass of a system. Every ring is its direct child, and its gravity reaches as far as the shorter side of the universe.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <!-- The default reach: the shorter side of the universe. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-12"></div>
      <div class="orbit-9" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.4"><div class="satellite angle-120"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-6"></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"><div class="satellite at-center"></div></div>
    </div>
    <!-- A second system in the same universe, with a fixed reach. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot fixed" id="fixed" style="--o-force: 120px">
      <div class="orbit-12"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"><div class="satellite angle-300"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-4"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-force <input id="force" type="range" min="40" max="360" value="120"></label>
    <output id="out">120px</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
/* A wide universe, tinted so you can see its box. */
.stage > .bigbang {
  width: 100%;
  height: calc(100vh - 84px);
  aspect-ratio: auto;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, transparent);
  border-radius: 6px;
}
.gravity-spot > [class*="orbit-"] { border-color: var(--accent); }
.gravity-spot > .orbit-9, .gravity-spot > .orbit-6 { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 40%, transparent); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.fixed > [class*="orbit-"] { border: 1px dashed var(--amber); }
.fixed .satellite { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const force = document.getElementById('force');
force.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('fixed').style.setProperty('--o-force', force.value + 'px');
  document.getElementById('out').value = force.value + 'px';
});
```

Two systems in one universe. The teal one uses the default reach and touches the top and bottom of the box; the amber one has `--o-force` in px and ignores the box.

## Reach

The reach is `--o-force`, the diameter of `orbit-12`. Between the center and that edge there are 12 lanes. The default, `100cqmin`, is the shorter side of the nearest `.bigbang` or satellite, so the system follows its box as it resizes. Set it when you want something else:

- a length, for a fixed size that ignores the box: `--o-force: 120px`;
- `100cqw`, to reach the width of a wide universe instead of its height;
- a fraction of the default, like `calc(100cqmin * .8)`, to leave a margin around the system.

Systems with a fixed px reach can still scale with their container through `Orbit.resize()`. See [Runtime and resizing](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

## Every system starts fresh

A `.gravity-spot` resets the reach, the angles, the thickness and the spacing to their defaults. A system nested in a satellite does not inherit any of them from the one around it.

A satellite is a universe too: a `.gravity-spot` inside one reaches the satellite's edge, so its `orbit-12` is the satellite's outline. Here the outer system makes its planets five lanes thick, and each planet holds a system of its own whose moons start again from one lane and set their own size.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <!-- Planets five lanes thick... -->
    <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-size-ratio: 5">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 4">
        <div class="satellite at-center sun"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="satellite planet">
          <!-- ...each a universe with its own system: moons start again from one lane. -->
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-8 moons" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite planet">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-8 moons" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite planet">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-8 moons" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
              <div class="satellite moon"></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.gravity-spot > .orbit-8 { border-color: var(--line); }
.sun { background: var(--amber); box-shadow: 0 0 24px color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 60%, transparent); }
/* The planet's outline is the orbit-12 of the system inside it. */
.planet {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 10%, var(--bg));
  border: 1px solid var(--accent);
}
.moons {
  border: 1px dashed color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 45%, transparent);
  animation: turn 12s linear infinite;
}
.moon { background: var(--accent); }
@keyframes turn { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
```

Each planet holds a system of its own. Its moons are three lanes of the planet, not of the sun.

## An empty core

`.core-1` to `.core-12` on a `.gravity-spot` leave an empty core in the middle, N lanes wide. With `core-4` the radius is split into 16 lanes instead of 12 and `orbit-N` lands on lane N + 4: rings sit closer together, further from the center, and `orbit-12` still touches the edge. Compare the cyan rings (default) with the purple ones (`core-4`), both `orbit-4`, `orbit-8` and `orbit-12`.

In 1.x these classes were `from-1x` to `from-12x`. They still work.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-4"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8"></div>
      <div class="orbit-12"></div>
    </div>
    <!-- The same three rings, with an empty core. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot core-4" id="cored">
      <div class="orbit-4"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8"></div>
      <div class="orbit-12"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>core <input id="core" type="range" min="0" max="8" value="4"></label>
    <output id="out">core-4</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.gravity-spot > * { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent); }
#cored > * { border: 1px dashed var(--amber); }
```

```js
const core = document.getElementById('core'), cored = document.getElementById('cored');
core.addEventListener('input', () => {
  cored.className = 'gravity-spot' + (core.value > 0 ? ' core-' + core.value : '');
  document.getElementById('out').value = core.value > 0 ? 'core-' + core.value : 'no core';
});
```

Teal: `orbit-4`, `orbit-8` and `orbit-12` with no core. Amber: the same rings in a system with an empty core.

## Rings off the center

A `.gravity-spot` centers its rings on itself. An alignment class on it (`.at-top-left`, `.at-top`, `.at-bottom-right` and the rest) moves every ring toward that edge or corner, so the rings touch the center instead of surrounding it. Four systems in the same spot, one per corner:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <!-- Four systems on the same spot, each pushed toward a corner. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot at-top-left"><div class="orbit-3"></div><div class="orbit-6"></div></div>
    <div class="gravity-spot at-top-right"><div class="orbit-3"></div><div class="orbit-6"></div></div>
    <div class="gravity-spot at-bottom-left"><div class="orbit-3"></div><div class="orbit-6"></div></div>
    <div class="gravity-spot at-bottom-right"><div class="orbit-3"></div><div class="orbit-6"></div></div>
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"><div class="satellite at-center center"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.gravity-spot[class*="at-"] > * {
  border-color: var(--accent);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, transparent);
}
.center { background: var(--amber); }
```

Every ring touches the center, the amber dot, instead of surrounding it.

## Reference

Set these on the `.gravity-spot` to change the whole system, or on a ring or element for just that part.

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `--o-force` | `100cqmin` | Reach: the diameter of `orbit-12`. |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Thickness of the elements on the rings, in lanes. |
| `--o-range` | `360deg` | How much of the circle the rings use. See [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#angles). |
| `--o-from` | `0deg` | Where the range starts, clockwise from the top. |
| `--o-gap` | `1` | Space between sibling arcs. |
| `--o-ellipse-x` / `--o-ellipse-y` | `1` | Stretch the rings into ellipses. See [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#ellipses). |
| `.core-1` … `.core-12` | | An empty core N lanes wide; every ring moves N lanes out. Old name: `from-Nx`. |
| `.at-top-left` … `.at-bottom-right` | `.at-center` | Move the rings toward an edge or a corner, touching the center. |
| `.depth` | | Stacks the rings as 3D layers. See [Depth layers](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html). |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html

# Orbits

Gravity draws orbits. A ring, `.orbit-N`, is a lane around the gravity spot, N twelfths of the way out to the edge, and it is where satellites, vectors, sides, arcs and progress travel.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot" id="lanes"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Lane <input id="lane" type="range" min="0" max="12" value="6"></label>
    <output id="out"></output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
#lanes > * { border-color: var(--line); }
#lanes > .orbit-12 { border-color: var(--accent); }
/* The chosen lane, filled so you can see its diameter. */
#lanes > .on {
  border: 2px solid var(--amber);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 10%, transparent);
}
.dot { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const lanes = document.getElementById('lanes'), lane = document.getElementById('lane');
// orbit-1 … orbit-12, and a dot on orbit-0, the center.
lanes.innerHTML = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => `<div class="orbit-${i + 1}"></div>`).join('') +
  '<div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"><div class="satellite at-center dot"></div></div>';
const show = () => {
  const n = Number(lane.value);
  lanes.querySelectorAll(':scope > *').forEach(ring => ring.classList.toggle('on', ring.matches('.orbit-' + n) && n > 0));
  document.getElementById('out').value = n ? `orbit-${n}: ${n}/12 of the reach` : 'orbit-0: the center';
};
lane.addEventListener('input', show);
show();
```

The 12 lanes. `orbit-6` is halfway and `orbit-12`, in teal, touches the edge of the universe.

## Which lane

- The diameter of `orbit-N` is N/12 of the reach (`--o-force`): `orbit-3` is a quarter, `orbit-6` half, `orbit-12` all of it.
- `orbit-0` is the center itself. It holds centered content; see The center.
- `orbit-13` to `orbit-24` lie past the edge, for things that should stick out. With the runtime, higher numbers work too.
- `.orbit` without a number takes the next lane in order: the first `.orbit` of a system is lane 1, the second lane 2. Numbered rings are not counted.

Rings are direct children of a `.gravity-spot`, never of another ring. A ring holds only `.satellite`, `.vector`, `.side`, `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`. With `dev-orbit` on the `.bigbang`, the console points out anything else.

## Look

Rings are invisible. Give them a border or a background to draw them.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-11 glow"></div>
      <div class="orbit-7 dotted"></div>
      <div class="orbit-3 filled"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
/* A ring is a round box: borders, backgrounds and shadows draw it. */
.glow {
  border: 2px solid var(--accent);
  box-shadow: 0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, transparent),
              inset 0 0 18px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 30%, transparent);
}
.dotted {
  border: 3px dotted var(--amber);
}
.filled {
  border: 1px dashed var(--accent);
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
}
```

## Thickness

Everything on a ring is one lane thick: a twelfth of the radius. Set `--o-size-ratio`, in lanes, on the ring to change all its elements, on the `.gravity-spot` for the whole system, or on one element. An element on `orbit-N` reaches half its thickness past lane N, so a band two lanes thick on `orbit-11` ends exactly at the edge.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-4" id="a"></div>
      <div class="orbit-7" id="b" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
      <div class="orbit-10" id="c" style="--o-size-ratio: .5"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-size-ratio on orbit-7 <input id="size" type="range" min=".5" max="3" step=".1" value="2"></label>
    <output id="out">2</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
[class*="orbit-"] { border-color: var(--line); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
#b .satellite { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const fill = (id, count) => document.getElementById(id).innerHTML = '<div class="satellite"></div>'.repeat(count);
fill('a', 3); fill('b', 4); fill('c', 6);
const size = document.getElementById('size');
size.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('b').style.setProperty('--o-size-ratio', size.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = size.value;
});
```

`orbit-4` at the default, `orbit-10` at half a lane, and `orbit-7` at the thickness you pick.

## Spacing

`.shrink-5` to `.shrink-100`, in steps of 5, move a ring toward the previous lane: `orbit-10 shrink-40` sits 40% of a lane inside lane 10. On a ring, `shrink-N` only changes where it sits; the elements on it keep their size.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <!-- Zoomed in: the center sits on the bottom edge, and the reach is twice the box. -->
  <div class="bigbang at-bottom">
    <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-force: 200cqmin">
      <div class="orbit-10 lane"><div class="satellite angle-322"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-10</span></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-9 lane"><div class="satellite angle-38"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-9</span></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-10 shrink-40 range-100 from-310 fit-range" id="ring" style="--o-size-ratio: .6">
        <div class="satellite"></div><div class="satellite"></div><div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div><div class="satellite"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>shrink <input id="shrink" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="5" value="40"></label>
    <output id="out">shrink-40</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: 100%; height: calc(100vh - 84px); aspect-ratio: auto; overflow: hidden; }
.lane { border-color: var(--faint); }
#ring { border: 2px solid var(--amber); }
#ring .satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.label {
  white-space: nowrap;
  padding: 1px 6px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: var(--panel);
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  color: var(--muted);
}
```

```js
const shrink = document.getElementById('shrink'), ring = document.getElementById('ring');
shrink.addEventListener('input', () => {
  const n = Number(shrink.value);
  ring.className = 'orbit-10 range-100 from-310 fit-range' + (n ? ' shrink-' + n : '');
  document.getElementById('out').value = n ? 'shrink-' + n : 'no shrink';
});
```

The amber ring is `orbit-10` with `shrink-N`: at 100 it reaches `orbit-9`. Its satellites keep their size.

## Angles

A ring spreads its elements evenly. Five satellites on a full ring sit 72° apart, starting at the top and going clockwise. Each kind is spread on its own, so five satellites and twelve vectors can share a ring.

- `--o-range` is how much of the circle the ring uses (`360deg` by default). `.range-0` to `.range-360` set it in whole degrees.
- `--o-from` is where the range starts, clockwise from the top. `.from-0` to `.from-360` set it.
- `.fit-range` puts the first and last element on the two ends of a partial range, instead of leaving one step free at the end.
- `.ccw` goes counterclockwise.

All of them cascade, so you can set them on the `.gravity-spot` for every ring at once. To place one element at an exact angle, use `.angle-N` on it; see [Satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html#angle).

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- A band over the part of the circle the ring uses. -->
      <div class="orbit-9 band" id="band" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"><o-arc></o-arc></div>
      <div class="orbit-9" id="ring" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>range <input id="range" type="range" min="45" max="360" step="15" value="180"></label>
    <label>from <input id="from" type="range" min="0" max="345" step="15" value="270"></label>
    <label><input id="fit" type="checkbox"> fit-range</label>
    <label><input id="ccw" type="checkbox"> ccw</label>
  </div>
  <code id="classes"></code>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 10px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 120px); }
#ring { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
.band o-arc { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.capsule { color: var(--bg); font-weight: 650; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
#classes { color: var(--muted); }
input[type=checkbox] { accent-color: var(--accent); }
```

```js
const ring = document.getElementById('ring'), band = document.getElementById('band');
ring.innerHTML = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(n => `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">${n}</div></div>`).join('');
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const set = () => {
  const range = Number($('range').value), from = Number($('from').value), ccw = $('ccw').checked;
  // The ring: what you would write in your markup.
  ring.className = `orbit-9 range-${range} from-${from}` + ($('fit').checked ? ' fit-range' : '') + (ccw ? ' ccw' : '');
  // The band always runs clockwise, so a ccw range starts `range` degrees earlier.
  band.style.setProperty('--o-range', range + 'deg');
  band.style.setProperty('--o-from', (ccw ? from - range : from) + 'deg');
  $('classes').textContent = ring.className;
};
document.querySelectorAll('input').forEach(input => input.addEventListener('input', set));
set();
```

Five satellites and the range they share. Try `range-180` with and without `fit-range`.

## The center

`orbit-0` is the center of the system. Put a `.satellite.at-center` in it for centered content, and size it with `--o-size-ratio` on `orbit-0`: the value is its diameter in lanes, so `12` reaches `orbit-6` and `24` fills the universe.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-12 guide"><div class="satellite angle-45"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-12</span></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-6 guide"><div class="satellite angle-45"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">orbit-6</span></div></div></div>
      <!-- The center: its --o-size-ratio is a diameter, in lanes. -->
      <div class="orbit-0" id="center" style="--o-size-ratio: 16">
        <div class="satellite at-center disc"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-size-ratio on orbit-0 <input id="size" type="range" min="1" max="24" value="16"></label>
    <output id="out">16</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.guide { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); z-index: 1; }
.disc {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, transparent);
  border: 2px solid var(--accent);
}
.label {
  white-space: nowrap;
  padding: 1px 6px;
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: var(--panel);
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  color: var(--muted);
}
```

```js
const size = document.getElementById('size');
size.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('center').style.setProperty('--o-size-ratio', size.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = size.value;
});
```

At 12 the disc reaches `orbit-6`; at 24 it fills the universe.

## Ellipses

`--o-ellipse-x` and `--o-ellipse-y` stretch a ring into an ellipse. Values below 1 stretch it along that axis: `--o-ellipse-x: .5` makes it twice as wide. Satellites and vectors follow the ellipse; arcs, progress and sides are drawn for circles, so leave them on round rings.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-6 round"></div>
      <div class="orbit-6 stretched" id="ring" style="--o-ellipse-x: .5; --o-ellipse-y: 1"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-ellipse-x <input id="x" type="range" min=".4" max="1" step=".05" value=".5"></label>
    <output id="x-out">0.5</output>
    <label>--o-ellipse-y <input id="y" type="range" min=".5" max="1" step=".05" value="1"></label>
    <output id="y-out">1</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.round { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); }
.stretched { border: 1px solid var(--accent); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
```

```js
const ring = document.getElementById('ring');
ring.innerHTML = '<div class="satellite"></div>'.repeat(8);
for (const axis of ['x', 'y']) {
  const input = document.getElementById(axis);
  input.addEventListener('input', () => {
    ring.style.setProperty('--o-ellipse-' + axis, input.value);
    document.getElementById(axis + '-out').value = Number(input.value);
  });
}
```

Eight satellites on a stretched `orbit-6`, over the round one.

## Gooey effect

`.gooey-fx` (or `.gooey-fx-light`), `.gooey-fx-medium` and `.gooey-fx-max` blend touching elements of a ring into one blob with an SVG filter. Safari does not support it.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 track"></div>
      <!-- Four satellites over 90°: when they touch, the filter melts them together. -->
      <div class="orbit-8 range-90 gooey-fx blob" id="ring" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.5">
        <div class="satellite"></div><div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div><div class="satellite"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-size-ratio <input id="size" type="range" min="1.5" max="5" step=".1" value="3.5"></label>
    <output id="out">3.5</output>
    <label><input id="gooey" type="checkbox" checked> gooey-fx</label>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.track { border-color: var(--line); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.blob { animation: turn 8s linear infinite; }
input[type=checkbox] { accent-color: var(--accent); }
@keyframes turn { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
```

```js
const ring = document.getElementById('ring'), size = document.getElementById('size');
size.addEventListener('input', () => {
  ring.style.setProperty('--o-size-ratio', size.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = size.value;
});
document.getElementById('gooey').addEventListener('change', (event) => ring.classList.toggle('gooey-fx', event.target.checked));
```

## Stacking

Rings stack in document order: a later ring paints over an earlier one. To stack them in 3D, with perspective and animated depth changes, see [Depth layers](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html).

## Reference

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `.orbit-0` … `.orbit-24` | | A ring on lane N. 0 is the center, 13 and up stick out. |
| `.orbit` | | A ring on the next lane, counted in document order. |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Thickness of the ring's elements, in lanes. |
| `--o-range`, `.range-N` | `360deg` | How much of the circle the ring uses. |
| `--o-from`, `.from-N` | `0deg` | Where the range starts, clockwise from the top. |
| `.fit-range` | | First and last element on the two ends of the range. |
| `.ccw` | | Counterclockwise. |
| `.shrink-5` … `.shrink-100` | | Moves the ring toward the previous lane, by that percentage of a lane. |
| `--o-ellipse-x` / `--o-ellipse-y` | `1` | Stretch the ring into an ellipse. |
| `.gooey-fx`, `-medium`, `-max` | | Blends touching elements together. |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html

# Satellites

Satellites travel the orbits. A `.satellite` sits on a ring and carries your content in a `.capsule`; Orbit spreads all the satellites of a ring evenly around it.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8" id="ring" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Satellites <input id="count" type="range" min="1" max="12" value="5"></label>
    <output id="out">5</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.orbit-8 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.capsule { color: var(--bg); font-weight: 650; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const ring = document.getElementById('ring'), count = document.getElementById('count');
// Orbit spreads whatever is on the ring: change the count, the spacing follows.
const fill = () => {
  ring.innerHTML = Array.from({ length: count.value }, (_, i) =>
    `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">${i + 1}</div></div>`).join('');
  document.getElementById('out').value = count.value;
};
count.addEventListener('input', fill);
fill();
```

A satellite is a circle one lane across, with no border or background until you give it one. Put content in a `.capsule` inside it, never directly in the satellite: the capsule keeps it centered and upright. See [Capsules](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/capsule.html).

## Size

Set `--o-size-ratio`, in lanes, on the satellite, its ring or the `.gravity-spot`. For one satellite there are also classes, which win over any ratio set around them:

- `.shrink-5` to `.shrink-100` make it smaller than a lane: `shrink-30` is 0.7 lanes.
- `.grow-1x` to `.grow-12x` make it 2 to 24 lanes. Decimals add fifths of a lane: `grow-1.2x` is 2.4 lanes.
- `.grow-0.1x` to `.grow-0.9x` add tenths of a lane: `grow-0.5x` is 1.5 lanes.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="satellite shrink-50"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite grow-0.5x"></div>
        <div class="satellite grow-1x"></div>
        <div class="satellite grow-1.5x"></div>
        <div class="satellite grow-2x"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-8 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
```

Clockwise from the top: half a lane, one lane, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 lanes.

## Shape and look

Satellites are round. `.box` makes one square and `.rounded-box` a square with soft corners. Anything else is plain CSS: backgrounds, borders, images, SVG.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.6">
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite box"></div>
        <div class="satellite rounded-box"></div>
        <div class="satellite sphere"></div>
        <div class="satellite outline"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-8 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
/* Anything else is plain CSS. */
.sphere {
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #fff, var(--accent) 35%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 35%, black));
  box-shadow: 0 0 16px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 45%, transparent);
}
.outline {
  background: var(--bg);
  border: 2px dashed var(--accent);
}
```

Clockwise from the top: round, `.box`, `.rounded-box`, a gradient and a border.

## Position on the lane

A satellite is centered on its lane. `.inner-orbit` moves it in so its outer edge touches the lane, and `.outer-orbit` moves it out so its inner edge does. `.quarter-inner-orbit` and `.quarter-outer-orbit` move it part of the way. For any other offset, set `--o-alignment`: a positive length moves it in, a negative one out.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
        <div class="satellite outer-orbit"></div>
        <div class="satellite quarter-outer-orbit"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite quarter-inner-orbit"></div>
        <div class="satellite inner-orbit"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
/* The lane on top, so you can see where each satellite sits. */
.orbit-8 { border: 2px solid var(--amber); z-index: 1; }
.satellite {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 30%, transparent);
  border: 1px solid var(--accent);
}
```

Clockwise from the top: `outer-orbit`, `quarter-outer-orbit`, default, `quarter-inner-orbit`, `inner-orbit`.

## An exact angle

`.angle-0` to `.angle-360` place a satellite at that angle, clockwise from the top, instead of its turn on the ring. It ignores the ring's `--o-from`.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 lane" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
        <div class="satellite angle-45" id="moon"><div class="capsule" id="label">45°</div></div>
      </div>
      <!-- A vector 8 lanes long on orbit-4 starts at the center: a hand pointing at it. -->
      <div class="orbit-4" style="--o-size-ratio: 8">
        <div class="vector angle-45" id="hand"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Angle <input id="angle" type="range" min="0" max="360" step="5" value="45"></label>
    <output id="out">angle-45</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.lane { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
.capsule { color: var(--bg); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 650; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.vector { height: 2px; background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const angle = document.getElementById('angle');
angle.addEventListener('input', () => {
  const n = angle.value;
  document.getElementById('moon').className = `satellite angle-${n}`;
  document.getElementById('hand').className = `vector angle-${n}`;
  document.getElementById('label').textContent = n + '°';
  document.getElementById('out').value = 'angle-' + n;
});
```

## Facing the center

A satellite keeps its content upright wherever it is. With `.spin-lock` it turns with its angle instead, so the top of its content always points at the center, like the labels on a wheel. Add `.flip` to the capsule to make it point outward. Left, the default; right, `spin-lock`.

```html
<main class="stage pair">
  <div class="cell">
    <div class="bigbang">
      <div class="gravity-spot">
        <div class="orbit-8" id="upright" style="--o-size-ratio: 3"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <code>default</code>
  </div>
  <div class="cell">
    <div class="bigbang">
      <div class="gravity-spot">
        <div class="orbit-8" id="locked" style="--o-size-ratio: 3"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <code>spin-lock</code>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.pair { grid-auto-flow: column; justify-content: center; gap: 48px; }
```
