```css
.cell { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 8px; }
.cell .bigbang { width: min(210px, 38vw, 100vh - 70px); }
.cell code { color: var(--muted); }
.orbit-8 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 20%, var(--bg)); border: 1px solid var(--accent); }
.capsule { color: var(--accent); font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; }
```

```js
const arrows = cls => '<div class="satellite ' + cls + '"><div class="capsule">↑</div></div>';
document.getElementById('upright').innerHTML = arrows('').repeat(6);
document.getElementById('locked').innerHTML = arrows('spin-lock').repeat(6);
```

Left, every arrow points up. Right, with `spin-lock`, every arrow points at the center.

## Which way is out

Each satellite exposes `--o-dir-x` and `--o-dir-y`: the direction from the center of its system to the satellite, from -1 to 1. `x` grows to the right and `y` grows down, so a satellite at the top has `0` and `-1`, and a `.satellite.at-center` has both at `0`. Its content inherits them, so CSS can push a label outward whatever the angle:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-7" id="ring"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Push <input id="push" type="range" min="0" max="40" value="22"></label>
    <output id="out">22px</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.bigbang { --push: 22px; }
.orbit-7 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite { background: var(--accent); }
/* --o-dir-x/-y point away from the center: move each label along them. */
.label {
  translate: calc(var(--o-dir-x) * var(--push)) calc(var(--o-dir-y) * var(--push));
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--text);
}
```

```js
const points = ['N', 'NE', 'E', 'SE', 'S', 'SW', 'W', 'NW'];
document.getElementById('ring').innerHTML = points.map(p =>
  `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><span class="label">${p}</span></div></div>`).join('');
const push = document.getElementById('push');
push.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.querySelector('.bigbang').style.setProperty('--push', push.value + 'px');
  document.getElementById('out').value = push.value + 'px';
});
```

Each label moves away from the center along its own direction.

[How Orbit thinks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/universe.html) shows the other common use: labels that hang above the satellites of the upper half and below the rest.

## A satellite is a universe

Put a `.gravity-spot` directly inside a satellite and it reaches the satellite's edge: a moon system around a planet, a gauge inside a menu item. Make the satellite thicker to give it room. See [Gravity spot](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html).

## Reference

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Diameter, in lanes. |
| `.shrink-5` … `.shrink-100` | | Smaller than a lane: `shrink-N` is 1 − N/100 lanes. |
| `.grow-1x` … `.grow-12x`, `.grow-0.1x` … | | Bigger: `grow-Nx` is 2N lanes. |
| `.box`, `.rounded-box`, `.circle` | round | Shape. |
| `.inner-orbit`, `.outer-orbit`, `.quarter-inner-orbit`, `.quarter-outer-orbit` | | Moves it in or out from its lane. |
| `--o-alignment` | `0px` | Any offset from the lane; positive is inward. |
| `.angle-0` … `.angle-360` | | An exact angle, clockwise from the top. |
| `.spin-lock` | | Turns with its angle instead of staying upright. |
| `.at-center` | | In `orbit-0`: the satellite sits at the center. |
| `.at-top-left` … `.at-bottom-right` | | Where the capsule sits inside the satellite. |
| `--o-dir-x` / `--o-dir-y` | read only | Direction from the center, from -1 to 1. |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/capsule.html

# Capsules

A `.capsule` is the cargo a satellite carries: your content. It stays centered and upright however far around the ring the satellite travels.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-size-ratio: 4">
        <div class="satellite">
          <div class="capsule">Text</div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite">
          <div class="capsule">
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="22" height="22" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 3l2.6 5.6 6.1.7-4.5 4.2 1.2 6L12 16.6 6.6 19.5l1.2-6L3.3 9.3l6.1-.7z" fill="currentcolor"/></svg>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite">
          <div class="capsule"><button type="button" id="add" aria-label="Add one">+1</button></div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite">
          <div class="capsule number"><strong id="count">72</strong></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-8 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 10%, var(--bg));
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, transparent);
}
.capsule { color: var(--accent); font-size: 14px; }
.capsule button { padding: 4px 8px; }
.number strong { font-size: 18px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const count = document.getElementById('count');
document.getElementById('add').addEventListener('click', () => {
  count.textContent = (Number(count.textContent) + 1) % 100;
});
```

Text, an SVG icon, a button and a number, each in a capsule.

Any HTML goes in a capsule. It works inside a `.satellite` and inside a `.side`. Content placed directly in a satellite is not centered or kept upright, and with `dev-orbit` on the `.bigbang` the console says so.

A capsule is as wide as its satellite and as tall as its content, so text wraps at the satellite's width. Give the capsule its own `width` for a label wider than the satellite. Like satellites, capsules have no border or background until you give them one.

## Where it sits in the satellite

A capsule is centered in its satellite. An alignment class on the satellite moves it: `.at-top-left`, `.at-top`, `.at-top-right`, `.at-center-left`, `.at-center-right`, `.at-bottom-left`, `.at-bottom` or `.at-bottom-right`. `.at-center` is the exception: on a satellite it places the satellite itself at the center of the system.

## Turning the content

`.flip` turns a capsule upside down, `.turn-left` a quarter turn left and `.turn-right` a quarter turn right. In a `.spin-lock` satellite the content turns with the satellite and points its top at the center; `.flip` makes it point outward.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-9" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.4">
        <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">Orbit</div></div>
        <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule turn-right">right</div></div>
        <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule flip">flip</div></div>
        <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule turn-left">left</div></div>
      </div>
      <!-- spin-lock satellites point their top at the center; flip makes them read outward. -->
      <div class="orbit-4 inner" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.4">
        <div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">out</div></div>
        <div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">out</div></div>
        <div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">out</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-9, .orbit-4 { border-color: var(--faint); }
.satellite {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, var(--bg));
  color: var(--accent);
  font-size: 13px;
  font-weight: 600;
}
.inner .satellite {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 14%, var(--bg));
  color: var(--amber);
}
```

Outer ring: the four orientations. Inner ring: `spin-lock` satellites with flipped capsules, reading outward.

## In a side

In a `.side`, a capsule lies along the side and turns with it, which suits labels on the edges of a polygon. Labels on the lower edges read upright; `.flip` turns over the ones at the top, and `.horizontal` keeps a capsule level instead.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule flip"><span>flip</span></div></div>
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule"><span>along</span></div></div>
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule"><span>along</span></div></div>
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule horizontal"><span>horizontal</span></div></div>
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule"><span>along</span></div></div>
        <div class="side"><div class="capsule flip"><span>flip</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.side { height: 2px; background: var(--faint); }
.capsule span {
  padding: 2px 9px;
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 16%, var(--bg));
  color: var(--accent);
  font-size: 12px;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
```

## Reference

| Class | Goes on | What it does |
| `.capsule` | child of `.satellite` or `.side` | Holds content, centered and upright. As wide as its satellite. |
| `.flip` | capsule | Upside down. |
| `.turn-left` / `.turn-right` | capsule | A quarter turn. |
| `.horizontal` | capsule in a side | Stays level instead of following the side. |
| `.at-top-left` … `.at-bottom-right` | satellite | Moves the capsule inside the satellite. |
| `.spin-lock` | satellite | The capsule turns with the satellite. See [Satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html). |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html

# Vectors

A `.vector` is a ray pointing out from the center, laid across its ring. A ring of vectors is a scale; a long one is a needle.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang clock" role="img" aria-label="Clock">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center face"></div></div>
      <!-- Two scales on one lane: 60 short ticks and 12 long ones. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 minutes" id="minutes" style="--o-size-ratio: .5"></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 hours" id="hours"></div>
      <!-- Each hand is a vector twice as long as its lane, so it starts at the center. -->
      <div class="orbit-3 hand" id="hour" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-4 hand" id="minute" style="--o-size-ratio: 8"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-5 hand" id="second" style="--o-size-ratio: 10"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 1"><div class="satellite at-center hub"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.face {
  background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #1a222c, #0e1318 72%);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line);
}
.minutes .vector { background: var(--faint); }
.hours .vector { height: 3px; background: var(--text); }
/* A hand turns with its ring. */
.hand { rotate: var(--turn, 0deg); }
#hour .vector { height: 5px; border-radius: 3px; background: var(--text); }
#minute .vector { height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
#second .vector { height: 1px; background: var(--amber); }
.hub { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
document.getElementById('minutes').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(60);
document.getElementById('hours').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(12);
const turn = (id, deg) => document.getElementById(id).style.setProperty('--turn', deg + 'deg');
const tick = () => {
  const now = new Date(), s = now.getSeconds(), m = now.getMinutes() + s / 60, h = now.getHours() % 12 + m / 60;
  turn('second', s * 6);
  turn('minute', m * 6);
  turn('hour', h * 30);
  document.querySelector('.clock').setAttribute('aria-label', now.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' }));
};
tick();
setInterval(tick, 1000);
```

60 and 12 ticks share `orbit-11`. The three hands are vectors on `orbit-3`, `orbit-4` and `orbit-5`, each turned with `rotate`.

## Length and look

A vector is one lane long and 1px thick, in the text color. Its look is plain CSS: `height` for the thickness, `background` for the color, `border-radius` for round ends. For the length, set `--o-size-ratio` in lanes on the vector, its ring or the `.gravity-spot`, or use the classes:

- `.shrink-5` to `.shrink-100`: shorter than a lane. `shrink-30` is 0.7 lanes.
- `.grow-1x` to `.grow-12x`: 2 to 24 lanes, with decimals like `grow-1.5x` (3 lanes). `.grow-0.1x` to `.grow-0.9x` add tenths of a lane.

Like every element on a ring, a vector is centered on its lane and reaches half its length to each side. So a vector `2N` lanes long on `orbit-N` starts at the center: that is the minute hand above, 8 lanes on `orbit-4`.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="vector shrink-50"></div>
        <div class="vector"></div>
        <div class="vector grow-0.5x"></div>
        <div class="vector grow-1x"></div>
        <div class="vector grow-1.5x"></div>
        <div class="vector grow-2x"></div>
        <div class="vector thick"></div>
        <div class="vector dashed"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-8 { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); }
.vector { height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
/* The look is plain CSS. */
.thick { --o-size-ratio: 2; height: 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--amber); }
.dashed {
  --o-size-ratio: 3;
  border-radius: 0;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--amber) 0 5px, transparent 5px 9px);
}
```

Clockwise from the top: half a lane, one, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 lanes, then two styled with CSS.

## Position and angle

`.inner-orbit` moves a vector in so it ends on its lane, and `.outer-orbit` moves it out so it starts there; `.quarter-inner-orbit` and `.quarter-outer-orbit` go part of the way, and `--o-alignment` takes any length. `.angle-0` to `.angle-360` point a vector at an exact angle, clockwise from the top. The ring's range, start and direction work as for satellites; see [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#angles).

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 lane" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
        <div class="vector angle-0 outer-orbit"></div>
        <div class="vector angle-90"></div>
        <div class="vector angle-180 inner-orbit"></div>
      </div>
      <!-- Seven ticks over 90°, from 225°: the first and last on the ends. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 range-90 from-225 fit-range ticks" id="ticks"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.lane { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); }
.lane .vector { height: 4px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
.ticks .vector { height: 2px; background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
document.getElementById('ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(7);
```

On `orbit-8`: `outer-orbit` at 0°, default at 90°, `inner-orbit` at 180°. On `orbit-11`: seven ticks over 90° from 225°.

## Reference

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Length, in lanes. |
| `height`, `background` | `1px`, `currentcolor` | Thickness and color. |
| `.shrink-5` … `.shrink-100` | | Shorter: `shrink-N` is 1 − N/100 lanes. |
| `.grow-1x` … `.grow-12x`, `.grow-0.1x` … | | Longer: `grow-Nx` is 2N lanes. |
| `.inner-orbit`, `.outer-orbit`, `.quarter-inner-orbit`, `.quarter-outer-orbit` | | Moves it in or out from its lane. |
| `--o-alignment` | `1px` | Any offset from the lane; positive is inward. |
| `.angle-0` … `.angle-360` | | An exact angle, clockwise from the top. |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html

# Sides

A `.side` is a straight line between two neighbors on a ring. Put N sides on a ring and they close a regular polygon with N corners.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-11 outer" id="outer"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8 mid">
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-5 inner">
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Sides on orbit-11 <input id="count" type="range" min="3" max="12" value="6"></label>
    <output id="out">6</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.side { height: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
.mid .side { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 60%, transparent); }
.inner .side { background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const outer = document.getElementById('outer'), count = document.getElementById('count');
const draw = () => {
  outer.innerHTML = '<div class="side"></div>'.repeat(count.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = count.value;
};
count.addEventListener('input', draw);
draw();
```

Sides on `orbit-11`, four on `orbit-8` and three on `orbit-5`.

A side is 1px thick, in the text color. Its look is plain CSS: `height` for the thickness and `background` for the color. Its length comes from the number of sides on the ring, so it has no size classes.

## Inside or around the ring

By default the corners of the polygon sit on the ring. With `.outer-orbit` on every side, the middle of each side touches the ring instead, and the polygon wraps around it.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 ring">
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      </div>
      <!-- The same five sides, touching the ring at their middle. -->
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="side outer-orbit"></div><div class="side outer-orbit"></div><div class="side outer-orbit"></div>
        <div class="side outer-orbit"></div><div class="side outer-orbit"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.ring { border: 1px dashed var(--faint); }
.side { height: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
.outer-orbit { background: var(--amber); }
```

Teal: corners on the ring. Amber: `.outer-orbit`, sides touching it.

## Partial polygons

Sides follow the ring's `--o-range` and `--o-from`: three sides on `range-180` are half a hexagon. To put a single side at a given angle, use `.angle-N` on it, as with satellites: `angle-90` is the right edge.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10 range-180 from-270">
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-6 range-240 from-240 four">
        <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.orbit-10, .orbit-6 { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
.side { height: 3px; background: var(--accent); }
.four .side { background: var(--amber); }
```

Half a hexagon on `orbit-10` (`range-180 from-270`), and four sides over 240° on `orbit-6`.

A side can carry a `.capsule` for a label along its edge. See [Capsules](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/capsule.html).

## Reference

| Class or property | Default | What it does |
| `.side` | | One edge of a regular polygon, as long as the ring's range divided by the number of sides. |
| `height`, `background` | `1px`, `currentcolor` | Thickness and color. |
| `.outer-orbit` | | The side touches the ring at its middle, so the polygon wraps around it. |
| `--o-range`, `--o-from`, `.ccw` | | From the ring. See [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#angles). |
| `.angle-N` | | Puts the side at N degrees, clockwise from the top. |

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html

# Arcs

`<o-arc>` draws a piece of a lane, with text along it if you want. Sibling arcs split their ring between them, or stack one after another by value.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- Text only: a label as long as its words. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 label">
        <o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle">Segments</o-arc>
      </div>
      <!-- No value: eight arcs split the ring evenly. -->
      <div class="orbit-9 segments" id="segments" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.5"></div>
      <!-- With value: arcs stack one after another, a donut. -->
      <div class="orbit-5 donut" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
        <o-arc value="45"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="30"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="25"></o-arc>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.label o-arc { --o-fill: transparent; color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; }
.segments o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, transparent);
  --o-gap: 3;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.segments o-arc:hover { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
.donut o-arc { --o-stroke: none; }
.donut o-arc:nth-child(1) { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
.donut o-arc:nth-child(2) { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, var(--bg)); }
.donut o-arc:nth-child(3) { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 25%, var(--bg)); }
```

```js
document.getElementById('segments').innerHTML = '<o-arc interactive></o-arc>'.repeat(8);
```

A label that fits its text, eight equal segments (hover them), and a donut of 45, 30 and 25.

Arcs go straight into a ring, next to satellites or vectors if you like. They are drawn by the runtime, so they need the Orbit script.

## Reference

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | | Share of the ring's range, out of `max`. Without it, arcs split the range equally. See Split or stack. |
| `max` | `100` | The value that fills the whole range. |
| `range` | | `auto` makes the arc as long as its text. See Arcs that fit their text. |
| `shape` | `none` | The ending. See Endings. |
| `text-anchor` | `middle` | Text along the arc: `start`, `middle` or `end`. On a `range="auto"` arc, where the arc sits around its angle. |
| `flip` | | Runs the text the other way, so it reads upright at the bottom. Also works as a class. |
| `fit-range` | | Stretches or squeezes the text to the whole arc. Also works as a class. |
| `interactive` | | Makes the whole band clickable, even where it is transparent. See Pointer interaction. |
| `hit-width` | `0` | Extra touch area, in px, on each side of an `interactive` band. |
| Property or class | Default | What it does |
| `--o-fill` | `var(--o-gray-light)` | Band color. `transparent` for text only. |
| `--o-stroke` | `var(--o-fill)` | Outline color. |
| `--o-stroke-width` | `1` | Outline width, in px. |
| `color` or `--o-color` | `currentcolor` | Text color. Other font properties apply too. |
| `--o-gap`, `.gap-0` … `.gap-30` | `1` | Space at each end of the arc. Cascades from the ring and the system. |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Thickness, in lanes. `.grow-*` and `.shrink-*` work as on [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html). |
| `.inner-orbit`, `.outer-orbit`, `.quarter-*-orbit` | | Moves the band in or out from its lane. |
| `.angle-0` … `.angle-360` | | Starts the arc at that angle. |

## Split or stack

Without `value`, sibling arcs share the ring equally: a segmented ring, or a pie when they are thick. With `value`, each takes its share of the range and starts where the previous one ended: a donut chart. Values are not normalized, so make them add up to `max` for a full ring. With `max="24"`, `value="6"` is a quarter. An explicit `value="0"` draws nothing and takes no room.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-7 slices" style="--o-size-ratio: 5; --o-gap: 0">
        <o-arc value="50" style="--o-fill: var(--accent)"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="25" style="--o-fill: var(--blue)"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="15" style="--o-fill: var(--violet)"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="5" style="--o-fill: var(--amber)"></o-arc>
        <o-arc value="5" style="--o-fill: var(--coral)"></o-arc>
      </div>
      <!-- Labels at the middle angle of the three big slices. -->
      <div class="orbit-7">
        <div class="satellite angle-90"><div class="capsule">50</div></div>
        <div class="satellite angle-225"><div class="capsule">25</div></div>
        <div class="satellite angle-297"><div class="capsule">15</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.slices o-arc { --o-stroke: var(--bg); --o-stroke-width: 2; }
.capsule {
  color: var(--bg);
  font-size: 15px;
  font-weight: 700;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
```

Five arcs with values 50, 25, 15, 5 and 5, and three satellites at the middle angle of the big ones.

## Color

`--o-fill` colors the band, and `--o-stroke` and `--o-stroke-width` its outline. They change with a short transition, so a hover state is one rule. Hover needs `interactive`: arcs ignore the pointer until you ask.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8" id="ring" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-arc { cursor: pointer; }
o-arc.outlined {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: var(--accent);
  --o-stroke-width: 2;
}
o-arc.plain {
  --o-fill: var(--line);
}
/* One rule per state: the colors change with a short transition. */
o-arc.outlined:hover { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
o-arc.plain:hover { --o-fill: var(--amber); }
```

```js
document.getElementById('ring').innerHTML =
  '<o-arc interactive class="outlined"></o-arc><o-arc interactive class="plain"></o-arc>'.repeat(4);
```

Hover the segments.

## Endings

`shape` sets how each end looks: `circle` (or `circle-a`), `circle-b`, `bullet`, `arrow`, `slash`, `backslash`, `rounded` and `zigzag`. Endings are sized from the band, so they look the same on every ring and at every size.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="grid" id="grid"></div>
</main>
```

```css
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, 92px);
  justify-content: center;
  justify-items: center;
  width: min(100%, 560px);
  gap: 14px 24px;
}
.cell { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 4px; }
.cell code { color: var(--muted); }
.bigbang { width: 92px; }
.gravity-spot { --o-size-ratio: 3; --o-gap: 6; }
o-arc { --o-stroke: none; }
o-arc:nth-child(1) { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, var(--bg)); }
o-arc:nth-child(2) { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 65%, var(--bg)); }
o-arc:nth-child(3) { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
```

```js
const shapes = ['none', 'circle', 'circle-b', 'bullet', 'arrow', 'slash', 'backslash', 'rounded', 'zigzag'];
// Three arcs per ring, all with the same ending.
document.getElementById('grid').innerHTML = shapes.map(shape => `
  <div class="cell">
    <div class="bigbang"><div class="gravity-spot"><div class="orbit-9">
      ${`<o-arc shape="${shape}"></o-arc>`.repeat(3)}
    </div></div></div>
    <code>${shape}</code>
  </div>`).join('');
```

## Thickness, position and gaps

An arc is one lane thick. Set `--o-size-ratio` in lanes on the arc, its ring or the `.gravity-spot`, or use the `.grow-*` and `.shrink-*` classes on the arc. `.inner-orbit` and `.outer-orbit` move the band in or out so one of its edges sits on the lane, and the `.quarter-` versions go part of the way.

`--o-gap` is the space left at each end of an arc. It cascades, so one value on the ring spaces all its arcs; `.gap-0` to `.gap-30` set it on one arc. A ring of 3 to 6 thick segments usually wants `--o-gap` between 24 and 60 to read as separate pieces.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10 lane" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-arc class="outer-orbit"></o-arc>
        <o-arc class="quarter-outer-orbit"></o-arc>
        <o-arc></o-arc>
        <o-arc class="quarter-inner-orbit"></o-arc>
        <o-arc class="inner-orbit"></o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-5 gaps" id="gaps" style="--o-size-ratio: 3; --o-gap: 40">
        <o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-gap on orbit-5 <input id="gap" type="range" min="0" max="60" value="40"></label>
    <output id="out">40</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
/* The lane on top, so you can see where each band sits. */
.lane { border: 2px solid var(--amber); z-index: 1; }
.lane o-arc { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, transparent); --o-stroke: none; }
.gaps o-arc { --o-fill: var(--accent); --o-stroke: none; }
```

```js
const gap = document.getElementById('gap');
gap.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('gaps').style.setProperty('--o-gap', gap.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = gap.value;
});
```

Outer ring, clockwise from the top: `outer-orbit`, `quarter-outer-orbit`, default, `quarter-inner-orbit`, `inner-orbit`. Inner ring: `--o-gap`.

Arcs follow the ring's `--o-range`, `--o-from` and `.ccw` (see [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#angles)). `.angle-N` on an arc starts it at that angle instead of its turn on the ring.

## Curved text

Text inside an `<o-arc>` is drawn along it. Style it like any text: `color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `text-transform`. The font size is the same in px on every ring. Set `--o-fill: transparent` for text with no band.

`text-anchor` places the text at the `start`, `middle` (default) or `end` of its arc.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-9" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-arc text-anchor="start">start</o-arc>
        <o-arc text-anchor="middle">middle</o-arc>
        <o-arc text-anchor="end">end</o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-5 range-180 from-270">
        <o-arc class="plain">No band, in bold</o-arc>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-gap: 4;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 14px;
}
o-arc.plain {
  --o-fill: transparent;
  color: var(--accent);
  font-weight: 700;
}
```

Text runs clockwise, so on the lower half of a ring it reads upside down. `flip` runs it the other way:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10" id="months" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-gap: 3;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 13px;
}
o-arc[flip] {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 20%, transparent);
}
```

```js
const months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
// April to September sit on the lower half: flip them so they read upright.
document.getElementById('months').innerHTML = months.map((month, i) =>
  `<o-arc${i >= 3 && i <= 8 ? ' flip' : ''}>${month}</o-arc>`).join('');
```

April to September, in amber, have `flip`.

Text longer than its arc is cut off, and the console says so with an `[orbit]` message. Shorten it, widen the range, let the arc fit the text with `range="auto"`, or add `fit-range` to squeeze or stretch the text to the arc:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 from-225" id="ring" style="--o-range: 270deg; --o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-arc fit-range>This text runs along the whole arc</o-arc>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Range <input id="range" type="range" min="150" max="360" step="5" value="270"></label>
    <output id="out">270°</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 14px;
}
```

```js
const range = document.getElementById('range');
range.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('ring').style.setProperty('--o-range', range.value + 'deg');
  document.getElementById('out').value = range.value + '°';
});
```

Change the range: the text stretches or squeezes to fill it.

## Arcs that fit their text

With `range="auto"` an arc is as long as its text, with half a letter of room at each end. Consecutive auto arcs follow each other, which makes curved menus easy:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <nav class="orbit-10 from-300 menu" style="--o-size-ratio: 2" aria-label="Sections">
        <o-arc interactive range="auto" tabindex="0" role="link" aria-current="page">Home</o-arc>
        <o-arc interactive range="auto" tabindex="0" role="link">Projects</o-arc>
        <o-arc interactive range="auto" tabindex="0" role="link">About</o-arc>
      </nav>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 12">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong id="page">Home</strong><span>you are here</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-gap: 4;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 14px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
o-arc:hover, o-arc:focus-visible { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 32%, transparent); outline: none; }
.menu { border-color: var(--line); }
o-arc[aria-current] { --o-fill: var(--accent); color: var(--bg); font-weight: 600; }
.readout strong { font-size: 30px; }
```

```js
const items = document.querySelectorAll('.menu o-arc');
const pick = item => {
  items.forEach(other => other.toggleAttribute('aria-current', other === item));
  document.getElementById('page').textContent = item.textContent;
};
items.forEach(item => {
  item.addEventListener('click', () => pick(item));
  item.addEventListener('keydown', event => { if (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ') { event.preventDefault(); pick(item); } });
});
```

Three auto arcs, one after another. Click one, or tab to it and press Enter.

An auto arc starts at its angle. `text-anchor="middle"` centers it there instead, and `text-anchor="end"` ends it there. Both labels here are anchored at the top:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10 lane">
        <o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle">Centered at 0°</o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-7 lane">
        <o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="end">Ends at 0°</o-arc>
      </div>
      <!-- A line pointing at 0°, the angle both labels are anchored to. -->
      <div class="orbit-3" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"><div class="vector angle-0 mark"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.lane { border: 1px dashed var(--line); }
o-arc {
  --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 14px;
}
.mark { height: 2px; background: var(--amber); }
```

The amber line points at 0°.

## Pointer interaction

Arcs are decorative by default, so they never steal clicks from controls nearby. `interactive` makes the whole band clickable, even where its fill is transparent, and `hit-width` adds touch area in px on each side, which helps with thin arcs on touch screens.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8 range-270 from-225" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-arc interactive hit-width="12" tabindex="0" role="switch" aria-checked="false" aria-label="Toggle"></o-arc>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-arc {
  --o-fill: transparent;
  --o-stroke: var(--accent);
  --o-stroke-width: 2;
  cursor: pointer;
}
o-arc:focus-visible { outline: none; --o-stroke-width: 3; }
o-arc[aria-checked="true"] { --o-stroke: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const arc = document.querySelector('o-arc');
const toggle = () => arc.setAttribute('aria-checked', String(arc.getAttribute('aria-checked') !== 'true'));
arc.addEventListener('click', toggle);
arc.addEventListener('keydown', event => { if (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ' ') { event.preventDefault(); toggle(); } });
```

Only the outline is drawn, yet a click anywhere on the band, or up to 12px around it, toggles the color.

When an arc acts as a control, you bring the keyboard behavior and the accessible name. Arcs are placed with the `rotate` property, so your own `transform` or `scale` (on hover, say) adds to it instead of replacing it.

## After drawing

Each `<o-arc>` fires a bubbling `o-rendered` event after it redraws. To wait for every arc on the page, for example before measuring, use `await Orbit.ready()`. See [Runtime and resizing](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html

# Progress

`<o-progress>` fills a lane up to a value, over a track that shows the whole range. It is the base of progress rings, gauges and meters.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-progress id="bar" value="0" shape="rounded" role="progressbar"
          aria-label="Upload" aria-valuenow="0" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 12">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong id="value">0%</strong><span>uploaded</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Value <input id="input" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72"></label>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 40px; }
```

```js
const bar = document.getElementById('bar'), input = document.getElementById('input');
const set = value => {
  bar.setAttribute('value', value);
  bar.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', value);
  document.getElementById('value').textContent = value + '%';
};
input.addEventListener('input', () => set(input.value));
// Fill up on load.
const target = Number(input.value), start = performance.now();
const grow = now => {
  const t = Math.min(1, (now - start) / 900);
  set(Math.round(target * (1 - (1 - t) ** 3)));
  if (t < 1) requestAnimationFrame(grow);
};
requestAnimationFrame(grow);
```

A progress goes straight into a ring, one per ring: put each bar of a multi-bar meter on its own ring. It is drawn by the runtime, so it needs the Orbit script. For screen readers, give it `role="progressbar"` and the `aria-` values, as above.

## Reference

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | `0` | Progress, out of `max`. |
| `max` | `100` | The value that fills the ring's range. |
| `shape` | `none` | The ending. See Endings. |
| `variant` | | `stroke` draws thin lines instead of filled bands. See Stroke variant. |
| `interactive` | | Makes the whole track clickable, whatever its colors. See Pointer interaction. |
| `hit-width` | `0` | Extra touch area, in px, on each side of an `interactive` track. |
| Property or class | Default | What it does |
| `--o-progress` | | The value, set from CSS. Wins over `value`. |
| `--o-fill` | `var(--o-gray-light)` | Bar color. Not used by `variant="stroke"`. |
| `--o-stroke` | `var(--o-fill)` | Bar outline, or the line color with `variant="stroke"`. |
| `--o-stroke-width` | `1` (`2` with `stroke`) | Bar outline width, or the line width, in px. |
| `--o-back-fill` | `transparent` | Track color. Not used by `variant="stroke"`. |
| `--o-back-stroke` | `none` (gray with `stroke`) | Track outline, or the track line color. |
| `--o-back-stroke-width` | `1` | Track outline or line width, in px. |
| `--o-size-ratio` | `1` | Thickness, in lanes. `.grow-*` and `.shrink-*` work as on [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html). |
| `.inner-orbit`, `.outer-orbit`, `.quarter-*-orbit` | | Moves the band in or out from its lane. |
| `.angle-0` … `.angle-360` | | Starts the bar at that angle instead of the ring's `--o-from`. |

## Value and color

`value` runs from 0 to `max` (100 by default) and fills that share of the ring's range. `--o-fill` colors the bar and `--o-back-fill` the track behind it; `--o-stroke` and `--o-back-stroke` outline them.

`--o-progress` sets the value from CSS and wins over the attribute. Use it when a class or a parent owns the state:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- The value comes from CSS: a class on the universe changes it. -->
      <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-progress class="level"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-6" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-progress value="50" max="80" class="other"></o-progress>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" id="toggle" aria-pressed="false">Toggle full</button>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
o-progress { --o-stroke: none; }
o-progress.level {
  --o-progress: 30;
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
}
.full o-progress.level {
  --o-progress: 90;
}
o-progress.other {
  --o-fill: var(--amber);
  --o-back-stroke: var(--faint);
}
```

```js
const toggle = document.getElementById('toggle');
toggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const full = document.querySelector('.bigbang').classList.toggle('full');
  toggle.setAttribute('aria-pressed', full);
});
```

Outer ring: `--o-progress` from a class. Inner ring: `value="50" max="80"`, with an outlined track.

Orbit redraws when the element's or an ancestor's `class` or `style` changes. After a change it cannot see, such as editing a stylesheet rule, call `Orbit.refresh()`. The value does not animate: a `transition` on `--o-progress` jumps straight to the new value.

## Gauges

A progress fills the ring's range, so a partial range makes a gauge. `range-240 from-240` leaves the gap at the bottom:

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang" role="meter" aria-label="Speed" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="64">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- 240° with the gap at the bottom. -->
      <div class="orbit-10 range-240 from-240" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
        <o-progress id="bar" value="64" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 10">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong id="value">64</strong><span>km/h</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>Speed <input id="input" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="64"></label>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: var(--line);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 36px; }
```

```js
const input = document.getElementById('input');
input.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('bar').setAttribute('value', input.value);
  document.querySelector('.bigbang').setAttribute('aria-valuenow', input.value);
  document.getElementById('value').textContent = input.value;
});
```

## Endings

`shape` sets how the bar ends: `circle` (or `circle-a`), `circle-b`, `bullet`, `arrow`, `slash`, `backslash`, `rounded` and `zigzag`. Endings are sized from the band, so they look the same on every ring and at every size.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="grid" id="grid"></div>
</main>
```

```css
.grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, 92px);
  justify-content: center;
  justify-items: center;
  width: min(100%, 560px);
  gap: 14px 24px;
}
.cell { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 4px; }
.cell code { color: var(--muted); }
.bigbang { width: 92px; }
.gravity-spot { --o-size-ratio: 3; }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 18%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
```

```js
const shapes = ['none', 'circle', 'circle-b', 'bullet', 'arrow', 'slash', 'backslash', 'rounded', 'zigzag'];
document.getElementById('grid').innerHTML = shapes.map(shape => `
  <div class="cell">
    <div class="bigbang"><div class="gravity-spot"><div class="orbit-9">
      <o-progress value="70" shape="${shape}"></o-progress>
    </div></div></div>
    <code>${shape}</code>
  </div>`).join('');
```

## Stroke variant

By default the bar is a filled band. For a thin gauge line, add `variant="stroke"`: the bar and the track become lines along the middle of the lane, with round caps.

- `--o-stroke` colors the line and `--o-back-stroke` the track. `--o-fill` and `--o-back-fill` are not used.
- The line is 2px wide (`--o-stroke-width`) and the track 1px (`--o-back-stroke-width`), in screen pixels at any size.
- The track is gray by default; set `--o-back-stroke` to color it, or `none` to hide it.
- `shape` does not apply. A full value on a 360° range draws a closed circle.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-11">
        <o-progress variant="stroke" value="72" class="thick"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-9">
        <o-progress variant="stroke" value="45" class="tinted"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-7">
        <o-progress variant="stroke" value="100" class="full"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-5 range-270 from-225">
        <o-progress variant="stroke" value="60" class="gauge"></o-progress>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-progress { --o-stroke: var(--accent); }
o-progress.thick {
  --o-stroke-width: 8;
  --o-back-stroke: var(--line);
  --o-back-stroke-width: 4;
}
o-progress.tinted {
  --o-stroke: var(--amber);
  --o-back-stroke: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 30%, transparent);
}
o-progress.full { --o-stroke: var(--muted); }
o-progress.gauge {
  --o-stroke-width: 4;
  --o-back-stroke: var(--line);
}
```

From the outside in: an 8px line, a tinted track, a full circle, and a 270° gauge.

## Thickness and position

A progress is one lane thick. Set `--o-size-ratio` in lanes on the element, its ring or the `.gravity-spot`, or use the `.grow-*` and `.shrink-*` classes on the element. `.inner-orbit` and `.outer-orbit` move the band in or out so one of its edges sits on the lane, and the `.quarter-` versions go part of the way. A band two lanes thick on `orbit-11` ends exactly at the edge of the universe.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <!-- One thickness for every ring, set once on the system. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot" id="system" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
      <div class="orbit-11"><o-progress value="80" shape="circle" class="move"></o-progress></div>
      <div class="orbit-9"><o-progress value="60" shape="circle" class="exercise"></o-progress></div>
      <div class="orbit-7"><o-progress value="45" shape="circle" class="stand"></o-progress></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <label>--o-size-ratio <input id="size" type="range" min=".5" max="2" step=".1" value="2"></label>
    <output id="out">2</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--c);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 16%, transparent);
}
.move { --c: var(--coral); }
.exercise { --c: var(--lime); }
.stand { --c: var(--accent); }
```

```js
const size = document.getElementById('size');
size.addEventListener('input', () => {
  document.getElementById('system').style.setProperty('--o-size-ratio', size.value);
  document.getElementById('out').value = size.value;
});
```

Three rings, their thickness set once on the `.gravity-spot`. At 2 lanes they touch each other and the edge.

## Pointer interaction

`<o-progress>` is decorative by default, so it never steals clicks from controls nearby. `interactive` makes the whole track clickable, including the part the bar does not cover, whatever its colors. `hit-width` adds touch area in px on each side, which helps with thin bars on touch screens.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <o-progress id="bar" interactive hit-width="12" variant="stroke" value="30"
          tabindex="0" role="slider" aria-label="Level" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="30"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 10">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong id="value">30</strong><span>click the ring</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: var(--accent);
  --o-stroke-width: 4;
  --o-back-stroke: var(--line);
  --o-back-stroke-width: 4;
  cursor: pointer;
}
o-progress:focus-visible { outline: none; --o-back-stroke: var(--faint); }
.readout strong { font-size: 30px; }
```

```js
const bar = document.getElementById('bar');
const set = value => {
  bar.setAttribute('value', value);
  bar.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', value);
  document.getElementById('value').textContent = value;
};
// A click adds 10 and wraps after 100; the arrow keys step by 10 too.
bar.addEventListener('click', () => set((Number(bar.getAttribute('value')) + 10) % 110));
bar.addEventListener('keydown', event => {
  const step = { ArrowUp: 10, ArrowRight: 10, ArrowDown: -10, ArrowLeft: -10 }[event.key];
  if (step) { event.preventDefault(); set(Math.max(0, Math.min(100, Number(bar.getAttribute('value')) + step))); }
});
```

Each click on the thin track, or up to 12px around it, adds 10.

When a progress acts as a control, you bring the keyboard behavior and the accessible name. It is placed with the `rotate` property, so your own `transform` or `scale` adds to it instead of replacing it.

## After drawing

Each `<o-progress>` fires a bubbling `o-rendered` event after it redraws. To wait for everything on the page, for example before measuring, use `await Orbit.ready()`. See [Runtime and resizing](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html

# Depth layers

Add `depth` to a `.gravity-spot` and its rings stack on the z axis. The layer in front is the one people read and use; the others wait behind it.

Each direct child of the `.depth` element is a layer: a ring, or a nested `.gravity-spot` when a layer needs several rings of its own.

- `data-depth="1"` moves a layer one step back. Values go from `0` to `8`.
- `.layer-front` marks the active layer and places it at depth 0.
- `--o-z` sets the position directly, in unitless pixels. Negative values are farther away.

Layers keep their apparent size: the scale makes up for the perspective, `(perspective − z) / perspective`. So three rings on `orbit-6` would sit exactly on top of each other. `--o-depth-grow` makes each step back a bit bigger, so you can see them all. Depth changes animate.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <!-- Each ring is a layer; data-depth sends it back. -->
  <div class="gravity-spot depth">
    <div class="orbit-6 layer-front" data-depth="0">
      <o-progress value="82" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-6" data-depth="1">
      <o-progress value="40" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-6" data-depth="2">
      <o-progress value="65" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="controls"><button id="next">Next layer</button></div>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
  height: 100vh;
  padding: 16px 16px 14px;
}
.bigbang { max-height: 100%; }
.controls { justify-content: center; }
.gravity-spot {
  --o-size-ratio: 1.2;
  --o-depth-grow: .42;
  --o-back-opacity: .5;
}
o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--faint);
  --o-back-fill: var(--line);
}
.layer-front o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 16%, transparent);
}
```

```js
const layers = [...document.querySelectorAll('.depth > [data-depth]')];
let front = 0;
document.querySelector('#next').addEventListener('click', () => {
  front = (front + 1) % layers.length;
  layers.forEach((layer, i) => {
    const depth = (i - front + layers.length) % layers.length;
    layer.dataset.depth = depth;
    layer.classList.toggle('layer-front', depth === 0);
  });
});
```

## A whole system as a layer

A layer can hold several rings, a label and a face that move together. Make it a nested `.gravity-spot` with `data-depth`. It has the same reach as its parent, so it needs no `--o-force`, and it does not block the pointer outside its satellites.

Below, three gauges are stacked that way. Click a face to bring it forward, and move the pointer over the frame to tilt the stack.

```html
<div class="tilt">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot depth outer-perspective stack">
      <div class="gravity-spot layer layer-front" data-depth="0" style="--c: var(--accent)">
        <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
        <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 14">
          <div class="satellite at-center"><button class="capsule face" type="button"><strong>72%</strong><span>CPU</span></button></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="gravity-spot layer" data-depth="1" style="--c: var(--amber)">
        <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><o-progress value="48" shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
        <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 14">
          <div class="satellite at-center"><button class="capsule face" type="button"><strong>48%</strong><span>Memory</span></button></div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="gravity-spot layer" data-depth="2" style="--c: var(--violet)">
        <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><o-progress value="91" shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
        <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 14">
          <div class="satellite at-center"><button class="capsule face" type="button"><strong>91%</strong><span>Disk</span></button></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
/* The ancestor that owns the perspective. */
.tilt {
  width: min(90vw, 260px);
  perspective: 1000px;
}
.tilt > .bigbang {
  rotate: x var(--rx, 0deg);
  transform: rotateY(var(--ry, 0deg));
  transition: rotate .2s, transform .2s;
}
/* Same value as the perspective above, without the unit. */
.stack {
  --o-perspective: 1000;
  --o-depth-grow: .24;
  --o-back-opacity: .3;
}
.layer o-progress {
  --o-stroke: none;
  --o-fill: var(--c);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 14%, var(--bg));
}
.face {
  width: 100%;
  aspect-ratio: 1;
  border-radius: 50%;
  display: grid;
  place-content: center;
  text-align: center;
  background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 10%, var(--panel));
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 40%, transparent);
  border: 0;
  padding: 0;
  color: var(--text);
  cursor: pointer;
}
.face strong {
  color: var(--c);
  font-size: 30px;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.face span {
  font-size: 13px;
  color: var(--muted);
}
```

```js
const layers = [...document.querySelectorAll('.stack > .layer')];
let front = 0;
const bring = (index) => {
  front = (index + layers.length) % layers.length;
  layers.forEach((layer, i) => {
    const depth = (i - front + layers.length) % layers.length;
    layer.dataset.depth = depth;
    layer.classList.toggle('layer-front', depth === 0);
    layer.style.zIndex = layers.length - depth;
  });
};
layers.forEach((layer, i) => {
  layer.querySelector('.face').addEventListener('click', () => bring(i === front ? i + 1 : i));
});
bring(0);

const tilt = document.querySelector('.tilt');
document.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  tilt.style.setProperty('--ry', (e.clientX / innerWidth - .5) * 30 + 'deg');
  tilt.style.setProperty('--rx', -(e.clientY / innerHeight - .5) * 30 + 'deg');
});
document.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => {
  tilt.style.setProperty('--rx', '0deg');
  tilt.style.setProperty('--ry', '0deg');
});
```

## Perspective from an ancestor

By default the `.depth` element owns the perspective. To tilt the whole object, as above, an ancestor has to own it instead: add `outer-perspective` next to `depth`, give the ancestor a `perspective`, and set `--o-perspective` to the same number so layers still keep their apparent size. Elements between that ancestor and `.depth` need `transform-style: preserve-3d`; a `.bigbang` that holds the `.depth` element gets it automatically.

```html
<div style="perspective: 1000px">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot depth outer-perspective" style="--o-perspective: 1000">
      <div class="gravity-spot layer-front" data-depth="0">…</div>
      <div class="gravity-spot" data-depth="1">…</div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Properties

Set these on the `.depth` element, or on a single layer.

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--o-z` | `depth × step` | Position on the z axis in unitless pixels. Set it on a layer to override `data-depth`. |
| `--o-depth-step` | `-110` | Distance between depth steps. |
| `--o-perspective` | `900` | Perspective in unitless pixels. |
| `--o-depth-grow` | `0` | Extra size per step back. `.42` gives 1×, 1.42×, 1.84×, so no two layers share a radius. |
| `--o-depth-compensate` | `1` | `0` lets farther layers look smaller. |
| `--o-back-opacity` | `1` | Opacity of the layers behind the front one. |
| `--o-depth-duration` | `.8s` | Duration of the depth transition. |
| `--o-depth-easing` | `cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)` | Easing of the depth transition. |

The transition is off when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Rules

- **Layers are direct children of `.depth`.** An element in between flattens the 3D context.
- **Rings outside `.depth` are not transformed.** `data-depth` alone does nothing.
- **Satellites, vectors, sides, `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>` are never layers.** They keep their own transforms; put them in a ring and move the ring.
- **Back layers still receive clicks.** Rings ignore the pointer and satellites accept it, so a click on a satellite of a back layer reaches it. That is how the faces above come forward.

The [depth demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/11-depth-layers.html) has the gauges above at full size, and [layered status rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/layered-status-rings.html) a fuller example with alerts.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/themes.html

# Themes

Orbit ships a plain default look, a cyan theme and a helper for building. All of them are written with `:where()`, so they have zero specificity apart from their own class: a single class of yours wins, without `!important`.

## Default theme

Always on. Satellites have no border or background, arcs and progress bands are light gray, and vectors and sides take the current text color. There are no hover colors.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.25">
    <div class="orbit-3">
      <o-arc class="shrink-10 gap-2"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="shrink-10 gap-2"></o-arc>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-5">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">A</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">B</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">C</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">D</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-8">
      <o-progress shape="arrow" value="67"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-10 from-23">
      <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-10">
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Your own look

Style Orbit like anything else: satellites and capsules with ordinary CSS, arcs and progress with custom properties. The [color palette](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/colors.html) is there if you want it. Here is the same layout once more, with a few rules of its own and a hover color on the satellites.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.25">
    <div class="orbit-3">
      <o-arc class="shrink-10 gap-2"></o-arc>
      <o-arc class="shrink-10 gap-2"></o-arc>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-5">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">A</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">B</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">C</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">D</div></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-8">
      <o-progress shape="arrow" value="67"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-10 from-23">
      <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
      <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-10">
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
      <div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div><div class="vector"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* Your own look: ordinary CSS and Orbit's custom properties. */
.orbit-5 .satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--panel);
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line);
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 13px;
}
.orbit-5 .satellite:hover { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
o-arc { --o-fill: var(--line); --o-stroke: none; }
o-progress { --o-fill: var(--accent); --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 12%, transparent); --o-stroke: none; }
.vector { background: var(--faint); }
.side { background: var(--line); }
```
