Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/colors.html

# Colors

Orbit's stylesheet defines a palette of custom properties: ten hues, each in seven shades. The themes use it, and you can too, or ignore it and use your own colors.

The hues are `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `cyan`, `blue`, `indigo`, `purple`, `pink` and `gray`. Each one comes as `--o-{hue}` plus six shades mixed from it in OKLab. For cyan:

| Property | Mix |
| `--o-cyan-white` | 95% white |
| `--o-cyan-lighter` | 75% white |
| `--o-cyan-light` | 30% white |
| `--o-cyan` | the hue itself |
| `--o-cyan-dark` | 20% black |
| `--o-cyan-darker` | 40% black |
| `--o-cyan-black` | 78% black |

Below, every shade on an arc: one ring per shade, from `-black` in the middle to `-white` outside, and one arc per hue. A few lines of JavaScript write the seventy arcs.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot" id="wheel">
    <!-- One ring per shade (orbit-3 to orbit-9) and one arc per hue,
         written by the script. Hue names sit on orbit-11. -->
    <div class="orbit-11 from-18" id="names"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
o-arc {
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.name {
  font: 12px var(--mono);
  color: var(--muted);
}
```

```js
const hues = ['red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'cyan', 'blue', 'indigo', 'purple', 'pink', 'gray'];
const shades = ['-black', '-darker', '-dark', '', '-light', '-lighter', '-white'];
const wheel = document.getElementById('wheel');

shades.forEach((shade, i) => {
  const arcs = hues.map((hue) =>
    `<o-arc class="shrink-10 gap-2" style="--o-fill: var(--o-${hue}${shade})"></o-arc>`).join('');
  wheel.insertAdjacentHTML('afterbegin', `<div class="orbit-${i + 3}">${arcs}</div>`);
});

document.getElementById('names').innerHTML = hues.map((hue) =>
  `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule name">${hue}</div></div>`).join('');
```

## Your own color

`--o-color` is the eleventh hue, and it is yours. Set it on a system, a ring or a satellite, and `--o-color-white` to `--o-color-black` are mixed from it right there. Each ring below sets its own `--o-color` and the arcs use the same three shades: `-lighter`, `-light` and `-dark`.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-11" style="--o-color: #ff7a6b"><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc></div>
    <div class="orbit-8" style="--o-color: #60a5fa"><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc></div>
    <div class="orbit-5" style="--o-color: #a3e635"><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc><o-arc></o-arc></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.gravity-spot { --o-size-ratio: 2.4; }
o-arc { --o-gap: 3; --o-stroke: none; }
o-arc:nth-child(1) { --o-fill: var(--o-color-lighter); }
o-arc:nth-child(2) { --o-fill: var(--o-color-light); }
o-arc:nth-child(3) { --o-fill: var(--o-color-dark); }
```

Arcs and progress take the shades of their ring. On an `<o-arc>` itself, `--o-color` is the color of its text. To change one shade only, set it on the element that uses it.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/visual-aids.html

# Visual aids

Add `dev-orbit` to a `.bigbang` while you build. It draws the gravity spot, the rings and the satellites with dashed red lines, outlines anything in the wrong place, and explains it in the console.

It changes how things look, never where they are, so you can switch it on and off freely. It combines with a theme on the same element. [Themes](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/themes.html) shows a full layout with it on.

## Wrong children of a gravity spot

A `.gravity-spot` holds rings (`.orbit`, `.orbit-N`) and nested gravity spots, nothing else. If it holds anything else, the whole system is dimmed and a warning sign pulses at its center. Here a satellite sits directly in the gravity spot:

```html
<div class="bigbang dev-orbit">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-8">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">A</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">B</div></div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">C</div></div>
    </div>
    <!-- A satellite needs a ring -->
    <div class="satellite"></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.orbit-8 {
  --o-size-ratio: 2;
}
```

## Wrong children of a satellite or a ring

A `.satellite` holds a `.capsule` or a nested `.gravity-spot`. With anything else in it, it gets an orange dotted border and the console names the element. A ring nested in another ring is outlined the same way. This example logs on purpose:

```
[orbit] <div .orbit-10> sits directly in a .satellite. Put content in a .capsule so it stays upright and centered.
```

```html
<div class="bigbang dev-orbit">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-8">
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">A</div></div>
      <div class="satellite">
        <!-- A ring needs a gravity spot -->
        <div class="orbit-10"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">C</div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.orbit-8 {
  --o-size-ratio: 2;
}
```

Content placed directly in a ring, instead of in a `.satellite`, is not outlined, but the console reports it. The full list of messages and their fixes is on the [install page](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/install.html#console).

The outlines use `:has()`. In a browser without it you still get the console messages. The pulsing sign stops when the user prefers reduced motion.

## Arcs on ellipses

`<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>` are drawn on circles only. On a ring stretched into an ellipse with `--o-ellipse-x` or `--o-ellipse-y`, they are hidden. Satellites, vectors and sides follow the ellipse. See [Orbits](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html#ellipses).

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html

# Runtime and resizing

Most of the time there is nothing to call. Layouts follow their box, and the runtime notices changes on its own. The few functions it exports are for waiting, forcing an update, and old fixed-size layouts.

## Sizing needs no code

Every ring, satellite and band is a fraction of its `.bigbang`, so when the box changes size everything inside changes with it. There is no breakpoint to write. Drag the corner of the dashed box:

```html
<div class="wrapper">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-12 reach"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* Drag the corner of the box. */
.wrapper {
  width: 280px;
  height: 200px;
  margin: 16px;
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
  border-radius: 10px;
  resize: both;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.reach {
  border: 1px dashed var(--accent);
}
.orbit-8 {
  --o-size-ratio: 2;
}
.satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
}
```

The `.bigbang` is square and as wide as its parent, and a parent with a height keeps it from growing taller. Here the box is 280 × 200, so the universe is 200px across. Give the `.bigbang` a `width`, `height` or `aspect-ratio` of its own and the system follows that instead.

## What the runtime watches

Orbit watches the page for added, removed and reordered elements, attribute and style changes, and containers that change size. It batches what it sees into the next animation frame. That is why a framework can re-render a layout, or you can change `value` on an `<o-progress>`, and the drawing follows with no extra call.

## Waiting for the drawing

`Orbit.ready()` returns a promise that resolves when every pending layout is drawn. Pass an element, a document or a shadow root to wait only for that part. Use it in tests, or before you measure something.

Each `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>` also fires an `o-rendered` event after it redraws. It bubbles and crosses shadow roots, so one listener on a container hears all of its arcs.

```html
<div class="bigbang">
  <div class="gravity-spot">
    <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 2">
      <o-progress value="40" shape="rounded" role="progressbar" aria-label="Value" aria-valuenow="40"></o-progress>
    </div>
    <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 12">
      <div class="satellite at-center">
        <div class="capsule readout"><strong id="value">40%</strong><span id="draws">waiting</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<label class="controls">Value <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="40"></label>
```

```css
body {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) auto;
  height: 100vh;
  padding: 16px 16px 14px;
}
.bigbang { max-height: 100%; }
.controls { justify-content: center; }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.readout strong { font-size: 34px; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
let draws = 0;

// Fires after every redraw of the arc.
progress.addEventListener('o-rendered', () => {
  draws++;
  document.getElementById('value').textContent = progress.getAttribute('value') + '%';
  document.getElementById('draws').textContent = `drawn ${draws}×`;
});

document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  progress.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', e.target.value);
});

Orbit.ready().then(() => console.log('ready'));
```

## Updating by hand

Two kinds of change are invisible to the runtime: rules you edit through CSSOM, and CSS that depends on something outside the layout, like a class on `<html>` or a checkbox elsewhere on the page. After one of those, call `Orbit.refresh()` with the part that changed. Without an argument it refreshes the whole document.

```js
sheet.cssRules[0].style.setProperty('--o-range', '180deg');
Orbit.refresh(panel);
```

For shadow DOM, include the stylesheet inside each shadow root. Arcs and progress register their shadow root on their own; for a shadow tree with only CSS elements, call `Orbit.refresh(shadowRoot)` once.

## Fixed sizes and Orbit.resize()

When a system should keep a fixed size, give its `.gravity-spot` a length: `--o-force: 300px`. That system no longer follows its box. `Orbit.resize()` brings part of that back: it watches a container and scales the fixed-size systems inside it with its **width**, taking 500px as 1×.

```js
const stopResizing = Orbit.resize('.wrapper');
// When the container goes away:
stopResizing();
```

It takes a selector or an element and returns a function that stops watching. Calling it again on the same container replaces the previous watcher. It leaves systems without a fixed reach alone, and if it finds none the console says `[orbit] Orbit.resize() has nothing to do here`.

Here the same layout has `--o-force: 300px` and `Orbit.resize('.wrapper')`. At 280px wide the reach is 168px (300 × 280 / 500). Drag the corner: only the width counts.

```html
<div class="wrapper">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-force: 300px">
      <div class="orbit-12 reach"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8">
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
        <div class="satellite"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
/* Drag the corner of the box. */
.wrapper {
  width: 280px;
  height: 200px;
  margin: 16px;
  border: 1px dashed var(--faint);
  border-radius: 10px;
  resize: both;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.reach {
  border: 1px dashed var(--accent);
}
.orbit-8 {
  --o-size-ratio: 2;
}
.satellite {
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
}
```

```js
const stopResizing = Orbit.resize('.wrapper');
```

For new layouts, leave `--o-force` alone and size the `.bigbang` instead. `Orbit.resize()` is there mostly for layouts written for Orbit 1.x, where every system was 500px across. [Coming from 1.x](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/migrating.html) has the rest.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/react.html

# React

Orbit is HTML and CSS with a runtime that watches the page, so in React you write the same markup with `className`. There is no wrapper component to install.

## Install

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

Import the stylesheet and the runtime once, in your entry file or in the component that uses Orbit:

```js
import '@zumer/orbit/style';
import '@zumer/orbit';
```

## A gauge

A progress ring with its value in the middle, bound to state. `value` on `<o-progress>` is an attribute, and React sets it like any other.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import '@zumer/orbit/style';
import '@zumer/orbit';
import './gauge.css';

export default function Gauge() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(72);
  return (
    <div className="gauge">
      <div className="bigbang">
        <div className="gravity-spot">
          <div className="orbit-10">
            <o-progress value={value} shape="rounded"></o-progress>
          </div>
          <div className="orbit-0">
            <div className="satellite at-center">
              <div className="capsule">{value}%</div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value={value}
        onChange={(e) => setValue(Number(e.target.value))} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```css
/* gauge.css */
.gauge { width: 220px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--o-cyan);
  --o-back-fill: var(--o-cyan-lighter);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; }
```

Sizes go in CSS rather than in `style`, so TypeScript does not complain about custom properties. Lists work as you expect: render satellites with `map()` and Orbit spreads however many there are.

```html
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule">72%</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72" aria-label="Value">
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.gauge { width: 220px; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
const label = document.querySelector('.capsule');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  label.textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

The same markup in plain HTML. Move the slider: changing `value` is all it takes.

Orbit watches the page for added, removed and reordered elements, attribute and style changes, and containers that change size, so a re-render needs no extra call. To wait until arcs are drawn, or to update after a change Orbit cannot see, use the [runtime API](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

## TypeScript

The package ships JSX types for `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>`. Load them once, for example in a `.d.ts` file of your app:

```ts
import type {} from '@zumer/orbit/react';
```

Then `<o-progress value={72} shape="rounded" />` is checked like any other element, attributes included.

## Server rendering

Importing Orbit on the server is safe; it does nothing there. It has to run in the browser too, to register the elements and watch the page. In the Next.js App Router, import the stylesheet in `app/layout.tsx` and the runtime in a component marked `'use client'`.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/vue.html

# Vue

In Vue you write Orbit's markup straight into templates. The only setup is telling the compiler that `<o-arc>` and `<o-progress>` are custom elements, not Vue components.

## Install

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

Import the stylesheet and the runtime in your entry file:

```js
// main.js
import '@zumer/orbit/style';
import '@zumer/orbit';

import { createApp } from 'vue';
import App from './App.vue';

createApp(App).mount('#app');
```

Then, in the Vite config:

```js
// vite.config.js
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue({
      template: {
        compilerOptions: {
          isCustomElement: (tag) => tag.startsWith('o-'),
        },
      },
    }),
  ],
});
```

## A gauge

A progress ring with its value in the middle, bound to a ref:

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
import './gauge.css';

const value = ref(72);
</script>

<template>
  <div class="gauge">
    <div class="bigbang">
      <div class="gravity-spot">
        <div class="orbit-10">
          <o-progress :value="value" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
        </div>
        <div class="orbit-0">
          <div class="satellite at-center">
            <div class="capsule">{{ value }}%</div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <input type="range" min="0" max="100" v-model.number="value">
  </div>
</template>
```

```css
/* gauge.css */
.gauge { width: 220px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--o-cyan);
  --o-back-fill: var(--o-cyan-lighter);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; }
```

Satellites rendered with `v-for` are spread around their ring however many there are.

```html
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule">72%</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72" aria-label="Value">
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.gauge { width: 220px; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
const label = document.querySelector('.capsule');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  label.textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

The same markup in plain HTML. Move the slider: changing `value` is all it takes.

Orbit watches the page for added, removed and reordered elements, attribute and style changes, and containers that change size, so a re-render needs no extra call. To wait until arcs are drawn, or to update after a change Orbit cannot see, use the [runtime API](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

## Nuxt

Importing Orbit on the server is safe. Put the stylesheet in `css`, the custom element rule in `vue.compilerOptions`, and the runtime in a client plugin:

```js
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  css: ['@zumer/orbit/style'],
  vue: {
    compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (tag) => tag.startsWith('o-') },
  },
});

// app/plugins/orbit.client.ts
import '@zumer/orbit';
export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {});
```

In Nuxt 3 the plugin is `plugins/orbit.client.ts`, at the root. Nuxt 4 ignores that folder, so there the elements would never be defined.

## Without a build step

With Vue from a CDN, load Orbit's two files with `<link>` and `<script>` (see [Install](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/install.html)) and set the same rule on the app:

```js
const app = Vue.createApp({ data: () => ({ value: 72 }) });
app.config.compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (tag) => tag.startsWith('o-');
app.mount('#app');
```

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/frameworks/svelte.html

# Svelte

Svelte needs no setup for Orbit: custom elements with a dash in their name are passed through as they are. Import the two files and write the markup.

## Install

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

## A gauge

A progress ring with its value in the middle, bound to state (Svelte 5):

```svelte
<script>
  import '@zumer/orbit/style';
  import '@zumer/orbit';
  import './gauge.css';

  let value = $state(72);
</script>

<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress {value} shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center">
          <div class="capsule">{value}%</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" bind:value>
</div>
```

```css
/* gauge.css */
.gauge { width: 220px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--o-cyan);
  --o-back-fill: var(--o-cyan-lighter);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; }
```

In Svelte 4, write `let value = 72` instead of `$state(72)`. The CSS can also live in the component's `<style>`: everything it targets is in the markup, so scoping does not get in the way.

```html
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule">72%</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72" aria-label="Value">
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.gauge { width: 220px; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
const label = document.querySelector('.capsule');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  label.textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

The same markup in plain HTML. Move the slider: changing `value` is all it takes.

Orbit watches the page for added, removed and reordered elements, attribute and style changes, and containers that change size, so a re-render needs no extra call. To wait until arcs are drawn, or to update after a change Orbit cannot see, use the [runtime API](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

## SvelteKit

Importing Orbit during server rendering is safe, so it needs no `onMount` guard. Import the stylesheet and the runtime once in `src/routes/+layout.svelte` and every page can use Orbit.

# Angular

In Angular, Orbit's markup goes into component templates. Two details matter: allow custom elements with `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA`, and bind `value` as an attribute.

## Install

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

Add the stylesheet to the global styles in `angular.json`:

```json
"styles": [
  "node_modules/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.css",
  "src/styles.css"
]
```

Import the runtime once, in `src/main.ts`:

```ts
import '@zumer/orbit';
```

## A gauge

A progress ring with its value in the middle, bound to a signal. `value` works as an attribute and as a property, so `[value]` and `[attr.value]` both redraw the ring. `[attr.value]` also writes it into the server-rendered HTML.

```ts
import { Component, CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-gauge',
  standalone: true,
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  templateUrl: './gauge.component.html',
  styleUrl: './gauge.component.css',
})
export class GaugeComponent {
  value = signal(72);
}
```

```html
<!-- gauge.component.html -->
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress [attr.value]="value()" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center">
          <div class="capsule">{{ value() }}%</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" [value]="value()"
    (input)="value.set(+$any($event.target).value)">
</div>
```

```css
/* gauge.component.css */
.gauge { width: 220px; }
.orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--o-cyan);
  --o-back-fill: var(--o-cyan-lighter);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.capsule { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; }
```

```html
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule">72%</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72" aria-label="Value">
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.gauge { width: 220px; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
const label = document.querySelector('.capsule');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  label.textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

The same markup in plain HTML. Move the slider: changing `value` is all it takes.

Orbit watches the page for added, removed and reordered elements, attribute and style changes, and containers that change size, so bound values and `@for` blocks need no extra call. Importing Orbit during server rendering is safe. To wait until arcs are drawn, use the [runtime API](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/runtime.html).

# Astro

Astro renders Orbit's markup on the server as plain HTML. Import the stylesheet in the frontmatter and the runtime in a `<script>`, which Astro bundles for the browser. No framework island or `client:` directive is needed.

## Install

```sh
npm install @zumer/orbit
```

## A gauge

```astro
---
import '@zumer/orbit/style';
const value = 72;
---

<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value={value} shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center">
          <div class="capsule">{value}%</div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
  import '@zumer/orbit';
</script>

<style>
  .gauge { width: 220px; }
  .gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
  .gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
  .gauge o-progress {
    --o-fill: var(--o-cyan);
    --o-back-fill: var(--o-cyan-lighter);
    --o-stroke: none;
  }
  .gauge .capsule { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; }
</style>
```

To load Orbit from a CDN instead, put the `<link>` and `<script>` from [Install](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/install.html) in your layout's `<head>`, with `is:inline` on the script so Astro leaves it alone.

```html
<div class="gauge">
  <div class="bigbang">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-10">
        <o-progress value="72" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule">72%</div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="72" aria-label="Value">
</div>
```

```css
body {
  height: 100vh;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
}
.gauge { width: 220px; display: grid; gap: 10px; }
.gauge .orbit-10 { --o-size-ratio: 2; }
.gauge .orbit-0 { --o-size-ratio: 12; }
.gauge o-progress {
  --o-fill: var(--accent);
  --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent);
  --o-stroke: none;
}
.gauge .capsule { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 650; letter-spacing: -.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const progress = document.querySelector('o-progress');
const label = document.querySelector('.capsule');
document.querySelector('input').addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  progress.setAttribute('value', e.target.value);
  label.textContent = e.target.value + '%';
});
```

The same markup in plain HTML. Move the slider: changing `value` is all it takes.

Inside a React, Vue or Svelte island, Orbit works as described on those pages.

# Orbit Kit

Ready-made components built on Orbit: gauges, charts, knobs, menus, pickers, clocks, timers, spinners and status rings, one tag each.

[Star Orbit Kit](https://github.com/zumerlab/orbit-kit) [Sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/tinchox5)

```html
<o-gauge value="72" unit="%" size="150px"></o-gauge>
<o-knob value="40" label="Gain" aria-label="Gain" fill="#ffb547" size="150px"></o-knob>
<o-clock live seconds size="150px"></o-clock>
<o-status label="Jobs" size="150px" data='[
  {"label": "Build", "status": "ok"}, {"label": "Test", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "Lint", "status": "warn"}, {"label": "Deploy", "status": "off"}
]'></o-status>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Four components, four tags. Turn the knob, or edit the HTML.

Each component writes the Orbit structure you would write by hand (a `.bigbang`, a `.gravity-spot`, rings, arcs and satellites) into the page, so it scales with its box, takes your CSS and shows up as plain elements in the inspector. When you need something the kit does not do, open the inspector and start from what it built.

## Install

The kit needs Orbit 2 on the page: its stylesheet and its script, which draws the arcs. With npm:

```
npm install @zumer/orbit @zumer/orbit-kit
```

```
import '@zumer/orbit/style'
import '@zumer/orbit'
import '@zumer/orbit-kit'
```

Or in a plain page:

```
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.min.css">
<script defer src="https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit/dist/orbit.min.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/@zumer/orbit-kit/src/orbit-kit.js"></script>
```

The entry registers every component. To load only some, import their files: `import '@zumer/orbit-kit/o-gauge.js'`. Orbit 2 is a peer dependency; the kit does not work with Orbit 1.x.

## Components

- [Gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/gauge.html): One value on an arc.
- [Donut](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/donut.html): A donut chart from an array.
- [Rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/rings.html): Concentric activity rings.
- [Knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html): A rotary control.
- [Menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/menu.html): A radial menu, flat or nested.
- [Instrument](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/instrument.html): Needle gauges with presets.
- [Clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/clock.html): Clocks and watch faces.
- [Compass](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/compass.html): A heading indicator.
- [Radar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar.html): A scope with a sweep and blips.
- [Timer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/timer.html): A countdown ring with controls.
- [Status](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/status.html): Health of many things, in layers.
- [Range](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/range.html): Two handles on one ring: a span of values or hours.
- [Time picker](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/time-picker.html): Pick a time by turning a clock.
- [Spinner](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/spinner.html): Loading rings, dots and orbits.
- [Radar chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar-chart.html): Values across axes, on a web.
- [Sunburst](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/sunburst.html): A tree as nested rings, with zoom.
- [Wheel](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/wheel.html): A prize wheel that spins to a result.
- [Color wheel](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/color-wheel.html): A hue ring color picker.

## What they share

Once you know one component, you know most of the others.

| Attribute | What it does |
| `size` | Width of the widget, as any CSS length. Most are square; `100%` follows the container as it resizes. |
| `thickness` | Band thickness in lanes, Orbit's unit: a lane is a twelfth of the radius. |
| `fill`, `track` | Value and track colors of the band components: gauge, knob and timer. |
| `accent` | The highlight of the dial components: instrument, clock, compass and menu. |
| `label`, `unit` | The text in the middle. |
| `range`, `from` | Arc span and start angle in degrees. Partial ranges center their gap at the bottom. |
| `glow` | A glow in the indicator color; `glow="12"` sets the blur in px. |
| `data`, `items`, `targets`, `zones` | Lists, as JSON in the attribute. |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | The range of a value, read like `<input type="range">`. |
| `format`, `locale` | How numbers are written: percent, currency, units, compact. |
| `theme` | `dark`, `light` or `glass`, or an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. |
| `name` | The knob and the menu are form controls. |

The last four work the same everywhere; [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html) has the details and live examples.

Change an attribute and the component updates. Values only move what moves; a new structure, like a different number of segments, rebuilds the inside.

Colors live in custom properties that inherit, so one rule themes a whole panel:

```
.dashboard {
  --ok-fill: var(--accent);    /* value arcs */
  --ok-track: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 22%, #0c0f13);   /* tracks */
  --ok-accent: #f97316;  /* needles, hands, highlights */
  --ok-text: #e2e8f0;    /* readouts */
  --ok-face: #0b1220;    /* dials */
}
```

Each page lists the properties of its component. Attributes set the same properties on the element itself, so an attribute wins over a rule on a parent.

Text inside a component scales with it: the base font size is a share of the widget (`--ok-font-size`), and readouts are sized in `em`. A 120px gauge and a 400px gauge look the same, only bigger.

Every component has a role and a name that follow its value: gauges and instruments are meters, the knob is a slider, the menu is a menu, the timer is a timer. Write your own `aria-label` and the component keeps it. Decorative motion stops when the system asks for reduced motion.

## Coming from 0.x

Tag names and attributes from 0.x still work. What changed is underneath:

- The kit runs on Orbit 2 and no longer works with 1.x.
- Components are sized by their universe. The outer band touches the edge of the widget, so a gauge looks a little bigger in the same `size`.
- `thickness` sets band thickness. `orbit` and `stroke-width` still work as before.
- `gap` is now a share of the widget width, the same in the donut, the menu and the status ring.
- Colors are custom properties you can set from CSS, and text scales with the widget.
- New: [`<o-timer>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/timer.html) and [`<o-status>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/status.html), `min` on the gauge, `accent` on the compass and the radar.
- `<o-meter>` still ships; [`<o-instrument>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/instrument.html) does all it does and more.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html

# Shared options

Themes, number format, `min`, `max` and `step`, and forms work the same in every kit component that has them.

## Themes

Put `theme="dark"`, `"light"` or `"glass"` on a component, or the class `ok-theme-dark`, `ok-theme-light` or `ok-theme-glass` on a container. Everything inside follows, so one class themes a whole dashboard.

```html
<!-- One class per panel; every component inside takes the theme. -->
<section class="panel ok-theme-dark">
  <o-gauge value="64" unit="%" size="120px"></o-gauge>
  <o-knob value="64" size="96px" aria-label="Dark level"></o-knob>
  <p>Dark</p>
</section>
<section class="panel ok-theme-light">
  <o-gauge value="64" unit="%" size="120px"></o-gauge>
  <o-knob value="64" size="96px" aria-label="Light level"></o-knob>
  <p>Light</p>
</section>
<section class="panel ok-theme-glass">
  <o-gauge value="64" unit="%" size="120px"></o-gauge>
  <o-knob value="64" size="96px" aria-label="Glass level"></o-knob>
  <p>Glass</p>
</section>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; padding: 16px; }
.panel { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 18px 22px 12px; border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--line); }
.panel p { margin: 0; font-size: 13px; color: var(--ok-text); opacity: .7; }
.ok-theme-dark { background: var(--panel); }
.ok-theme-light { background: #f6f7f9; }
.ok-theme-glass { background: linear-gradient(140deg, #6d28d9, #0ea5e9 60%, #14b8a6); }
```

```js
// Each knob drives the gauge in its panel.
for (const panel of document.querySelectorAll('.panel')) {
  const gauge = panel.querySelector('o-gauge');
  panel.querySelector('o-knob').addEventListener('input', (e) => gauge.setAttribute('value', e.detail.value));
}
```

Turn a knob: the gauge next to it follows.

- A theme is a set of the `--ok-*` custom properties, inside `:where()`. It has zero specificity, so any rule of yours wins, and color attributes like `fill` win too.
- Custom properties inherit, so the closest theme wins: a `theme="light"` gauge inside an `ok-theme-dark` panel is light.
- Without a theme, components keep their own defaults.
- Glass makes faces and panels translucent and blurs what is behind them (`backdrop-filter`). It wants a colorful or photographic background.

The properties a theme sets, and what reads them:

| Property | What it colors |
| `--ok-fill`, `--ok-track` | Value arcs and their tracks. |
| `--ok-accent` | Needles, second hands, compass index, menu highlight. |
| `--ok-text` | Readouts, numerals and labels. |
| `--ok-face`, `--ok-bezel`, `--ok-case` | Dials, their rims and the case around them. |
| `--ok-tick`, `--ok-hand` | Minor ticks; hands, major ticks and strong numbers. |
| `--ok-surface` | Panels such as the menu hub and the needle cap. |
| `--ok-focus` | Focus rings. |
| `--ok-backdrop` | The `backdrop-filter` of faces and panels. Set by glass. |

To tweak a theme, set a property next to it:

```
.dashboard { --ok-fill: #ffb547; }   /* beats the theme */
<div class="dashboard ok-theme-dark"> … </div>
```

The menu already had a `theme` attribute for its sector colors. That is now `palette="mono|color"`; `theme="color"` still works and combines with the others, as in `theme="color light"`.

## Number format

`format` picks how numbers are written, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. It reaches the readout, the tick labels and `aria-valuetext`.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <o-instrument id="dial" min="0" max="2000" value="1234.5" ticks="5" minor="4" size="250px"></o-instrument>
  <div class="controls">
    <span id="formats"></span>
    <label>Locale
      <select id="locale">
        <option>en-US</option><option>de-DE</option><option>fr-FR</option><option>ja-JP</option><option>hi-IN</option>
      </select>
    </label>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 14px; align-content: center; }
.controls { justify-content: center; }
#formats { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
button[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
select { font: inherit; background: var(--panel); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; padding: 6px 8px; }
```

```js
const dial = document.getElementById('dial');
// Each button is a set of attributes; "plain" removes them all.
const formats = {
  plain: {},
  decimal: { format: 'decimal', decimals: '1' },
  percent: { format: 'percent' },
  currency: { format: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' },
  unit: { format: 'unit', unit: 'megabyte' },
  compact: { format: 'compact' }
};
const buttons = document.getElementById('formats');
for (const name of Object.keys(formats)) {
  const button = document.createElement('button');
  button.textContent = name;
  button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', name === 'plain');
  button.onclick = () => {
    for (const attr of ['format', 'decimals', 'currency', 'unit']) dial.removeAttribute(attr);
    for (const [attr, value] of Object.entries(formats[name])) dial.setAttribute(attr, value);
    for (const other of buttons.children) other.setAttribute('aria-pressed', other === button);
  };
  buttons.append(button);
}
document.getElementById('locale').onchange = (e) => dial.setAttribute('locale', e.target.value);
```

Switch the format and the locale: the readout and the scale change together.

| Attribute | What it does |
| `format` | `decimal`, `percent`, `currency`, `unit` or `compact` (1.2K, 3.4M). |
| `decimals` | Digits after the decimal point, fixed. Without it, each format uses its usual number. |
| `currency` | ISO code for `format="currency"`, `USD` by default. Setting it alone implies the currency format. |
| `unit` | Text after the number, as before (`unit="%"`). With `format="unit"` it names an Intl unit instead: `kilometer-per-hour`, `celsius`, `megabyte`. |
| `locale` | A language tag like `de-DE`. Without it, the closest `lang` attribute, then the browser's language. |

`percent` shows where the value sits between `min` and `max`: 50 on a 0 to 200 gauge reads 25%. In a donut it is the share of the total. Without any of these attributes, numbers look the way they did in 1.0. A bad currency or unit never breaks the component: it falls back to a plain number.

### A formatter for full control

Set `formatter` to a function and it writes every number. The second argument says where the number goes: `kind` is `value`, `tick` or `aria`, and you get `min`, `max` and `locale`. Its text is used as is, without the unit.

```html
<o-gauge id="time" value="95" max="240" fill="#a78bfa" aria-label="Screen time"></o-gauge>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
// Minutes as "1h 35m" on screen, and in words for screen readers.
document.getElementById('time').formatter = (minutes, { kind }) => {
  const h = Math.floor(minutes / 60), m = Math.round(minutes % 60);
  return kind === 'aria' ? `${h} hours ${m} minutes` : `${h}h ${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}m`;
};
```

## min, max and step

Every component with a value reads `min`, `max` and `step` the way `<input type="range">` does.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <!-- Half-decibel steps from -12 to +12; the readout uses one decimal. -->
  <o-knob id="trim" min="-12" max="12" step="0.5" value="-3" format="decimal" decimals="1" unit=" dB" fill="#ffb547" aria-label="Trim"></o-knob>
  <p class="controls">Screen readers hear <output id="said"></output></p>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 6px; align-content: center; }
.controls { margin: 0; }
```

```js
const trim = document.getElementById('trim'), said = document.getElementById('said');
const show = () => { said.textContent = trim.getAttribute('aria-valuetext'); };
trim.addEventListener('input', show);
customElements.whenDefined('o-knob').then(show);
```

Drag, scroll or use the arrow keys: every value lands on a half step.

- Values are clamped to the range, readouts included. A `max` below `min` becomes `min`.
- `step` snaps values to a grid that starts at `min`. Both ends stay reachable, even when the step does not divide the range. `step="any"` turns snapping off.
- Display components (gauge, meter, instrument) do not snap unless you give them a `step`. The knob steps by 1.
- Keys: arrows move one step, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home and End go to the ends. Without a step they move 1% of the range.
- `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` follow, the last one through the number format.

Rings read `min` and `max` as defaults for each ring, and a ring in `data` can set its own. The radar reads `dist` between them, so blips can be in kilometers. On the rings, `step` was already the space between rings; it keeps that meaning, and `spacing` is its new name.

## Forms

`<o-knob>` and `<o-menu>` are form controls. Give them a `name` and they submit with their form like an `<input>`.

```html
<form id="order" class="stage">
  <div class="row">
    <o-knob name="strength" min="1" max="5" value="3" size="130px" aria-label="Strength"></o-knob>
    <!-- required: the form will not submit until a size is picked. -->
    <o-menu name="size" required label="Size" size="170px" items='[
      {"label":"S","value":"small"},{"label":"M","value":"medium"},{"label":"L","value":"large"}]'></o-menu>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button>Order</button>
    <button type="reset">Reset</button>
    <output id="sent"></output>
  </div>
</form>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 14px; align-content: center; }
.row { display: flex; gap: 28px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }
.controls { justify-content: center; }
```

```js
const form = document.getElementById('order'), sent = document.getElementById('sent');
form.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  sent.textContent = new URLSearchParams(new FormData(form)).toString();
});
form.addEventListener('reset', () => { sent.textContent = ''; });
```

Order without a size and the browser points at the menu. Reset puts the knob back on 3.

| Name | What it does |
| `name` | The field name in the form data. Without it, nothing is sent. |
| `value` | The attribute is the default value: the control starts there and a form reset goes back to it. The property is the current value; setting it fires no event. |
| `disabled` | Out of the tab order, ignores input and is not sent. A disabled `<fieldset>` does the same. `:disabled` works in CSS. |
| `required` | Menu only: the form does not submit until an item is picked. A knob always has a value. |
| `input`, `change` | Events, as on native inputs: `input` on every change by the user, `change` when a gesture ends, on each key press, and on each menu pick. `event.detail.value` has the value. |
| `form`, `labels`, `validity`, `checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()` | The same as on an `<input>`. A `<label for>` names the control. |

The menu submits the `value` of the picked item, as JSON when it is an object. Pages restored with the back button come back with the values they had.

## Which component takes what

| Component | Theme | Format | min / max / step | Form |
| [Gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/gauge.html) | yes | readout | all three | |
| [Knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html) | yes | readout | all three, keys | yes |
| [Menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/menu.html) | yes | | | yes |
| [Instrument](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/instrument.html) | yes | readout, scale | all three | |
| [Donut](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/donut.html) | yes | segments | | |
| [Rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/rings.html) | yes | rings | `min`, `max` | |
| [Compass](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/compass.html) | yes | heading | | |
| [Radar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar.html) | yes | distances | `min`, `max` | |
| [Radar chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar-chart.html) | yes | tooltip, scale, table | `min`, `max`, also per axis | |
| [Spinner](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/spinner.html) | yes | progress readout | `min`, `max` | |
| [Sunburst](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/sunburst.html) | yes | values, middle | | |
| [Range](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/range.html) | yes | readout | all three, keys | yes |
| [Time picker](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/time-picker.html) | yes | | `min`, `max` (times) | yes |
| [Color wheel](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/color-wheel.html) | yes | | | yes |
| [Wheel](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/wheel.html) | yes | | | |
| [Clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/clock.html), [Timer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/timer.html), [Status](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/status.html) | yes | | | |

`<o-meter>` takes the same as the instrument. Clocks and timers show times, not numbers, so they have no number format.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/gauge.html

# Gauge

`<o-gauge>` shows one value on an arc, with a readout in the middle.

```html
<o-gauge value="72" unit="%"></o-gauge>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The arc is a band on `orbit-12`, so it touches the edge of the widget, and the gap of the default 270° range sits at the bottom. Change `value` and only the arc redraws.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | `min` | The current value, kept in range: a value past the end is drawn and shown at the end. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | The range of the value. A `max` below `min` becomes `min`. |
| `step` | none | Snaps the value to a grid that starts at `min`. See [min, max and step](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#range). |
| `range` | `270` | Arc span in degrees: `360` is a full ring, `180` a semicircle. |
| `from` | auto | Start angle, clockwise from the top. By default the gap is centered at the bottom. |
| `label` | | Text in the middle. Without it, the readout is `value` followed by `unit`. |
| `unit` | | Suffix for the value, like `%` or `" km/h"`. With `format="unit"`, an Intl unit such as `kilometer-per-hour`. |
| `fill` | `#6366f1` | Color of the value arc. Sets `--ok-fill`. |
| `track` | `#262d38` | Color of the track behind it. Sets `--ok-track`. |
| `thickness` | `2.4` | Band thickness in lanes. A lane is a twelfth of the radius. |
| `shape` | `rounded` | Ending of the arc: any Orbit shape, such as `none`, `rounded`, `arrow` or `slash`. |
| `size` | `200px` | Width of the widget. Any CSS length; `100%` follows its container. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in the value color. `glow="12"` sets the blur radius in px. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of the readout and `aria-valuetext`, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

Two attributes from 0.x still work: `orbit` sets the thickness the old way, and `stroke-width` draws an outline in the band's own color, in px.

## Styling

Colors are custom properties that inherit, so you can theme every gauge on a page from one rule.

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#6366f1` | Value arc. |
| `--ok-track` | `#262d38` | Track. |
| `--ok-hub-color` | inherits | Color of the readout in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-bg` | `none` | Background of the hole in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-size` | `1.4em` | Font size of the readout. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size, as a share of the widget. Text scales with it. |

```html
<div class="panel">
  <o-gauge value="38" unit="°" label="38°"></o-gauge>
  <o-gauge value="64" unit="%"></o-gauge>
  <o-gauge value="91" unit="%"></o-gauge>
</div>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
.panel { display: contents; --ok-fill: var(--accent); --ok-track: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 22%, #0c0f13); }
.panel o-gauge:last-child { --ok-fill: #ffb547; --ok-track: #3a2112; }
```

One rule themes the group; the last gauge overrides it.

## More examples

### Semicircle with a range

```html
<o-gauge value="1450" min="0" max="2000" range="180" label="1,450 kWh" thickness="3" shape="none" fill="#ffb547" size="240px"></o-gauge>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Full ring with a glow

```html
<o-gauge value="125" max="240" label="125 km/h" range="360" glow fill="#ff7a6b"></o-gauge>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Live value

```html
<o-gauge id="cpu" value="0" unit="%" thickness="1.4" fill="#a3e635"></o-gauge>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const gauge = document.getElementById('cpu');
setInterval(() => {
  gauge.setAttribute('value', Math.round(30 + Math.random() * 60));
}, 1200);
```

## Accessibility

The gauge has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext` kept in sync; `aria-valuetext` uses the number format. Its name is the readout; set `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to give it a better one, and the gauge keeps it. Color is never the only signal: the number is always in the middle unless you replace it with `label`.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/donut.html

# Donut

`<o-donut>` draws a donut chart from a JSON array.

```html
<o-donut label="$2.4k" data='[
  {"value": 52, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Rent"},
  {"value": 28, "color": "#ffb547", "label": "Food"},
  {"value": 20, "color": "#4fd1c5", "label": "Other"}
]'></o-donut>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Each item becomes an `<o-arc>` with a `value`, and Orbit stacks them one after another around the ring. Values are shares of their sum, or of `total` when you want a ring that is not full.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `data` | `[]` | Segments: `[{ value, color?, label? }]`. Without a color, a segment takes the next one of the palette. |
| `total` | the sum | What a full ring is worth. With `total="100"` and values that add up to 70, 30% stays empty. |
| `range` / `from` | `360` / `0` | Arc span and start angle, in degrees. |
| `label` / `unit` | | Text in the middle. |
| `thickness` | `3` | Band thickness in lanes. |
| `gap` | `1.5` | Space between segments, in percent of the widget width. |
| `shape` | `none` | Segment endings. `rounded` gives pill-shaped segments. |
| `track` | faint gray | Color of the ring behind the segments, seen in the gaps and in an empty part. |
| `size` | `200px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in each segment color. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of segment titles and the accessible name; `percent` is the share of the total, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

Change `data` with the same number of items and the arcs are patched in place. A different count rebuilds the ring.

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-track` | `rgba(127,127,127,.12)` | Ring behind the segments. |
| `--ok-hub-color` | inherits | Color of the readout in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-bg` | `none` | Background of the hole in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-size` | `1.4em` | Font size of the readout. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size, as a share of the widget. Text scales with it. |

## More examples

### Rounded segments with wider gaps

```html
<o-donut shape="rounded" gap="4" thickness="2" label="Q3" data='[
  {"value": 40, "color": "#60a5fa"},
  {"value": 25, "color": "#ff7a6b"},
  {"value": 20, "color": "#8a97a5"},
  {"value": 15, "color": "#ffb547"}
]'></o-donut>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### A partial ring

```html
<o-donut total="100" range="270" from="225" label="70%" thickness="2.4" data='[
  {"value": 45, "color": "#a78bfa", "label": "Used"},
  {"value": 25, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Cached"}
]'></o-donut>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

45 + 25 out of a total of 100 leaves the last 30% of the 270° range empty.

### Updating the data

```html
<o-donut id="votes" label="Votes" data='[{"value":1},{"value":1},{"value":1}]'></o-donut>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const donut = document.getElementById('votes');
setInterval(() => {
  const data = [0, 1, 2].map(() => ({ value: 1 + Math.round(Math.random() * 9) }));
  donut.setAttribute('data', JSON.stringify(data));
}, 1500);
```

## Accessibility

The donut has `role="img"` and a name that lists every segment, such as “Rent: 52; Food: 28; Other: 20”. Give items a `label` so the list makes sense; each segment also shows it as a tooltip. Set `aria-label` to replace the generated name. When colors are close, add the numbers somewhere in text as well.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/rings.html

# Rings

`<o-rings>` draws concentric activity rings, outermost first.

```html
<o-rings data='[
  {"value": 80, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Move"},
  {"value": 55, "color": "#a3e635", "label": "Exercise"},
  {"value": 92, "color": "#4fd1c5", "label": "Stand"}
]'></o-rings>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The first ring touches the edge and the others step inward by whole lanes, as many as fit. Each ring is an `<o-progress>` over a track in a dim wash of its own color.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `data` | `[]` | Rings: `[{ value, min?, max?, color?, label? }]`. Values are kept between the ring's `min` and `max`. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | Defaults for every ring that does not set its own. |
| `range` / `from` | `360` / auto | Arc span and start angle. Partial rings center their gap at the bottom. |
| `thickness` | auto | Ring thickness in lanes. By default it fills most of the space between rings. |
| `spacing` | `1` | Multiplies the space between rings. `step` is its old name and still works. |
| `track` | dim ring color | One track color for every ring. |
| `shape` | `rounded` | Ring endings. |
| `label` / `unit` | | Text in the middle. |
| `size` | `200px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in each ring color. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of ring values in titles and the accessible name, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-hub-color` | inherits | Color of the readout in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-bg` | `none` | Background of the hole in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-size` | `1.4em` | Font size of the readout. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size, as a share of the widget. Text scales with it. |

Ring colors come from `data`; `track` overrides the dim tracks.

## More examples

### Half rings with a label

```html
<o-rings range="240" label="3/4" size="240px" data='[
  {"value": 7, "max": 8, "color": "#60a5fa", "label": "Sleep"},
  {"value": 5, "max": 8, "color": "#a78bfa", "label": "Focus"},
  {"value": 2, "max": 8, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Breaks"}
]'></o-rings>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Thin rings, many of them

```html
<o-rings thickness="1.2" shape="none" data='[
  {"value": 90}, {"value": 72}, {"value": 64}, {"value": 41}, {"value": 23}
]'></o-rings>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### A glowing light theme

```html
<o-rings glow="8" track="#e7ecf2" data='[
  {"value": 66, "color": "#ef4565"},
  {"value": 38, "color": "#3da9fc"}
]' label="Today"></o-rings>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The rings have `role="img"` and a name that reads every ring as “Move: 80 of 100”. Labels in `data` make it useful; without them the rings are called Ring 1, Ring 2 and so on. Set `aria-label` to replace it.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html

# Knob

`<o-knob>` is a rotary control you turn with the pointer, the wheel or the keyboard.

```html
<o-knob value="65" unit="%" aria-label="Volume"></o-knob>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Grab the band and turn it, or drag up and down anywhere else on the knob. The track is an `interactive` `<o-arc>` with a `hit-width`, so it takes the pointer along its whole length, a few pixels past its edges too.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | `min` | Starting value, snapped to `step` and kept in range. It is also the default a form reset returns to; the attribute follows the knob as it turns. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | The range. A `max` below `min` becomes `min`. |
| `step` | `1` | Increment for keys and the wheel, and the snapping grid. Decimals work; `any` turns snapping off. |
| `range` / `from` | `270` / auto | Arc span and start angle. |
| `label` | | Text in the middle instead of the value. It is also the default accessible name. |
| `unit` | | Suffix for the value. With `format="unit"`, an Intl unit. |
| `fill` / `track` | `#a1a1aa` / `#27272a` | Value and track colors. |
| `thickness` | `2.4` | Band thickness in lanes. |
| `shape` | `rounded` | Ending of the value arc. |
| `name` | | Field name: with it, the knob submits its value with the form. See [Forms](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#forms). |
| `disabled` | off | Dimmed, out of the tab order and not submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` does the same. Setting `value` from code still works. |
| `size` | `160px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in the value color. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of the readout and `aria-valuetext`, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `value` | Reads or sets the value. Setting it snaps and clamps like the attribute and fires no event, like a native input. |
| `min`, `max`, `step`, `stepUp()`, `stepDown()` | As on `<input type="range">`. |
| `form`, `labels`, `defaultValue`, `validity` | As on a native input. |
| `formatter` | A function that writes the readout and `aria-valuetext`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#formatter). |
| `input` | Fires on every change you make: turning, keys, the wheel. `event.detail.value` has the value. |
| `change` | Fires once a gesture ends with a different value, and on each key press or wheel step. |

```
knob.addEventListener('input', (e) => preview(e.detail.value))
knob.addEventListener('change', (e) => save(e.detail.value))
knob.value = 40
```

The knob is a form control. Inside a `<form>` with a `name`, it submits its value, resets with the form and comes back on page restore:

```
<form>
  <o-knob name="volume" value="30"></o-knob>
</form>
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#a1a1aa` | Value arc. |
| `--ok-track` | `#27272a` | Track. |
| `--ok-focus` | `#3da9fc` | Focus ring. |
| `--ok-hub-color` | inherits | Color of the readout in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-bg` | `none` | Background of the hole in the middle. |
| `--ok-hub-size` | `1.4em` | Font size of the readout. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size, as a share of the widget. Text scales with it. |

## More examples

### A row of knobs with readouts

```html
<o-knob value="40" label="Bass" aria-label="Bass" fill="#ff7a6b"></o-knob>
<o-knob value="55" label="Mid" aria-label="Mid" fill="#ffb547"></o-knob>
<o-knob value="70" label="Treble" aria-label="Treble"></o-knob>
<output id="out">Turn a knob</output>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
output { width: 100%; text-align: center; color: var(--muted); }
```

```js
const out = document.getElementById('out');
document.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  out.textContent = `${e.target.getAttribute('aria-label')}: ${e.detail.value}`;
});
```

### Decimals and a full turn

```html
<o-knob min="0" max="1" step="0.05" value="0.35" range="360" thickness="1.2" shape="none" fill="#a78bfa" aria-label="Mix"></o-knob>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Disabled

```html
<o-knob value="30" disabled aria-label="Locked"></o-knob>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The knob is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuetext` and `aria-disabled`. It is one tab stop. Arrow keys move one step, Page Up and Page Down ten, Home and End go to the ends. The wheel only turns it while it has focus, so scrolling the page never changes a value by accident.

Without a name it is called “Rotary control”, or takes its `label`. Give each knob an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/menu.html

# Menu

`<o-menu>` is a radial menu, flat or nested. Branches open in place or as rings around their parent.

```html
<o-menu label="Edit" items='[
  {"label": "Size", "icon": "🔠", "children": [
    {"label": "Bigger", "value": "size.up"},
    {"label": "Smaller", "value": "size.down"}]},
  {"label": "Format", "icon": "✏️", "children": [
    {"label": "Bold", "value": "fmt.bold"},
    {"label": "Italic", "value": "fmt.italic"}]},
  {"label": "Color", "icon": "🎨", "value": "color"}
]'></o-menu>
<output id="out">Pick something</output>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 12px; height: 100vh; }
output { color: var(--muted); }
```

```js
const out = document.getElementById('out');
document.querySelector('o-menu').addEventListener('select', (e) => {
  out.textContent = `Selected ${e.detail.value}`;
});
```

Each sector is an `interactive` `<o-arc>` with its label drawn along the arc. Click a branch to open it; the middle becomes a back button.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `items` | `[]` | Items: `[{ label, value?, icon?, color?, children? }]`, nested as deep as you like. `value` defaults to the label. |
| `expand` | `drill` | `drill` replaces the ring with the open branch. `concentric` keeps the parent and fans the children out around it. |
| `palette` | `mono` | `mono` draws slate sectors that turn `accent` on hover and focus. `color` gives each item its own color. Before 2.0 this was `theme`, and `theme="color"` still works. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`, like every component ([Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes)). It combines with `color`: `theme="color light"`. |
| `accent` | `#3da9fc` | Highlight color of the `mono` theme. |
| `label` | `MENU` | Text in the middle. |
| `label-color` | `#f8fafc` | Color of the sector labels. |
| `range` / `from` | `360` / auto | Arc span and start angle. A partial menu centers its gap at the bottom. |
| `thickness` | `3.6` | Ring thickness in lanes. |
| `gap` | `1.2` | Space between sectors, in percent of the widget width. |
| `size` | `280px` | Width of the widget. |
| `value` | | Picks the leaf with this value. It is also the default a form reset returns to. |
| `name` | | Field name: with it, the menu submits the picked value with the form. See [Forms](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#forms). |
| `required` | off | The form does not submit until a leaf is picked. |
| `disabled` | off | Dimmed, ignores pointer and keys, and is not submitted. |

`icon` takes an emoji, text, or a small inline SVG. SVG is cleaned down to basic shapes: scripts, links, event handlers and external resources are dropped. An item with an icon shows the icon instead of the curved label and keeps the label as its accessible name. Labels are always text, never HTML.

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `select` | A leaf was chosen. `event.detail` has `value`, `label`, `item` and `path`, the indexes from the root. |
| `navigate` | The open branch changed. `event.detail` has `path` and `depth`. |
| `input`, `change` | Fire with every pick, after `select`, like a `<select>`. Same `detail`. |
| `value` | The value of the last selected leaf. Setting it picks the leaf with that value (or none with `null`) and fires no event. |
| `form`, `labels`, `validity`, `checkValidity()` | As on a native input. |
| `path` | Indexes of the open branches, `[]` at the root. |
| `selectedIndex` | Index of the selected leaf in the visible level, or `-1`. |
| `back()` | Closes the innermost open branch. |
| `reset()` | Goes back to the root. |

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-menu-accent` | `#3da9fc` | Highlight of the `mono` theme and the focus glow. Falls back to `--ok-accent`. |
| `--ok-menu-slate` | `#2b333f` | Sector color of the `mono` theme. |
| `--ok-menu-text` | `#f8fafc` | Labels and the middle text. |
| `--ok-menu-hub` | dark slate | Background of the middle. |
| `--ok-menu-hub-hover` | lighter slate | Background of the middle when it is a back button. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `5cqmin` | Label size, as a share of the widget. |

## More examples

### Concentric branches

```html
<o-menu expand="concentric" label="Insert" items='[
  {"label": "Text", "children": [{"label": "Title"}, {"label": "Body"}]},
  {"label": "Media", "children": [{"label": "Image"}, {"label": "Video"}, {"label": "Audio"}]},
  {"label": "Table"},
  {"label": "Link"}
]'></o-menu>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Open Media: its children fan out over its slice, and the root ring moves inward to make room.

### A colored half menu

```html
<o-menu theme="color" range="180" from="270" label="Go" thickness="4" items='[
  {"label": "Home", "color": "#60a5fa"},
  {"label": "Files", "color": "#4fd1c5"},
  {"label": "Share", "color": "#ffb547"},
  {"label": "Help", "color": "#ff7a6b"}
]'></o-menu>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### SVG icons and a custom accent

```html
<o-menu label="Player" accent="#a3e635" size="220px" items='[
  {"label": "Previous", "icon": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"><path fill=\"currentColor\" d=\"M3 3h2v10H3zM13 3v10L6 8z\"/></svg>"},
  {"label": "Play", "icon": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"><path fill=\"currentColor\" d=\"M4 2.5v11l9-5.5z\"/></svg>"},
  {"label": "Next", "icon": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"><path fill=\"currentColor\" d=\"M11 3h2v10h-2zM3 3v10l7-5z\"/></svg>"},
  {"label": "Stop", "icon": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\"><path fill=\"currentColor\" d=\"M3.5 3.5h9v9h-9z\"/></svg>"}
]'></o-menu>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The menu has `role="menu"` and each sector `role="menuitem"`; branches add `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, and the selected leaf gets `aria-current`. Tab enters the menu once and leaves it on the next Tab. Arrow keys move around the visible items, Home and End jump to the first and last, Enter and Space activate, Escape and Backspace go back one level. Opening a branch moves focus to its first child; going back returns it to the branch.

The menu is called by its `label`; set `aria-label` to name it otherwise.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/instrument.html

# Instrument

`<o-instrument>` is a needle gauge with ticks, a scale, color zones and a digital readout. Presets cover cars, aircraft and computers.

```html
<o-instrument preset="tachometer" value="6.2"></o-instrument>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Ticks are `.vector`s spread over the range with `fit-range`, the scale is a ring of satellites, zones are arcs on the tick ring and the needle is a vector from the center. They all share one `--o-from` and `--o-range`, so they always agree. Changing `value` only turns the needle.

## Presets

`tachometer`, `speedometer`, `fuel`, `temp`, `boost`, `voltmeter`, `airspeed`, `altimeter`, `cpu`, `gpu` and `vu`. A preset is a set of defaults: any attribute you write wins over it.

```html
<o-instrument preset="speedometer" value="88" size="180px"></o-instrument>
<o-instrument preset="airspeed" value="120" size="180px"></o-instrument>
<o-instrument preset="fuel" size="180px"></o-instrument>
<o-instrument preset="voltmeter" size="180px"></o-instrument>
<o-instrument preset="cpu" value="64" case="square" size="180px"></o-instrument>
<o-instrument preset="vu" size="180px"></o-instrument>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `preset` | | One of the presets above. |
| `value` | `min` | The reading, kept in the scale: the needle and the readout stop at its ends. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | Scale range. |
| `range` / `from` | `270` / auto | Sweep and start angle. |
| `ticks` | `7` | Major ticks, each with a scale label. |
| `minor` | `5` | Minor ticks between two majors. |
| `zones` | `[]` | Color bands in value units: `[{ from, to, color }]`. |
| `redline` | | Shorthand for a red zone from this value to `max`. |
| `tick-labels` | numbers | Your own scale labels, as a JSON array: `'["E", "½", "F"]'`. |
| `step` | none | Snaps the reading. See [min, max and step](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#range). |
| `unit` / `label` | | Unit and caption under the readout. With `format="unit"`, `unit` is an Intl unit and the readout writes it. |
| `digital` | on | `digital="false"` hides the number. |
| `case` | auto | `round`, `square`, `rounded` or `bare`. Sweeps of 180° or less default to `bare`: a track band, centered in the box, without a dial. |
| `accent` / `needle-color` | preset | Needle color. `needle-color` wins. |
| `face` / `bezel` / `tick-color` | | Dial background, its rim and the minor ticks. |
| `size` | `240px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow on the needle and the zones. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of the readout, the scale and `aria-valuetext`, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Styling

The attributes above set these properties on the element. Each one falls back to a kit-wide name, so `--ok-accent` on a parent colors every instrument and clock inside it.

| Property | Falls back to | What it does |
| `--ok-inst-accent` | `--ok-accent` | Needle and center cap. |
| `--ok-inst-face` | `--ok-face` | Dial background. |
| `--ok-inst-bezel` | `--ok-bezel` | Dial rim. |
| `--ok-inst-tick` | `--ok-tick` | Minor ticks. |
| `--ok-inst-tick-M` | | Major ticks. |
| `--ok-inst-label` | `--ok-text` | Scale numbers and caption. |
| `--ok-inst-readout-color` | | The digital value. |
| `--ok-inst-track` | `--ok-track` | Track band of a `bare` instrument. |
| `--ok-inst-case-bg` | `--ok-case` | Background of a square or rounded case. |
| `--ok-font-size` | | Base text size, `7.2cqmin` by default. |

## More examples

### Your own scale

```html
<o-instrument min="0" max="100" ticks="6" value="40" unit="%" label="Load"
  zones='[{"from": 70, "to": 85, "color": "#ffb547"}, {"from": 85, "to": 100, "color": "#ff7a6b"}]'
  accent="#60a5fa"></o-instrument>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### A themed panel

```html
<div class="panel">
  <o-instrument preset="boost" value="1.4" size="200px"></o-instrument>
  <o-instrument preset="temp" size="200px" case="bare"></o-instrument>
</div>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
.panel { display: contents; --ok-face: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, #2b2116, #120d08); --ok-bezel: #5b4630; --ok-accent: #fb923c; --ok-text: #f5deb3; }
```

### A moving needle

```html
<o-instrument id="rpm" preset="tachometer" glow></o-instrument>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const rpm = document.getElementById('rpm');
let t = 0;
setInterval(() => {
  t += 0.08;
  rpm.setAttribute('value', (4 + 3.6 * Math.sin(t)).toFixed(1));
}, 250);
```

## Accessibility

An instrument has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`, and a name made of its caption, value and range, like “CPU: 64%; range 0 to 100”. Set `aria-label` to replace it. The needle eases to a new value, except with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/clock.html

# Clock

`<o-clock>` is an analog clock or watch face, live or set to a time.

```html
<o-clock live seconds></o-clock>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The dial is the universe: ticks are vectors on `orbit-11`, numerals are satellites on `orbit-9`, and the hands are vectors on the center orbit, turned with `--o-angle-composite`. Sub-dials are satellites that hold a universe of their own. A live clock only moves its hands; the face is built once.

## Presets

`classic`, `roman`, `minimal`, `chrono` and `smartwatch`. As with instruments, any attribute you write wins over the preset.

```html
<o-clock preset="roman" time="10:08:30" size="150px"></o-clock>
<o-clock preset="minimal" time="10:08:30" size="150px"></o-clock>
<o-clock preset="chrono" time="10:08:30" size="150px"></o-clock>
<o-clock preset="smartwatch" time="10:08:30" size="150px"></o-clock>
```

```css
body { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 28px; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `time` | now | A fixed time, `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`. |
| `live` | off | Follows the real clock, once a second. |
| `smooth` | off | A sweeping second hand, redrawn every frame. Implies `seconds`. |
| `seconds` | off | Shows the second hand. |
| `numerals` | `arabic` | `arabic`, `roman` or `none`. |
| `case` | `round` | `round`, `square`, `rounded` or `rectangle`. |
| `dial` | `round` | `oval` stretches the dial to follow the case; `rings` replaces the hands with three activity rings. |
| `digital` | off | A digital time below the center. |
