| `date` | off | A date window at 3 o'clock. |
| `brand` | | A name above the center. |
| `subdials` | off | Chronograph sub-dials: small seconds, 24 hours and date. They replace `digital` and `date`. |
| `accent` / `hand-color` / `tick-color` | | Second hand and cap, hour and minute hands, minute ticks. |
| `face` / `bezel` / `case-bg` | | Dial background, its rim and the case around it. |
| `hour-color` / `minute-color` / `second-color` | | Ring colors of `dial="rings"`. |
| `size` | `300px` | Width of the widget. A rectangle case is 1.26 times as tall. |
| `glow` | off | A glow on the hands. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Styling

| Property | Falls back to | What it does |
| `--ok-clock-accent` | `--ok-accent` | Second hand, cap, brand. |
| `--ok-clock-hand` | | Hour and minute hands. |
| `--ok-clock-face` | `--ok-face` | Dial background. |
| `--ok-clock-bezel` | `--ok-bezel` | Dial rim. |
| `--ok-clock-case-bg` | `--ok-case` | Case around a non-round dial. |
| `--ok-clock-tick` | `--ok-tick` | Minute ticks. |
| `--ok-clock-tick-h` | | Hour ticks. |
| `--ok-clock-numeral` | `--ok-text` | Numerals and readouts. |
| `--ok-font-size` | | Base text size, `7.5cqmin` by default. |

## More examples

### A tonneau watch

```html
<o-clock case="rectangle" dial="oval" live smooth size="200px" accent="#ffb547"></o-clock>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Activity rings for hours, minutes and seconds

```html
<o-clock dial="rings" live seconds size="220px"></o-clock>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### A light face

```html
<o-clock live seconds numerals="roman" face="#fdfcf8" bezel="#d8d2c4" hand-color="#1f2937" tick-color="#9ca3af" accent="#b91c1c" style="--ok-clock-numeral: #1f2937; --ok-clock-tick-h: #1f2937;"></o-clock>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The clock has `role="img"` and its time as the name, like “10:08:30”. The name follows the time, but a screen reader does not announce each change. Set `aria-label` to give it a fixed name, such as “Time in Tokyo”. The live loop stops while the clock is out of the document.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/compass.html

# Compass

`<o-compass>` is a heading indicator: the card turns so the heading sits under the index at the top.

```html
<o-compass heading="45"></o-compass>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The card is two rings, ticks and cardinal letters, turned by their own `--o-from`. The letters stay upright because capsules do by default. A new `heading` only changes that angle.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `heading` | `0` | Heading in degrees, clockwise from north. |
| `labels` | `N,E,S,W` | Card letters, comma-separated and spread evenly. The first one is colored. |
| `accent` | `#ef4444` | Index and first letter. `fill` still works too. |
| `unit` | `°` | Suffix of the readout. |
| `size` | `220px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow on the index. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of the heading readout, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Styling

| Property | Falls back to | What it does |
| `--ok-cmp-accent` | `--ok-accent` | Index and the first letter. |
| `--ok-cmp-face` | `--ok-face` | Dial background. |
| `--ok-cmp-bezel` | `--ok-bezel` | Dial rim. |
| `--ok-cmp-tick` | `--ok-tick` | Small ticks. |
| `--ok-cmp-tick-M` | | Ticks at the four cardinal points. |
| `--ok-cmp-text` | `--ok-text` | Letters and readout. |
| `--ok-font-size` | | Base text size, `7cqmin` by default. |

## More examples

### Eight points

```html
<o-compass heading="120" labels="N,NE,E,SE,S,SW,W,NW" accent="#60a5fa"></o-compass>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### Following the pointer

```html
<o-compass id="c" size="240px"></o-compass>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const compass = document.getElementById('c');
addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  const angle = Math.atan2(e.clientX - innerWidth / 2, innerHeight / 2 - e.clientY) * 180 / Math.PI;
  compass.setAttribute('heading', Math.round((angle + 360) % 360));
});
```

Move the pointer over the frame.

### A light dial

```html
<o-compass heading="300" style="--ok-face: #f8fafc; --ok-bezel: #cbd5e1; --ok-tick: #94a3b8; --ok-cmp-tick-M: #0f172a; --ok-text: #0f172a;"></o-compass>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The compass has `role="img"` and a name like “Heading 45°, NE”, kept in sync with `heading`. Set `aria-label` to replace it.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar.html

# Radar

`<o-radar>` is a scope with range rings, spokes, a rotating sweep and blips.

```html
<o-radar rings="4" spokes="12" label="Scan" targets='[
  {"angle": 60, "dist": 0.8, "label": "Alpha"},
  {"angle": 200, "dist": 0.45, "label": "Bravo"},
  {"angle": 310, "dist": 0.65, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Unknown"}
]'></o-radar>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Each blip is a satellite on `orbit-12`: `--o-angle-composite` points it and `--o-alignment` pulls it in toward the center. Spokes are vectors from the center, one radius long. Updating `targets` only touches the blips, so the sweep never restarts.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `targets` | `[]` | Blips: `[{ angle, dist, color?, label? }]`. `angle` in degrees clockwise from the top, `dist` from `min` (center) to `max` (edge). |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `1` | The distance range, so blips can be in kilometers or miles. |
| `rings` | `4` | Range rings. |
| `spokes` | `8` | Lines from the center. |
| `sweep` | on | `sweep="false"` hides the beam. |
| `sweep-width` | `110` | Width of the beam, in degrees. |
| `speed` | `4` | Seconds per turn. |
| `color` | `#22d3ee` | Color of the whole scope. `accent` works too. |
| `label` | | Text under the center dot. |
| `size` | `240px` | Width of the widget. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of distances in the accessible name, through `Intl.NumberFormat`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-radar-color` | `#22d3ee` | Rings, spokes, beam, blips and label. |
| `--ok-radar-speed` | `4s` | Duration of one turn of the beam. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `6cqmin` | Label size. |

## More examples

### Moving targets

```html
<o-radar id="r" color="#a3e635" spokes="4" rings="3"></o-radar>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const radar = document.getElementById('r');
const ships = [0, 1, 2, 3].map((i) => ({ angle: i * 90, dist: 0.3 + i * 0.15 }));
setInterval(() => {
  ships.forEach((s, i) => { s.angle = (s.angle + 2 + i) % 360; });
  radar.setAttribute('targets', JSON.stringify(ships));
}, 100);
```

### Narrow, fast beam

```html
<o-radar color="#a78bfa" rings="6" spokes="0" sweep-width="40" speed="1.5" size="220px"></o-radar>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### No sweep, as a static map

```html
<o-radar sweep="false" color="#8a97a5" rings="2" spokes="6" label="Base" targets='[
  {"angle": 60, "dist": 0.8, "label": "Alpha"},
  {"angle": 200, "dist": 0.45, "label": "Bravo"},
  {"angle": 310, "dist": 0.65, "color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Unknown"}
]'></o-radar>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The radar has `role="img"` and a name that lists the targets, like “Scan; Alpha: 60 degrees, 80% distance; …”. Give targets a `label` so the list makes sense. With reduced motion, the beam and the pings stand still.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/timer.html

# Timer

`<o-timer>` is a countdown ring with start, pause and reset.

```html
<o-timer duration="1:30" label="Tea"></o-timer>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The time left is an `<o-progress>` on `orbit-12` that shrinks back toward 12 o'clock. The buttons in the middle are real buttons inside the center capsule. The ring is redrawn in small steps rather than every frame, and the digits change once a second.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `duration` | `60` | Length of the countdown: seconds (`90` or `90s`), `m:ss` or `h:mm:ss`. |
| `remaining` | `duration` | Time left to start from, in the same formats. |
| `running` | off | Present while the timer runs. Add it to start, remove it to pause. |
| `label` | | A caption under the time. It is also part of the accessible name. |
| `warn` | | When the time left drops to this, the ring takes the warning color. |
| `ticks` | `0` | Marks around the inside of the ring, such as `60` or `12`. |
| `controls` | on | `controls="false"` hides the buttons, for a timer you drive from code. |
| `fill` / `track` | `#3da9fc` / faint gray | Ring colors. |
| `thickness` | `1.4` | Ring thickness in lanes. |
| `shape` | `rounded` | Ending of the ring. |
| `size` | `200px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in the ring color. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties, methods and events

| Name | What it does |
| `start()`, `pause()`, `toggle()`, `reset()` | Control the countdown. `start()` after the end starts over. |
| `remaining` | Seconds left. You can set it, also while running. |
| `running` | `true` while counting down. Setting it starts or pauses. |
| `duration` | Length in seconds. Setting it writes the attribute. |
| `start`, `pause`, `reset` | Fire when the state changes. |
| `tick` | Fires each time the shown second changes while running. |
| `done` | Fires once when the time is up. |

The methods exist once the element is defined. A classic script that runs before the kit module can write `running` instead, or wait for `customElements.whenDefined('o-timer')`.

Every event bubbles and carries `remaining` and `duration` in `event.detail`. While it runs, the element has the class `is-running`; near the end `is-warning`, and at zero `is-done`.

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#3da9fc` | Ring and main button. |
| `--ok-track` | faint gray | Track. |
| `--ok-timer-warn` | `#f59e0b` | Ring color in the warning time. |
| `--ok-timer-done` | `#ef4565` | Ring color at zero. |
| `--ok-timer-button` | `--ok-fill` | Background of the start and pause button. |
| `--ok-timer-button-text` | `#0c0f13` | Its icon color. |
| `--ok-timer-button-alt` | translucent gray | Background of the reset button. |
| `--ok-tick` | `currentColor` | Tick marks. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base text size. |

## More examples

### A dial with a warning

```html
<o-timer duration="20" warn="5" ticks="60" label="Plank" size="220px"></o-timer>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

The ring turns amber in the last five seconds.

### Driven from code

```html
<o-timer id="lap" duration="10" running controls="false" thickness="3" shape="none" fill="#a78bfa"></o-timer>
<p id="log">Starting…</p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 100vh; }
p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
```

```js
const timer = document.getElementById('lap');
const log = document.getElementById('log');
timer.addEventListener('tick', (e) => { log.textContent = `${Math.ceil(e.detail.remaining)} s left`; });
timer.addEventListener('done', () => {
  log.textContent = 'Done. Again in 2 s';
  setTimeout(() => timer.start(), 2000);
});
```

### A light pomodoro

```html
<o-timer duration="25:00" label="Focus" fill="#ef4565" track="#fde2e4" style="--ok-timer-button-alt: #f1f5f9;"></o-timer>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The timer has `role="timer"` and a name like “Tea: 1:30 left of 1:30”. The ticking digits are not announced, which is how a timer should behave. When the time is up, a polite live region says so (“Tea: time is up”). The buttons are named Start, Pause, Resume and Reset as the state changes, and work with Enter and Space like any button.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/status.html

# Status

`<o-status>` shows the health of a set of things as colored segments, in layers when they are grouped.

```html
<o-status label="Services" labels data='[
  {"label": "API", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "Web", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "DB", "status": "warn", "note": "slow queries"},
  {"label": "Queue", "status": "error", "note": "backlog 12k"},
  {"label": "CDN", "status": "ok"}
]'></o-status>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Each item is an `<o-arc>` with a `value`, so the segments stack around the ring. The middle counts the problems; point at a segment or focus it and the middle shows that item instead.

## Layers

Items with `children` become an inner ring of groups, each as wide as its children on the outer ring. A group without its own `status` takes the worst one of its children.

```html
<o-status label="Regions" labels pulse size="280px" data='[
  {"label": "EU", "children": [
    {"label": "api", "status": "ok"}, {"label": "web", "status": "ok"}, {"label": "db", "status": "ok"}]},
  {"label": "US", "children": [
    {"label": "api", "status": "ok"}, {"label": "web", "status": "down"}, {"label": "db", "status": "degraded"}]},
  {"label": "Asia", "children": [
    {"label": "api", "status": "ok"}, {"label": "web", "status": "unknown"}]}
]'></o-status>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `data` | `[]` | Items: `[{ label, status, note?, color?, value?, children? }]`, up to three levels deep. |
| `label` | | A title in the middle, above the count. |
| `labels` | off | Writes each label along its segment. Keep labels short: text longer than its arc is cut. |
| `pulse` | off | Error segments pulse, except with reduced motion. |
| `range` / `from` | `360` / auto | Arc span and start angle. |
| `thickness` | `2.4`, `2` with layers | Ring thickness in lanes. |
| `gap` | `0.8` | Space between segments, in percent of the widget width. |
| `shape` | `none` | Segment endings. |
| `size` | `220px` | Width of the widget. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |
| Status | Also accepted | Color |
| `ok` | good, up, healthy, success | `#16a34a` |
| `warn` | warning, degraded | `#d97706` |
| `error` | down, critical, fail, failed, danger | `#dc2626` |
| `info` | maintenance | `#2563eb` |
| `off` | unknown, idle, disabled, anything else | `#475569` |

`note` adds a detail to the item's name and to the middle while it is shown. `color` overrides the status color of one item; `value` is passed back in `select` untouched.

## Events

| Name | What it does |
| `select` | A segment was clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. `event.detail` has `label`, `status`, `note`, `value`, `item` and `path`, the indexes from the top level. |

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-status-ok` | `#16a34a` | OK segments and text. |
| `--ok-status-warn` | `#d97706` | Warnings. |
| `--ok-status-error` | `#dc2626` | Errors. |
| `--ok-status-info` | `#2563eb` | Info. |
| `--ok-status-off` | `#475569` | Off and unknown. |
| `--ok-status-text` | `#fff` | Labels on the segments. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `4.6cqmin` | Label size, as a share of the widget. The middle scales with it. |

## More examples

### Reacting to a selection

```html
<o-status id="s" label="Services" data='[
  {"label": "API", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "Web", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "DB", "status": "warn", "note": "slow queries"},
  {"label": "Queue", "status": "error", "note": "backlog 12k"},
  {"label": "CDN", "status": "ok"}
]'></o-status>
<p id="detail">Click a segment</p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 100vh; }
p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
```

```js
const detail = document.getElementById('detail');
document.getElementById('s').addEventListener('select', (e) => {
  const { label, status, note } = e.detail;
  detail.textContent = `${label} is ${status}${note ? ` (${note})` : ''}`;
});
```

### Many small checks

```html
<o-status id="grid" thickness="1.4" gap="0.5" size="200px"></o-status>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const grid = document.getElementById('grid');
const states = ['ok', 'ok', 'ok', 'ok', 'ok', 'ok', 'warn', 'error', 'off'];
const render = () => grid.setAttribute('data', JSON.stringify(
  Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, i) => ({ label: `Check ${i + 1}`, status: states[Math.floor(Math.random() * states.length)] }))
));
render();
setInterval(render, 2500);
```

### A light, half-ring version

```html
<o-status label="Deploy" labels range="240" size="260px" data='[
  {"label": "Build", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "Test", "status": "ok"},
  {"label": "Stage", "status": "info", "note": "in progress"},
  {"label": "Prod", "status": "off"}
]'></o-status>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The element has `role="group"` and a name that counts each status, like “Services: 1 error, 1 warning, 3 ok”. Each segment is a button named after its item, such as “DB: Warning, slow queries”, so status is never only a color.

The ring is one tab stop. Left and Right move around a ring, Up goes out to the first child of a group, Down comes back in to the group, Home and End jump to the ends, Enter and Space fire `select`.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/range.html

# Range

`<o-range>` is a circular range slider: two handles on one ring pick a start and an end, numbers or times of day.

```html
<o-range mode="time" start="22:30" end="06:45" start-icon="moon" end-icon="bell"
  start-label="Bedtime" end-label="Wake up" label="Sleep" size="320px"></o-range>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Drag a handle, drag the band to move both, or tap the track.

The dial is a whole day, so the band wraps through midnight. The track and the band are two `interactive` `<o-arc>`s on `orbit-12`: the band's ring takes the start as its `--o-from` and the span as its `value`. Each handle is a satellite on the same lane, placed by its angle, and the hours are satellites spread around an inner ring.

## Numbers

Without `mode`, the range is a pair of numbers between `min` and `max` on a 270° arc, and the end never comes before the start. The middle shows the span, formatted like any kit readout.

```html
<o-range start="20" end="80" unit="%" size="260px" aria-label="Comfort zone"></o-range>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `start` / `end` | `22:00` / `06:00`, or a quarter / three quarters of the range | The two values: `HH:MM` in time mode, numbers otherwise. They are also the default a form reset returns to; the attributes follow the handles. |
| `mode` | numbers | `time` makes the dial a 24-hour day, in minutes. |
| `hours` | from the locale | `12` or `24`: how times read, `10:30 PM` or `22:30`. The value is always 24-hour. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | The range of a number dial. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#range). |
| `step` | `1`, or `5` minutes | Snapping grid for handles and keys. `any` turns it off. |
| `wrap` | on for time | A number dial that goes round, like hues or angles: the start can come after the end. |
| `min-span` / `max-span` | one step / the whole dial | Limits for the span, in values (minutes in time mode, or `h:mm`). A handle pushed past a limit carries the other one along. |
| `range` / `from` | `270` / auto | Arc span and start angle of a number dial that does not wrap. |
| `label` | | A caption under the span. It is also the accessible name of the group. |
| `start-label` / `end-label` | `Start` / `End` | Accessible names of the handles. |
| `start-icon` / `end-icon` | | `moon`, `sun`, `bell`, a short text or a small inline SVG. |
| `ticks` | `48` / `40` | Marks around the inside of the band; `0` hides them. |
| `numbers` | `12` / `4` / `5` | Labels on the dial; `0` hides them. |
| `fill` / `track` | `#4fd1c5` / `#1f2630` | Band and track colors. |
| `thickness` | `2.4` | Band thickness in lanes. The handles follow it. |
| `name` | | Field name: the range submits `start-end` with the form. See [Forms](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#forms). |
| `disabled` | off | Dimmed, out of the tab order and not submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` does the same. |
| `size` | `280px` | Width of the widget. |
| `glow` | off | A glow in the band color. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `unit`, `locale` | | Number format of a number dial. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `value` | `"22:30-06:45"` or `"20-80"`. Setting it (also as `[start, end]`) fires no event. |
| `start`, `end` | One end each: `"22:30"` in time mode, a number otherwise. |
| `span` | The distance from start to end, in values (minutes in time mode). Read only. |
| `form`, `labels`, `defaultValue`, `validity` | As on a native input. |
| `formatter` | A function that writes the numbers. It also gets `kind: 'span'` for the readout in the middle. |
| `input` | Fires on every change you make. `event.detail` has `value`, `start`, `end` and `span`. |
| `change` | Fires once a drag ends with a different value, and on each key press. |

```
sleep.addEventListener('change', (e) => save(e.detail.start, e.detail.end))
sleep.value = '23:00-07:00'
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#4fd1c5` | Band, and the icons on the handles. |
| `--ok-track` | `#1f2630` | Track. |
| `--ok-range-handle` | `--ok-surface` | Handle color. |
| `--ok-range-icon` | `--ok-fill` | Icon color. |
| `--ok-tick` | `currentColor` | Dial marks. |
| `--ok-focus` | `#3da9fc` | Focus ring of a handle. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size, as a share of the widget. |

## More examples

### Opening hours with limits

A 24-hour clock with a 15-minute step, at least two hours and at most twelve.

```html
<o-range id="hours" mode="time" hours="24" step="15" min-span="2:00" max-span="12:00"
  start="09:00" end="17:30" start-icon="sun" label="Open" size="280px"></o-range>
<output id="out"></output>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 12px; height: 100vh; }
output { color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const range = document.getElementById('hours'), out = document.getElementById('out');
const show = () => { out.textContent = `Open ${range.start} to ${range.end}`; };
range.addEventListener('input', show);
customElements.whenDefined('o-range').then(show);
```

### Hues that go round

With `wrap`, a number dial is a circle too: here a band of hues from magenta to orange.

```html
<o-range id="hue" wrap min="0" max="360" start="300" end="40" unit="°" ticks="36"
  size="240px" aria-label="Hues"></o-range>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

```js
const hue = document.getElementById('hue');
// Each tick shows its own hue; the band takes the hue in the middle of the span.
const paint = () => {
  hue.querySelectorAll('.ok-range-tick').forEach((tick, i) => {
    tick.style.background = `hsl(${i * 10} 80% 62%)`;
    tick.style.opacity = 1;
  });
  hue.style.setProperty('--ok-fill', `hsl(${(hue.start + hue.span / 2) % 360} 80% 62%)`);
};
hue.addEventListener('input', paint);
customElements.whenDefined('o-range').then(paint);
```

### Light, in a form

```html
<form class="ok-theme-light">
  <o-range name="quiet" mode="time" hours="12" start="21:00" end="07:00" start-icon="moon"
    end-icon="sun" label="Do not disturb" size="240px"></o-range>
  <button type="reset">Reset</button>
  <output></output>
</form>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
form { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 12px; }
output { color: var(--muted); font: 13px var(--mono); }
```

```js
const form = document.querySelector('form'), out = form.querySelector('output');
const show = () => { out.textContent = `quiet=${new FormData(form).get('quiet')}`; };
form.addEventListener('input', show);
form.addEventListener('reset', () => setTimeout(show));
customElements.whenDefined('o-range').then(show);
```

## Accessibility

The range is a `role="group"` named by `label` (or “Time range” / “Range”), with two handles that are each a `role="slider"` and a tab stop, named by `start-label` and `end-label`. Each has `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and an `aria-valuetext` that reads the time or number and the span, like “22:30, span 8 h 15 min”.

Arrow keys move the focused handle one step, Page Up and Page Down ten steps (an hour in time mode), Home and End go to the ends. Shift with an arrow moves both handles. A handle pushed past `min-span` or `max-span` carries the other one, so keys never get stuck.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/time-picker.html

# Time picker

`<o-time-picker>` picks a time by turning a clock: hours first, then minutes.

```html
<o-time-picker value="07:30" label="Alarm" size="280px"></o-time-picker>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Tap or drag an hour; let go and the dial turns to minutes.

The dial is an Orbit universe. Hours and minutes are two rings of twelve satellites on `orbit-10`, and only one shows at a time. The hand is a `.vector` and the knob a satellite on the same ring; both are turned by one registered custom property, so switching from hours to minutes sweeps them round the dial instead of jumping. The fields above are ordinary elements, for reading and for the keyboard.

## 24 hours

With `hours="24"` the dial gets an inner ring for 00 and 13 to 23, like a phone's clock. Without the attribute, the picker follows the hour cycle of the page's language.

```html
<o-time-picker value="18:45" hours="24" size="280px" aria-label="Departure"></o-time-picker>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | empty | The time, `HH:MM` in 24 hours. It is also the default a form reset returns to; the attribute follows the picker. |
| `hours` | from the locale | `12` (with AM and PM) or `24` (with an inner ring). |
| `minute-step` | `1` | Minutes snap to multiples of it; minute labels it cannot reach are dimmed. |
| `min` / `max` | | Earliest and latest time, `HH:MM`. Hours and minutes outside are dimmed and cannot be picked. A `min` after `max` is a window across midnight. |
| `view` | `hours` | `hours` or `minutes`: which ring the dial shows. It follows the picker. |
| `label` | | The accessible name of the group, read with the time. |
| `fill` | `#4fd1c5` | Hand, knob and the active field. |
| `name` | | Field name: the picker submits `HH:MM`, or an empty string. See [Forms](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#forms). |
| `required` | off | The form is invalid until a time is picked. |
| `disabled` | off | Dimmed, out of the tab order and not submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` does the same. |
| `size` | `280px` | Width of the widget; the fields scale with it. |
| `locale` | the page's | Picks the hour cycle when `hours` is not set. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `value` | `"07:30"`, or `""`. Setting it snaps and clamps like the attribute and fires no event. |
| `valueAsNumber` | Minutes after midnight, or `NaN`. |
| `view` | Reads or sets the ring on the dial. |
| `min`, `max` | As the attributes. |
| `form`, `labels`, `defaultValue`, `validity` | As on a native input. |
| `input` | Fires on every change you make. `event.detail.value` has the time. |
| `change` | Fires when you let go of the dial with a different time, and on each key press. |

```
picker.addEventListener('change', (e) => save(e.detail.value))
picker.value = '06:15'
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#4fd1c5` | Hand, knob, pivot and the active field. |
| `--ok-time-face` | `--ok-face`, `#161b22` | The dial face. |
| `--ok-text` | `#e8edf2` | Numbers and fields. |
| `--ok-on-fill` | `#0c0f13` | The number under the knob. |
| `--ok-focus` | `--ok-fill` | Focus ring of the fields and buttons. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size of the dial, as a share of it. |

## More examples

### Office hours in quarter hours

`min`, `max` and `minute-step` together: only 9:00 to 17:30, every fifteen minutes.

```html
<o-time-picker id="meet" hours="24" min="09:00" max="17:30" minute-step="15" value="10:15"
  label="Meeting" size="260px"></o-time-picker>
<output id="out"></output>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 14px; height: 100vh; }
output { color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const meet = document.getElementById('meet'), out = document.getElementById('out');
const show = () => { out.textContent = `Meeting at ${meet.value}`; };
meet.addEventListener('input', show);
customElements.whenDefined('o-time-picker').then(show);
```

### Required, in a form

```html
<form>
  <o-time-picker name="pickup" required hours="12" size="240px" aria-label="Pickup time"></o-time-picker>
  <div class="controls"><button>Book</button><output></output></div>
</form>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
form { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 14px; }
output { font-family: var(--mono); }
```

```js
const form = document.querySelector('form'), out = form.querySelector('output');
form.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  out.textContent = `pickup=${new FormData(form).get('pickup')}`;
});
form.addEventListener('invalid', () => { out.textContent = 'Pick a time first'; }, true);
```

### Light

```html
<o-time-picker theme="light" value="16:20" hours="12" size="260px" aria-label="Reminder"></o-time-picker>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The picker is a `role="group"` whose name says the time. The hours and the minutes are each a `role="spinbutton"` and a tab stop, with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and `aria-valuetext`; AM and PM are toggle buttons with `aria-pressed`. The dial repeats what the fields say, so it is hidden from screen readers.

Up and Down change the focused field: hours round the day, minutes by `minute-step` round the hour, skipping anything outside `min` and `max`. Page Up and Page Down take bigger steps, digits type a value, Left and Right move between fields, and A or P switch the half of the day. Focusing a field turns the dial to it.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/spinner.html

# Spinner

`<o-spinner>` tells people something is loading, in five variants that share one size, speed and color.

```html
<main class="row">
  <figure><o-spinner size="72px"></o-spinner><figcaption>ring</figcaption></figure>
  <figure><o-spinner variant="dots" size="72px"></o-spinner><figcaption>dots</figcaption></figure>
  <figure><o-spinner variant="segments" size="72px"></o-spinner><figcaption>segments</figcaption></figure>
  <figure><o-spinner variant="orbit" size="72px"></o-spinner><figcaption>orbit</figcaption></figure>
  <figure><o-spinner variant="progress" value="64" readout size="72px"></o-spinner><figcaption>progress</figcaption></figure>
</main>
```

```css
.row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; align-content: center; gap: 28px 36px; min-height: 100vh; padding: 16px; }
figure { margin: 0; display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 12px; }
figcaption { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); }
```

ring

Each variant is a small Orbit universe. The ring is two equal `<o-arc>`s turning at two paces, so the arc they draw together stretches and shrinks. Dots are satellites on one ring, segments are vectors, and the orbit variant turns two rings of satellites around a core. All of it moves with CSS, so a spinner runs no script while it turns.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `variant` | `ring` | `ring`, `dots`, `segments`, `orbit` or `progress`. |
| `value` | | With `variant="progress"`, how much is done. Without it the progress ring turns like `ring`; set it and it fills to the value. Remove it to go back. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / `100` | The range of `value`. See [min, max and step](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#range). |
| `readout` | off | Shows the value in the middle of a progress ring: the share done, like `64%`, unless a format is set. |
| `label` | `Loading` | The accessible name: what is loading. |
| `size` | `48px` | Width of the spinner. Everything inside scales with it, from `16px` in a button to a full screen. |
| `speed` | `1` | Seconds per cycle. Each variant keeps its own rhythm around it. |
| `color` | `#4fd1c5` | Arcs, dots and ticks. Sets `--ok-spinner-color`. |
| `track` | faint gray | The ring behind the arcs and the orbit lines. Sets `--ok-spinner-track`. |
| `accent` | `#ffb547` | The small moons of the orbit variant. Sets `--ok-spinner-accent`. |
| `count` | `8` dots, `12` segments, `2` moons | How many dots, ticks or moons. |
| `thickness` | `2`, `1.8` for progress | Ring thickness in lanes. A lane is a twelfth of the radius. |
| `shape` | `rounded` | Ending of the arcs: any Orbit shape. |
| `paused` | off | Stops every animation where it is. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale`, `unit` | | Number format of the readout and `aria-valuetext`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties

| Name | What it does |
| `value` | The progress value, kept in range, or `undefined` while there is none. Setting it writes the attribute; `null` removes it. |
| `formatter` | A function `(value, { kind, min, max }) => string` for the readout and `aria-valuetext`. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |

## Progress

When you know how far along a task is, say so. The progress ring turns while there is no `value` and fills once there is one, gliding from one value to the next.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-spinner id="upload" variant="progress" readout size="150px" label="Uploading photos"></o-spinner>
  <div class="controls">
    <button id="go">Upload</button>
    <span id="status">Waiting</span>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 18px; align-content: center; }
#status { min-width: 9ch; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const upload = document.getElementById('upload');
const status = document.getElementById('status');
document.getElementById('go').addEventListener('click', () => {
  // Preparing: no value yet, so the ring turns.
  upload.value = null;
  status.textContent = 'Preparing';
  let done = 0;
  setTimeout(function step() {
    done = Math.min(100, done + 6 + Math.random() * 14);
    upload.value = Math.round(done);
    status.textContent = done < 100 ? 'Uploading' : 'Done';
    if (done < 100) setTimeout(step, 450);
  }, 1200);
});
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-spinner-color` | `var(--ok-fill, #4fd1c5)` | Arcs, dots, ticks and the orbit planet. |
| `--ok-spinner-track` | `var(--ok-track, rgba(127,127,127,.2))` | Track and orbit lines. |
| `--ok-spinner-accent` | `var(--ok-accent, #ffb547)` | Moons of the orbit variant. |
| `--ok-spinner-speed` | `1s` | Seconds per cycle. |
| `--ok-spinner-weight` | `1` | Thickness of the segment ticks. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `17cqmin` | Size of the readout, as a share of the spinner. |

```html
<main class="row">
  <o-spinner variant="segments" size="64px" class="ios"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner variant="dots" size="64px" count="12" color="#ff7a6b" speed="1.4"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner size="64px" thickness="1" color="#a78bfa" track="transparent"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner variant="orbit" size="64px" color="#60a5fa" accent="#a3e635" count="3"></o-spinner>
</main>
```

```css
.row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 36px; min-height: 100vh; }
/* A gray, thinner set of ticks, like the system spinner on a phone. */
.ios { --ok-spinner-color: var(--text); --ok-spinner-weight: .7; }
```

Each spinner restyled with an attribute or a custom property.

## More examples

### Inside a button

```html
<main class="stage">
  <button id="save" class="save">Save changes</button>
</main>
```

```css
.save { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-width: 156px; justify-content: center; font-size: 15px; padding: 10px 18px; }
.save o-spinner { --ok-spinner-color: currentColor; }
```

```js
const save = document.getElementById('save');
save.addEventListener('click', () => {
  save.disabled = true;
  // The button's own text already says what is going on, so the spinner is hidden from screen readers.
  save.innerHTML = '<o-spinner size="16px" thickness="2.6" aria-hidden="true"></o-spinner>Saving';
  setTimeout(() => { save.textContent = 'Saved'; save.disabled = false; }, 2200);
});
```

### A full-screen loader

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="loader">
    <o-spinner variant="orbit" size="132px" speed="1.4" label="Loading your dashboard"></o-spinner>
    <p>Loading your dashboard</p>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.loader { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 18px; }
.loader p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); }
```

### On a light page

```html
<main class="row ok-theme-light">
  <o-spinner size="56px"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner variant="dots" size="56px"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner variant="segments" size="56px"></o-spinner>
  <o-spinner variant="progress" value="0.35" max="1" format="percent" readout size="56px"></o-spinner>
</main>
```

```css
.row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 36px; min-height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The spinner has `role="progressbar"` and `aria-busy="true"`, named by `label` (“Loading” by default; say what is loading). While there is no value it has no `aria-valuenow`, which is how a progress bar says it does not know how far along it is. With a value it gets `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and an `aria-valuetext` in the number format, and `aria-busy` turns `false` at the end. Set `role="status"` yourself if the spinner should be announced as it appears; the spinner keeps it. It is never a tab stop.

With `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing turns or swells. The arcs, dots, ticks and moons stay in place and breathe slowly in and out, so the page still shows it is working, and a progress ring jumps straight to each new value.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar-chart.html

# Radar chart

`<o-radar-chart>` compares values across several axes, one polygon per series on a shared web.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-radar-chart label="Two players" size="340px"
    data='["Pace", "Shooting", "Passing", "Dribbling", "Defending", "Physical"]'
    series='[
      {"label": "Rivera", "values": [88, 79, 91, 90, 42, 64]},
      {"label": "Okafor", "values": [76, 58, 70, 66, 89, 91]}
    ]'></o-radar-chart>
</main>
```

The web is Orbit: one spoke per axis is a `.vector`, and each level is a ring of `.side`s, chords that close into a regular polygon. The labels are satellites on a ring just outside it, pushed outward with `--o-dir-x` and `--o-dir-y`. The values are an SVG polygon drawn in lanes, because every corner sits at its own distance. Point at a corner, or tab to it, to read its value. Click a name in the legend to hide that series.

Not to be confused with [`<o-radar>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/radar.html), the scope with a sweep and blips.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `data` | `[]` | The axes, clockwise from the top: names (`["Speed", "Range"]`) or `[{ label, max?, min?, value? }]`. Items with a `value` make a single series without `series`. |
| `series` | | `[{ label, values, color?, hidden? }]`, with one value per axis. A missing value sits at the axis minimum; values past the ends are drawn at the ends. |
| `min` / `max` | `0` / auto | The scale every axis shares, unless an axis sets its own. The automatic `max` rounds the largest value up to 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten. |
| `levels` | `4` | Rings of the web, 1 to 12. |
| `grid` | `polygon` | `polygon` or `circle`. Fewer than three axes always draw circles. |
| `scale` | on | Numbers on the levels, along the first axis. Shown only when the axes share a scale; `scale="false"` hides them. |
| `legend` | auto | Shown with two or more series. `legend` forces it, `legend="false"` hides it. |
| `points` | on | `points="false"` draws the polygons without corner points, and without the tooltip. |
| `label` | | The chart's name, for its accessible name and the table caption. Also the name of a series made from `data`. |
| `size` | `320px` | Width of the chart. The legend goes under it. |
| `duration` | `600` | Milliseconds for the shapes to glide to new values. `0` jumps. |
| `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale`, `unit` | | Number format of the tooltip, the scale and the table. `percent` is where a value sits on its axis. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `select` | A point was clicked, or activated with Enter or Space. `event.detail` has `axis`, `series`, `value`, `axisIndex` and `seriesIndex`. |
| `toggle` | The legend hid or showed a series. `event.detail` has `series`, `seriesIndex` and `hidden`. The last visible series cannot be hidden. |
| `hiddenSeries` | The indexes of the series the legend has hidden. |
| `formatter` | A function `(value, { kind, min, max, axis, axisIndex, series, seriesIndex }) => string` for every number the chart prints. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |

## Changing the data

Set `data` or `series` again and each polygon glides from its old shape to the new one. The web, the labels and the legend stay put; only a different number of axes or series rebuilds them.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-radar-chart id="week" label="Workouts" size="300px" max="60" unit=" min"></o-radar-chart>
  <div class="controls">
    <button id="prev">Last week</button>
    <button id="next">This week</button>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 14px; align-content: center; }
```

```js
const days = [
  { label: 'Run', value: 0 }, { label: 'Bike', value: 0 }, { label: 'Swim', value: 0 },
  { label: 'Yoga', value: 0 }, { label: 'Lift', value: 0 }
];
const weeks = { prev: [42, 20, 15, 30, 25], next: [30, 55, 25, 20, 45] };
const chart = document.getElementById('week');
const show = (week) => chart.setAttribute('data',
  JSON.stringify(days.map((d, i) => ({ ...d, value: weeks[week][i] }))));
show('prev');
document.getElementById('prev').addEventListener('click', () => show('prev'));
document.getElementById('next').addEventListener('click', () => show('next'));
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-fill` | `#4fd1c5` | The first series, when it has no `color`. The next ones take amber, coral, violet, blue and lime. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-grid` | `var(--ok-track, rgba(138,151,165,.3))` | Spokes and levels. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-edge` | a little stronger | The outer level. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-fill-opacity` | `.18` | How much the areas are filled. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-stroke` | `2px` | Outline of the areas. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-label` | inherits | Color of the axis labels. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-tip` / `--ok-radar-chart-tip-text` | `var(--ok-surface)` / `var(--ok-text)` | The tooltip. |
| `--ok-radar-chart-legend-size` | `.875em` | Font size of the legend. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `4.1cqmin` | Size of the labels and tooltip, as a share of the chart. |

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-radar-chart class="bold" size="300px" levels="5" grid="circle" scale="false"
    data='["Taste", "Price", "Speed", "Service", "Place"]'
    series='[{"label": "Café", "values": [9, 6, 7, 9, 8], "color": "#ffb547"}]'></o-radar-chart>
</main>
```

```css
/* Round levels, a stronger fill and a thicker outline. */
.bold {
  --ok-radar-chart-fill-opacity: .35;
  --ok-radar-chart-stroke: 3px;
  --ok-radar-chart-grid: rgba(255, 181, 71, .16);
}
```

## More examples

### A scale for each axis

Give an axis its own `max` (and `min`) when the axes measure different things. Each value is then drawn as a share of its own axis, and the level numbers go away because they would mean something different on every spoke.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-radar-chart id="cars" label="Two cars" size="330px" levels="5"
    data='[
      {"label": "Top speed", "max": 250},
      {"label": "Range", "max": 700},
      {"label": "Seats", "max": 7},
      {"label": "Trunk", "max": 600},
      {"label": "Power", "max": 400}
    ]'
    series='[
      {"label": "City EV", "values": [150, 320, 4, 280, 135]},
      {"label": "Tourer", "values": [230, 610, 5, 520, 310]}
    ]'></o-radar-chart>
</main>
```

```js
// One unit per axis, through the shared formatter.
const units = [' km/h', ' km', ' seats', ' l', ' hp'];
const cars = document.getElementById('cars');
cars.formatter = (value, { axisIndex }) => value + units[axisIndex];
```

### Reacting to a point

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-radar-chart id="skills" label="Team skills" size="300px" max="10"
    data='["Design", "Frontend", "Backend", "Data", "Ops", "Writing", "Research"]'
    series='[{"label": "Team", "values": [8, 9, 6, 4, 5, 7, 6]}]'></o-radar-chart>
  <p class="readout"><span id="picked">Click a point</span></p>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 4px; align-content: center; }
```

```js
const picked = document.getElementById('picked');
document.getElementById('skills').addEventListener('select', (e) => {
  const { axis, value } = e.detail;
  picked.textContent = `${axis}: ${value} of 10`;
});
```

### On a light page

```html
<main class="stage ok-theme-light">
  <o-radar-chart size="300px" format="percent"
    data='["North", "East", "South", "West", "Online"]'
    series='[
      {"label": "2025", "values": [62, 48, 71, 55, 80], "color": "#0d9488"},
      {"label": "2026", "values": [70, 66, 69, 61, 92], "color": "#ea580c"}
    ]'></o-radar-chart>
</main>
```

## Accessibility

The chart has `role="figure"` and a name that counts what it holds, like “Two players: 6 axes, 2 series”. Inside it, a visually hidden table lists every value by axis and series, captioned with `label`, so a screen reader can read the numbers in order instead of guessing them from a shape.

The points are one tab stop. Left and Right walk the axes, Up and Down switch series, Home and End jump to the first and last axis, Enter and Space fire `select`, and Escape hides the tooltip. Each point is named after its series, axis and value, such as “Rivera, Passing: 91”. The legend entries are buttons with `aria-pressed`, and a hidden series leaves the keyboard path too. With reduced motion, new data replaces the old shapes at once.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/sunburst.html

# Sunburst

`<o-sunburst>` draws a tree as nested rings: one ring per level, each child inside its parent. Click a branch to zoom in, click the middle to go back.

```html
<o-sunburst label="Week" unit=" h" size="min(380px, 86vw)" data='[
  {"label": "Work", "children": [
    {"label": "Meetings", "value": 12},
    {"label": "Focus", "children": [
      {"label": "Code", "value": 14}, {"label": "Docs", "value": 5}, {"label": "Review", "value": 3}]},
    {"label": "Email", "value": 8}]},
  {"label": "Home", "children": [
    {"label": "Cooking", "value": 8}, {"label": "Chores", "value": 9}, {"label": "Family", "value": 14}]},
  {"label": "Rest", "children": [
    {"label": "Reading", "value": 7},
    {"label": "Sport", "children": [{"label": "Run", "value": 3}, {"label": "Gym", "value": 3}]},
    {"label": "Friends", "value": 10}, {"label": "Screens", "value": 16}]}
]'></o-sunburst>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Point at a slice: its branch lights up and the middle shows where it is and what it is worth.

Every level is a ring of `<o-arc>`s with a `value`. Orbit stacks them in order, and because children come in the same order as their parents, each one lands inside its parent with no angles to compute. A branch that ends early leaves a transparent spacer in the rings outside it, so everything stays lined up.

A node is worth its `value`, or the sum of its children when there is no value or the sum is larger. A value above the sum leaves part of the branch empty in the next ring, which is how you show “the rest”.

## Zoom

Clicking a branch puts it in the middle and spreads its children around the whole circle. The rings move in, the slices outside the branch fold away, and the middle gets a tint of the branch color. Click the middle to go up one level. With `prefers-reduced-motion` the change is instant.

`levels` sets how many rings show at once (4 by default). A deeper tree is still there: zooming in brings the next levels into view.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `data` | `[]` | The tree: `{ label, value?, color?, children? }`, or an array of top-level nodes. Up to eight levels; deeper ones count as part of their parent. |
| `label` | the root's `label` | Name of the whole, shown in the middle and used as the accessible name. |
| `levels` | `4` | Rings shown at once, 1 to 6. |
| `hole` | auto | Radius of the middle, in lanes (a lane is a twelfth of the radius). By default 3.6, or more when there are few rings so they do not get too thick. |
| `gap` | `1` | Space between slices. |
| `from` | `0` | Angle where the first slice starts, in degrees. |
| `labels` | `true` | Names along the slices that have room for them. `labels="false"` turns them off. |
| `size` | `320px` | Width of the widget. |
| `unit`, `format`, `decimals`, `currency`, `locale` | | Number format of the middle and the accessible names. `percent` is the share of the whole tree. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

Top-level branches take the next color of the palette (teal, amber, coral, violet, blue, lime, pink, yellow) and their children lighter shades of it. A `color` on any node replaces its shade, and its children are shaded from it. A label shows only when it fits along its slice and across the band, so small slices stay clean; it reads upright on the lower half.

## Properties, methods and events

| Name | What it does |
| `data` | The tree as an object. Setting it writes the attribute. When the new tree still has the branch you zoomed into, the zoom stays. |
| `path` | Indexes of the branch in the middle, `[]` at the top. |
| `zoom(path)` | Zoom into the branch at `path`, such as `[0, 1]`. |
| `zoomOut()`, `reset()` | Go up one level, or back to the top. |
| `formatter` | A function `(value, context) => string` for every number. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#format). |
| `select` | A slice was clicked, or chosen with Enter or Space. `event.detail` has `label`, `value`, `item` (your object), `path`, `labels` (the names from the top) and `depth`. |
| `navigate` | The branch in the middle changed. `event.detail` has `path` and `depth`. |

Both events bubble. Clicking a branch fires `select` and then zooms; clicking a leaf only selects it.

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-sunburst-tint` | `#fff` | What children are mixed with to get their lighter shade. |
| `--ok-sunburst-label` | `#0c0f13` | Color of the names on the slices. |
| `--ok-sunburst-label-size` | `clamp(10px, 3.3cqmin, 15px)` | Size of those names. |
| `--ok-sunburst-dim` | `.3` | Opacity of the slices outside the lit branch. |
| `--ok-sunburst-muted` | the text color at 62% | The path and the share in the middle. |
| `--ok-text` | inherits | The value in the middle. |
| `--ok-focus` | `#e8edf2` | Outline of the slice in keyboard focus. |
| `--ok-sunburst-value-size` | `23cqmin` | Size of the value in the middle, as a share of the middle. |

While a zoom runs, the element has the class `is-moving` and the names on the slices are hidden.

## More examples

### Following the selection

```html
<main class="stage">
  <o-sunburst id="files" label="Project" format="unit" unit="kilobyte" size="min(320px, 80vw)"></o-sunburst>
  <div class="controls">
    <button id="up" type="button">Up</button>
    <output id="where">Project</output>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { align-content: center; gap: 14px; }
.controls output { min-width: 16ch; font-family: inherit; }
button:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: default; }
```

```js
const files = document.getElementById('files');
const where = document.getElementById('where');
// Folders hold files; sizes in kilobytes.
files.data = [
  { label: 'src', children: [
    { label: 'components', children: [{ label: 'menu.js', value: 18 }, { label: 'knob.js', value: 9 }, { label: 'gauge.js', value: 4 }] },
    { label: 'base.js', value: 26 }, { label: 'index.js', value: 2 }] },
  { label: 'docs', children: [{ label: 'guide.md', value: 21 }, { label: 'api.md', value: 14 }] },
  { label: 'test', children: [{ label: 'unit.mjs', value: 12 }, { label: 'browser.mjs', value: 17 }] }
];
files.addEventListener('select', (e) => { where.textContent = ['Project', ...e.detail.labels].join(' / '); });
files.addEventListener('navigate', () => { document.getElementById('up').disabled = !files.path.length; });
document.getElementById('up').addEventListener('click', () => files.zoomOut());
document.getElementById('up').disabled = true;
```

`select` writes the path under the chart; `navigate` turns the button on when there is somewhere to go back to.

### Two rings at a time

```html
<o-sunburst levels="2" label="Budget" currency="USD" decimals="0" size="min(340px, 86vw)" data='[
  {"label": "Housing", "color": "#60a5fa", "children": [
    {"label": "Rent", "value": 1450},
    {"label": "Utilities", "children": [{"label": "Power", "value": 80}, {"label": "Water", "value": 35}, {"label": "Internet", "value": 60}]}]},
  {"label": "Food", "color": "#a3e635", "children": [
    {"label": "Groceries", "children": [{"label": "Market", "value": 380}, {"label": "Bakery", "value": 60}]},
    {"label": "Eating out", "value": 210}]},
  {"label": "Savings", "color": "#a78bfa", "value": 600},
  {"label": "Other", "color": "#ff7a6b", "value": 900, "children": [
    {"label": "Transport", "value": 160}, {"label": "Health", "value": 120}]}
]'></o-sunburst>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

Utilities and Groceries have a third level: zoom in to see it. “Other” is worth more than its children, so part of it stays empty.

### Percent of the whole

```html
<o-sunburst format="percent" label="Traffic" size="min(300px, 86vw)" hole="4" gap="2" data='[
  {"label": "Search", "children": [{"label": "Google", "value": 41}, {"label": "Bing", "value": 6}, {"label": "Other", "value": 3}]},
  {"label": "Direct", "value": 22},
  {"label": "Social", "children": [{"label": "Mastodon", "value": 9}, {"label": "Reddit", "value": 7}, {"label": "HN", "value": 5}]},
  {"label": "Email", "value": 7}
]'></o-sunburst>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

## Accessibility

The element is one tab stop with `role="tree"`. The drawing is hidden from assistive technology; next to it is a visually hidden list with the same tree, one `treeitem` per node with its level, position and a name like “Focus: 22 h, 52% of Work”. Keyboard focus moves through that list with `aria-activedescendant`, and the focused slice gets an outline and lights its branch.

Left and Right move to the previous and next sibling, Home and End to the first and last. Up goes out to the first child, zooming in when the children are past the outer ring. Down comes back in to the parent, and from the first ring to the middle. Enter or Space chooses a slice (and zooms into a branch), or goes up from the middle; Escape and Backspace go up one level.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/wheel.html

# Wheel

`<o-wheel>` is a prize wheel: it spins, slows down and lands on a result picked by weight.

```html
<o-wheel id="lunch" items='["Pizza", "Tacos", "Sushi", "Ramen", "Curry", "Burgers", "Salad", "Pho"]'></o-wheel>
<p class="readout"><strong id="pick">Lunch?</strong><span>Press Spin, or click the wheel</span></p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 14px; height: 100vh; }
.readout { margin: 0; }
```

```js
const pick = document.getElementById('pick');
const lunch = document.getElementById('lunch');
lunch.addEventListener('spin', () => { pick.textContent = '…'; });
lunch.addEventListener('result', (e) => { pick.textContent = e.detail.label; });
```

The segments are `<o-arc>`s with a `value`, so Orbit stacks them around one ring, each as wide as its weight. The turning part is a universe inside the universe: a nested `.bigbang` that the Web Animations API rotates, so Orbit has nothing to redraw during a spin. The pointer and the button stay in the outer system. Each label is a satellite on its own ring, with `--o-from` at the middle of its segment.

The result is picked first, fairly by weight with `crypto.getRandomValues`, and the wheel then turns a few times and slows down onto it with a long ease-out. Every time a peg passes, the pointer flicks and a `tick` event fires. When it stops, labels on the left half turn over to read upright.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `items` | `[]` | JSON: strings, or `{ label, color?, weight?, value? }`. `weight` (default `1`) sets both the size of the segment and its odds; `0` leaves an item out. Up to 100 items. |
| `labels` | `across` | `across` writes labels from the middle out, `along` writes them along the rim, `none` hides them. Long labels are shortened with an ellipsis. |
| `duration` | `5` | Length of a spin, in seconds (`4`, `4s` or `4000ms`). |
| `turns` | `5` | Full turns before the wheel settles. |
| `remove-winner` | off | For raffles: the winner stays highlighted, then leaves the wheel when the next spin starts. |
| `controls` | on | `controls="false"` hides the Spin button. The wheel itself then becomes the button. |
| `label` | `Spin` | Text of the button. |
| `pegs` | up to 36 items | Dots on the rim at each boundary. `pegs="false"` hides them. |
| `gap` | `0.4` | Space between segments, in percent of the widget width. |
| `disabled` | off | No spins from the button, the pointer, keys or `spin()`. |
| `size` | `300px` | Width of the widget. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

Without a `color`, items take the six accents of the demos in turn, never the same color twice in a row. Label text is dark or white, whichever reads better on its segment.

## Properties, methods and events

| Name | What it does |
| `spin(index?)` | Spins and returns a promise with the result. Without an index the result is random, weighted; with one, the wheel lands on that item. While spinning it returns the same promise. It resolves with `null` when the wheel is empty or disabled. |
| `items` | The items, as given. Setting it writes the attribute. |
| `spinning` | `true` during a spin. |
| `result` | The last result, or `null`. |
| `spin` | A spin started. `event.detail.duration` is its length in seconds. |
| `tick` | A boundary passed the pointer. `event.detail` has the `index` and `label` now under it. Good for a click sound. |
| `result` | The wheel stopped. `event.detail` has `index`, `label`, `value` and `item`. |

```
wheel.addEventListener('result', (e) => claim(e.detail.value))
const { label } = await wheel.spin()
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-wheel-rim` | `--ok-bezel`, `#232b35` | Rim, lines between segments and the button's ring. |
| `--ok-wheel-pointer` | `--ok-hand`, `#e8edf2` | The pointer. |
| `--ok-wheel-peg` | `--ok-hand`, `#e8edf2` | Pegs on the rim. |
| `--ok-wheel-hub` | `--ok-surface`, `#161b22` | The button. |
| `--ok-wheel-hub-text` | `--ok-text`, `#e8edf2` | Text of the button. |
| `--ok-focus` | `#3da9fc` | Focus ring. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base font size of the button, as a share of the widget. |

During a spin the element has the class `is-spinning`; after one, `has-result`, and the winning segment `is-winner` while the others fade.

## More examples

### Labels along the rim, and weights

The jackpot is half as wide as the others, so it comes up half as often.

```html
<o-wheel id="show" labels="along" size="320px" items='[
  {"label": "100"}, {"label": "500"}, {"label": "200"},
  {"label": "Bankrupt", "color": "#222a33"},
  {"label": "300"}, {"label": "Free spin"}, {"label": "Jackpot", "weight": 0.5}
]'></o-wheel>
<p class="controls">Last: <output id="last">none</output></p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 10px; height: 100vh; }
p { margin: 0; }
```

```js
const last = document.getElementById('last');
document.getElementById('show').addEventListener('result', (e) => { last.textContent = e.detail.label; });
```

### A raffle

With `remove-winner` every name can win once. Setting `items` again starts over.

```html
<o-wheel id="raffle" remove-winner duration="4" size="280px"></o-wheel>
<p class="controls">
  <button id="again">Start over</button>
  <span>Winners: <output id="winners">none yet</output></span>
</p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 14px; height: 100vh; }
p { margin: 0; justify-content: center; }
```

```js
const names = ['Ana', 'Ben', 'Chen', 'Dara', 'Eli', 'Femi', 'Gus', 'Hana', 'Iris', 'Jon'];
const raffle = document.getElementById('raffle');
const winners = document.getElementById('winners');
const list = [];
const restart = () => { raffle.items = names; list.length = 0; winners.textContent = 'none yet'; };
raffle.addEventListener('result', (e) => {
  list.push(e.detail.label);
  winners.textContent = list.join(', ');
});
document.getElementById('again').addEventListener('click', restart);
restart();
```

### A result decided elsewhere

When the outcome comes from a server, ask it first and pass the index to `spin()`. Here the buttons stand in for the server, and the wheel is the button itself.

```html
<o-wheel id="prize" controls="false" pegs="false" size="280px" items='[
  {"label": "10% off", "value": "TEN"}, {"label": "Free shipping", "value": "SHIP"},
  {"label": "Try again"}, {"label": "20% off", "value": "TWENTY"},
  {"label": "Try again"}, {"label": "A gift", "value": "GIFT"}
]'></o-wheel>
<p class="controls">
  <button data-index="1">Land on shipping</button>
  <button data-index="5">Land on the gift</button>
</p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 14px; height: 100vh; }
p { margin: 0; }
```

```js
const prize = document.getElementById('prize');
for (const button of document.querySelectorAll('[data-index]')) {
  button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
    const { label, value } = await prize.spin(Number(button.dataset.index));
    button.textContent = value ? `${label}: ${value}` : label;
  });
}
```

## Accessibility

The wheel is a `role="group"` named after its items, with a real button in the middle. Enter or Space on the button spins it. With `controls="false"` the wheel itself is a `role="button"` in the tab order, and Enter or Space spin it. During a spin the button is `aria-disabled` and the wheel `aria-busy`; the result is announced through a polite live region, as “Result: Pizza”.

With reduced motion the spin takes under a second, without extra turns or the flicking pointer. The `result` event and the announcement are the same.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/color-wheel.html

# Color wheel

`<o-color-wheel>` is a color picker: a hue ring around a saturation and brightness square, with optional swatches.

```html
<o-color-wheel id="picker" value="#4fd1c5" aria-label="Accent color"></o-color-wheel>
<p class="readout"><strong id="hex">#4fd1c5</strong><span id="name">teal</span></p>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; align-content: center; gap: 14px; height: 100vh; --accent: #4fd1c5; }
.readout { margin: 0; }
.readout strong { font-family: var(--mono); font-size: 22px; color: var(--accent, var(--text)); }
```

```js
const picker = document.getElementById('picker');
picker.addEventListener('input', (e) => {
  document.getElementById('hex').textContent = e.detail.value;
  document.getElementById('name').textContent = e.detail.name;
  document.body.style.setProperty('--accent', e.detail.value);
});
```

Drag around the ring for the hue, and inside the square for saturation (left to right) and brightness (bottom to top). The hue handle is the only satellite of an `orbit-12` whose `--o-from` is the hue, so Orbit puts it on the ring; the ring and the square sit in center capsules. A gray keeps the hue you had, so turning the saturation back up brings it back.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | What it does |
| `value` | `#4fd1c5` | The color: hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` or a CSS name. It is read as hex. It is also the default a form reset returns to; the attribute follows the picker as you change it. |
| `format` | `hex` | How the color is submitted with a form: `hex` (`#1e90ff`), `rgb` (`rgb(30, 144, 255)`) or `hsl` (`hsl(210, 100%, 56%)`). |
| `swatches` | | JSON: colors, or `{ color, label }`. They go around the outside as satellites, and the picker shrinks to make room. Up to 36. |
| `thickness` | `1.9`, `1.7` with swatches | Hue ring thickness in lanes. |
| `label` | `Color picker` | Accessible name of the group, unless you give it an `aria-label`. |
| `name` | | Field name: with it, the picker submits its color with the form. See [Forms](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#forms). |
| `disabled` | off | Dimmed, out of the tab order and not submitted. A disabled `<fieldset>` does the same. |
| `size` | `240px` | Width of the widget. |
| `theme` | | `dark`, `light` or `glass`. Also inherited from an `ok-theme-*` class on a container. See [Shared options](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/options.html#themes). |

## Properties and events

| Name | What it does |
| `value` | The color as hex. Setting it takes any CSS color and fires no event, like a native input. |
| `rgb`, `hsl` | The color as `rgb()` and `hsl()` text. |
| `colorName` | A plain name, like “dark blue” or “light gray”. |
| `form`, `labels`, `defaultValue`, `validity` | As on a native input. |
| `input` | Fires on every change you make. `event.detail` has `value` (hex), `rgb`, `hsl` and `name`. |
| `change` | Fires once a drag ends with a different color, on each key press and on each swatch you pick. |

```
picker.addEventListener('input', (e) => preview(e.detail.value))
picker.value = 'tomato'
picker.value // '#ff6347'
```

## Styling

| Property | Default | What it does |
| `--ok-cw-thumb-border` | `#fff` | Ring of the handles and of the picked swatch. |
| `--ok-cw-swatch-border` | faint white | Edge of the swatches, so dark ones show on a dark page. |
| `--ok-cw-radius` | `.3em` | Corner radius of the square. |
| `--ok-focus` | `#3da9fc` | Focus ring. |
| `--ok-font-size` | `8cqmin` | Base size, as a share of the widget. The square's handle scales with it. |

## More examples

### Swatches

A palette of your own around the picker. The swatch that matches the color is pressed.

```html
<o-color-wheel id="paint" size="300px" value="#ffb547" swatches='[
  {"color": "#4fd1c5", "label": "Teal"}, {"color": "#ffb547", "label": "Amber"},
  {"color": "#ff7a6b", "label": "Coral"}, {"color": "#a78bfa", "label": "Violet"},
  {"color": "#60a5fa", "label": "Blue"}, {"color": "#a3e635", "label": "Lime"},
  {"color": "#e8edf2", "label": "Snow"}, {"color": "#8a97a5", "label": "Slate"},
  {"color": "#f472b6", "label": "Pink"}, {"color": "#facc15", "label": "Sun"}
]'></o-color-wheel>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
```

### In a form

With a `name` it submits like an input, here as `hsl()`.

```html
<form id="theme">
  <o-color-wheel name="brand" format="hsl" value="#a78bfa" size="220px" aria-label="Brand color"></o-color-wheel>
  <p class="controls">
    <button type="reset">Reset</button>
    <output id="sent"></output>
  </p>
</form>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
form { display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 14px; }
p { margin: 0; }
```

```js
const form = document.getElementById('theme');
const show = () => { document.getElementById('sent').textContent = new FormData(form).get('brand'); };
form.addEventListener('input', show);
form.addEventListener('reset', () => setTimeout(show));
customElements.whenDefined('o-color-wheel').then(show);
```

### A light theme

```html
<o-color-wheel theme="light" value="#0d9488" size="240px" swatches='["#0d9488", "#ea580c", "#2563eb", "#db2777", "#12161c", "#ffffff"]'></o-color-wheel>
```

```css
body { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 100vh; }
o-color-wheel { --ok-cw-swatch-border: rgba(18, 22, 28, .2); }
```

## Accessibility

The picker is a `role="group"` with two sliders, each one tab stop. The hue slider is called “Hue” and reads like “210 degrees, blue”; arrows move it one degree, Shift and Page Up or Page Down ten, Home and End go to the ends, and it wraps around. The square is called “Saturation and brightness”: Left and Right change the saturation, Up and Down the brightness, one percent at a time or ten with Shift. It reads like “Saturation 80%, brightness 60%, dark blue, #1f4c99”.

Swatches are buttons named after their label or their color, with `aria-pressed` on the one that matches. They share one tab stop; arrows move between them and Enter or Space picks one.

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/

# Examples

What you can build with Orbit. The first ones are full pages with live controls; start with the universe model, it shows how size works. The rest are smaller pieces with the code open under them: edit it, or copy the whole page.

For ready-made components, see [Orbit Kit](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/index.html).

## Full pages

- [The universe model](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/00-universe.html): Resize the space and watch the system follow: lanes, reach and size.
- [Playground](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/playground.html): Satellites, stacked arcs and progress shapes with live controls.
- [Progress rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/01-minimal-gauge.html): Three goals, rounded ends, one thickness for all.
- [Donut chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/02-donut-multilayer.html): Stacked values with a hoverable legend.
- [Radial menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/03-radial-menu.html): Six wedges with icons, hover and keyboard.
- [Speedometer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/04-arrow-gauge.html): Ticks, numbers, zones and a needle on one 270° dial.
- [Knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/05-knob.html): Drag, scroll or use the keys; a system inside a satellite.
- [Half gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/06-semicircle.html): A battery in 20 cells on a 2:1 universe.
- [Team map](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/07-satellites.html): Faces on three rings, sized by closeness.
- [Nested systems](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/08-nested-orbits.html): A moon orbiting a planet orbiting a sun.
- [Compass](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/09-compass.html): A card that turns under a fixed mark.
- [Radar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/10-radar.html): A sweeping beam and contacts that flash in time.
- [Depth layers](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/11-depth-layers.html): Composite layers in 3D, with tilt.

## Gauges

- [180° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/180-degree-gauge.html): Five named zones and a needle on a half circle.
- [240° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/240-degree-gauge.html): A stepped speedometer: bands light up with the speed.
- [Fuel gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/fuel-gauge.html): A 90° dial with E, F and a reserve, in a box cut to fit.

## Progress rings

- [Progress with background](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-background.html): A fill over its track, number in the middle.
- [Dashed progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/dashed-circular-progress-bar.html): Ten segments for progress counted in steps.
- [Progress with handle](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-handle.html): A circular slider you can drag.
- [Stacked progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/stacked-circular-progress-bars.html): Three live metrics, labeled in the open quarter.

## Knobs and menus

- [Knob with progress bar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/knob-with-progress-bar.html): A gain knob whose arc grows from the center.
- [LED knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/led-knob.html): Eleven LEDs and a knob that snaps between them.
- [Pie menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/piemenu.html): Wedges that open their options on an outer ring.

## Charts

- [Donut chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/donut-chart.html): Five arcs with values, and two weeks to switch.
- [Pie chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/pie-chart.html): Slices that slide out on hover and focus.
- [Sunburst chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/sunburst-chart.html): Two levels of nested data that line up on their own.

## Watches and clocks

- [Minimalist analog clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/minimalist-analog-clock.html): Ticks, numbers and three hands, on the real time.
- [Chronograph](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/chronograph-watch-face.html): Three sub-dials, each its own system, and a working stopwatch.
- [Roman numeral clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/roman-numeral-clock-face.html): Numerals along the radius, with spin-lock and flip.
- [Smartwatch face](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/smartwatch-face.html): Time and date as curved text along the bezel.
- [Circular timer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/circular_time.html): Turn the wheel to set it; three rings share one angle.

## Calendars

- [Circular year calendar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/circular-year-calendar.html): Seasons, months and days on one dial; step through the year.
- [Chronodex day planner](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/index.html#chronodex): A day as wedges; click one to plan that hour.

## Mandalas

- [Geometric square mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/geometric-square-mandala.html): Nested squares, copied and turned; one to eight folds.
- [Radial symmetry mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/radial-symmetry-mandala.html): Rings of circles with six, eight or twelve folds.
- [Starter patterns](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/index.html#starters): A hexagonal flower and a rosette.

## Interfaces and diagrams

- [Car dashboard](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/dashboard.html): A live clock and two pods, each its own system.
- [Layered status rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/layered-status-rings.html): Channels stacked in depth; alerts come to the front.
- [Sci-fi interface](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/scifi.html): Arcs and dashes at different depths, tilting with the pointer.
- [Abstract orbital map](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/abstract_map.html): Planets that are systems of their own, each ring turning.
- [Chemical structure](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/chemical_structures.html): Caffeine, from sides and satellites.

# Use cases

Where Orbit fits, where it does not, and which examples to start from.

- [Dashboards](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/dashboards.html): Headline numbers, breakdowns and goals.
- [IoT and hardware interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/iot-and-hardware-ui.html): Thermostats, levels and live telemetry.
- [Fitness and health apps](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html): Activity rings and workout readouts.
- [Audio app interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/audio-app-ui.html): Knobs and meters for audio tools.
- [Sci-fi and game interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/sci-fi-game-uis.html): HUDs, menus and decorative geometry.
