# Chronograph watch face

Each sub-dial is a whole clock inside a satellite, with its own center, ticks and hand. Start the stopwatch and three systems run at once.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang watch" role="img" aria-label="Chronograph">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 ticks"></div>
      <!-- Three satellites at 3, 6 and 9 o'clock, six lanes wide.
           Each one holds a system: see the JS tab. -->
      <div class="orbit-5 from-90 range-180 fit-range subdials" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"></div>
      <div class="orbit-3 hand hour" style="--o-size-ratio: 6.6"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-5 hand minute" style="--o-size-ratio: 10.6"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-4 hand chrono" style="--o-size-ratio: 13"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .7"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule pin"></div></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" class="toggle">Start</button>
    <button type="button" class="reset">Reset</button>
    <output class="elapsed" aria-label="Elapsed time">00:00.0</output>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.face { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #1a222c, #0e1318 72%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #26313d; }
.ticks .vector { background: var(--faint); }
.ticks .vector.major { height: 3px; background: var(--text); }
.subdials .face { background: #0b0f14; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line); }
.subdials .ticks .vector { background: var(--muted); }
.subdials .numbers .capsule { font: max(9px, 70cqmin) var(--mono); color: var(--muted); }
.subdials .ticks .vector.major { height: 2px; background: var(--text); }
.hand { rotate: var(--turn, 0deg); }
.hand .vector { height: clamp(2px, 1.4cqmin, 6px); border-radius: 3px; background: var(--text); }
.chrono .vector, .subdials .hand .vector { height: 2px; background: var(--coral); }
.pin { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--coral); }
.elapsed { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const repeat = (count, item) => Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => item(i)).join('');
const ticks = (count, every) => repeat(count, (i) => i % every
  ? '<div class="vector inner-orbit" style="--o-size-ratio: .5"></div>'
  : '<div class="vector inner-orbit major" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.1"></div>');

// A sub-dial: a satellite with its own gravity-spot. Its lanes are twelfths of the satellite.
const subdial = (name, count, every, numbers) => `
  <div class="satellite" aria-hidden="true">
    <div class="gravity-spot ${name}">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 ticks">${ticks(count, every)}</div>
      <div class="orbit-7 numbers" style="--o-size-ratio: 3">
        ${numbers.map((n) => `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">${n}</div></div>`).join('')}
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-4 hand" style="--o-size-ratio: 9"><div class="vector"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>`;

$('.watch > .gravity-spot > .ticks').innerHTML = ticks(60, 5);
$('.subdials').innerHTML =
  subdial('minutes', 30, 5, [30, 10, 20]) +   // 3 o'clock: 30 minutes a turn
  subdial('tenths', 10, 5, []) +              // 6 o'clock: one second a turn
  subdial('seconds', 60, 15, [60, 15, 30, 45]); // 9 o'clock: the running seconds

const turn = (selector, deg) => $(selector).style.setProperty('--turn', `${deg}deg`);

// The time: hours, minutes and the small seconds.
function time() {
  const d = new Date(), s = d.getHours() * 3600 + d.getMinutes() * 60 + d.getSeconds();
  turn('.watch .hour', s / 120);
  turn('.watch .minute', s / 10);
  turn('.seconds .hand', s * 6);
}
time();
setInterval(time, 1000);

// The stopwatch: the big center hand, minutes at 3, tenths at 6.
let elapsed = 0, since = null;
function chrono() {
  const ms = elapsed + (since ? performance.now() - since : 0);
  turn('.chrono', ms / 1000 * 6);
  turn('.minutes .hand', ms / 60000 * 12);
  turn('.tenths .hand', ms / 1000 * 360);
  const m = Math.floor(ms / 60000), s = (ms / 1000) % 60;
  $('.elapsed').value = `${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}:${s.toFixed(1).padStart(4, '0')}`;
  if (since) requestAnimationFrame(chrono);
}
$('.toggle').addEventListener('click', () => {
  if (since) { elapsed += performance.now() - since; since = null; }
  else { since = performance.now(); requestAnimationFrame(chrono); }
  $('.toggle').textContent = since ? 'Stop' : 'Start';
});
$('.reset').addEventListener('click', () => {
  elapsed = 0;
  if (since) since = performance.now();
  chrono();
});
chrono();
```

## How it's built

- The three sub-dials are satellites on `orbit-5`. `from-90 range-180 fit-range` puts the first at three o'clock, the last at nine and one between. See [rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html).
- `--o-size-ratio: 6` on that ring makes each one six lanes wide. The `.gravity-spot` inside a satellite takes the satellite as its universe and starts from the defaults, so the sub-dial uses the same `orbit-11` ticks and `orbit-4` hand as a big clock. See [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html).
- Every hand is one [vector](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html) on a ring turned with `rotate`. The stopwatch only sets an angle per hand, sixty times a second while it runs.
- The JS tab writes the ticks and the sub-dials, so the markup of a sub-dial appears once.

## Related

- [Minimalist analog clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/minimalist-analog-clock.html): the same hands, one system
- [Smartwatch face](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/smartwatch-face.html)
- [Nested systems demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/08-nested-orbits.html)
- [Gravity spot](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html): every system starts from the defaults

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/roman-numeral-clock-face.html

# Roman numeral clock

On a classic Roman dial each numeral stands along the radius, base toward the center, so VI reads upside down. Two capsule classes give it that turn; the button takes them off.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang clock" role="img" aria-label="Clock">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <!-- Railroad minute track: two thin rings with sixty ticks between them. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 rule"></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 shrink-50 rule"></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 ticks"></div>
      <!-- Numerals: spin-lock on the satellite, flip on the capsule. -->
      <div class="orbit-9 numerals" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
      <div class="orbit-3 hand hour" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-5 hand minute" style="--o-size-ratio: 10"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule pin"></div></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" class="toggle" aria-pressed="true">Along the radius</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.face { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #1d2026, #101216 72%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #2c2a26; }
.rule { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 45%, transparent); }
.ticks .vector { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 45%, transparent); }
.ticks .vector:nth-child(5n + 1) { height: 3px; background: var(--amber); }
.numerals .capsule { font-size: 46cqmin; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text); transition: rotate .5s; }
.hand { rotate: var(--turn, 0deg); }
.hand .vector { height: clamp(3px, 1.6cqmin, 7px); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--amber); }
.pin { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const numerals = ['XII', 'I', 'II', 'III', 'IV', 'V', 'VI', 'VII', 'VIII', 'IX', 'X', 'XI'];
$('.numerals').innerHTML = numerals.map((n) =>
  `<div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">${n}</div></div>`).join('');
$('.ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector inner-orbit" style="--o-size-ratio: .5"></div>'.repeat(60);

// Toggle the two classes that turn the numerals.
$('.toggle').addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const on = event.target.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
  event.target.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on);
  event.target.textContent = on ? 'Along the radius' : 'Upright';
  document.querySelectorAll('.numerals .satellite').forEach((s) => s.classList.toggle('spin-lock', on));
  document.querySelectorAll('.numerals .capsule').forEach((c) => c.classList.toggle('flip', on));
});

const clock = $('.clock');
function tick() {
  const d = new Date(), s = d.getHours() * 3600 + d.getMinutes() * 60 + d.getSeconds();
  $('.hour').style.setProperty('--turn', `${s / 120}deg`);
  $('.minute').style.setProperty('--turn', `${s / 10}deg`);
  clock.setAttribute('aria-label', `Clock showing ${d.toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' })}`);
}
tick();
setInterval(tick, 1000);
```

## How it's built

- `spin-lock` on a satellite turns its capsule with its position on the ring, so the text runs along the radius. See [capsules](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/capsule.html).
- `flip` on the capsule adds half a turn, base toward the center. Without it XII would stand on its head at the top.
- The railroad track is two empty rings with a border, `orbit-11` and `orbit-11 shrink-50`, half a lane apart. `shrink-N` on a ring only moves it toward the previous lane.
- Sixty [vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html) hang between them with `inner-orbit`. `:nth-child(5n + 1)` picks the hour marks, starting at the top.

## Variations

A California dial keeps numerals at XII, III, VI and IX and puts plain marks in between. Empty satellites hold the places, so the numerals stay where they belong.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang" role="img" aria-label="California dial">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-9 numerals" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.face { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: #101216; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #2c2a26; }
.numerals .capsule { font-size: 46cqmin; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text); }
.mark { width: 22%; aspect-ratio: 1 / 3; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
const numerals = { 0: 'XII', 3: 'III', 6: 'VI', 9: 'IX' };
document.querySelector('.numerals').innerHTML = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => `
  <div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">${numerals[i] || '<span class="mark"></span>'}</div></div>`).join('');
```

# Smartwatch face

Text written along the bezel: the digital time at the top, the date at the bottom and two complications on the sides, all `<o-arc>` elements that follow the live clock.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang watch" role="img" aria-label="Smartwatch face">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <!-- Curved text: an arc as long as its text (range="auto"), centered on its ring's from. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 from-0 text time"><o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle"></o-arc></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 from-180 text date"><o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle" flip></o-arc></div>
      <!-- Complications: a progress band and its value on each side. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 from-230 range-80 band steps"><o-progress shape="rounded" max="10000"></o-progress></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 from-50 range-80 band battery"><o-progress shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
      <div class="orbit-10 from-270 text value steps"><o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle"></o-arc></div>
      <div class="orbit-10 from-90 text value battery"><o-arc range="auto" text-anchor="middle"></o-arc></div>
      <div class="orbit-9 marks" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"></div>
      <div class="orbit-3 hand hour" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-5 hand minute" style="--o-size-ratio: 9.4"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-4 hand second" style="--o-size-ratio: 11"><div class="vector"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .7"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule pin"></div></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.face { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: #000; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #1d242d; }
.text o-arc { --o-fill: none; }
.time, .date { font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.time { color: var(--text); }
.date { color: var(--muted); }
.band { --o-size-ratio: .5; }
.band o-progress { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: var(--c); --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 18%, transparent); }
.value { font-size: 13px; color: var(--c); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.steps { --c: var(--lime); }
.battery { --c: var(--amber); }
.marks .vector { height: 3px; border-radius: 2px; background: var(--muted); }
.hand { rotate: var(--turn, 0deg); }
.hand .vector { height: clamp(3px, 1.6cqmin, 7px); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--text); }
.second .vector { height: 2px; background: var(--accent); }
.pin { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--accent); }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
$('.marks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector inner-orbit"></div>'.repeat(12);

// Complications. Changing value, or the text of an arc, redraws it.
const steps = 6840, battery = 72;
$('.band.steps o-progress').setAttribute('value', steps);
$('.band.battery o-progress').setAttribute('value', battery);
$('.value.steps o-arc').textContent = `${steps.toLocaleString('en')} steps`;
$('.value.battery o-arc').textContent = `${battery}%`;

const watch = $('.watch');
function tick() {
  const d = new Date(), s = d.getHours() * 3600 + d.getMinutes() * 60 + d.getSeconds();
  $('.hour').style.setProperty('--turn', `${s / 120}deg`);
  $('.minute').style.setProperty('--turn', `${s / 10}deg`);
  $('.second').style.setProperty('--turn', `${s * 6}deg`);
  const time = d.toLocaleTimeString('en', { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' });
  const date = d.toLocaleDateString('en', { weekday: 'short', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' });
  // Only touch the arcs when the text changes.
  if ($('.time o-arc').textContent !== time) {
    $('.time o-arc').textContent = time;
    $('.date o-arc').textContent = date;
    watch.setAttribute('aria-label', `Smartwatch face: ${time}, ${date}, ${steps} steps, battery ${battery}%`);
  }
}
tick();
setInterval(tick, 1000);
```

## How it's built

- Text inside an [`<o-arc>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) is drawn along it. `range="auto"` makes the arc as long as its text and `text-anchor="middle"` centers it on the `from-N` of its ring, so the time stays centered at the top whatever its length.
- `flip` on the date turns the text so it reads left to right at the bottom of the dial.
- The complications are [`<o-progress>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html) bands on an 80° range of `orbit-11`, half a lane thick, with their value as curved text one lane in.
- The script only writes text and attributes. Orbit watches the arcs and redraws them on the next frame.

# Circular timer

A timer you set by turning a wheel. The numbers, the ticks and the time sector are three rings that share one `--o-from`, so changing it turns them as one.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang timer" tabindex="0" role="slider" aria-label="Timer, seconds" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="60" aria-valuenow="15">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 21"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule wheel"></div></div></div>
      <!-- The wheel: every .turn ring gets the same --o-from from the script. -->
      <div class="orbit-5 turn" style="--o-size-ratio: 10"><o-progress class="sector" max="360" value="90"></o-progress></div>
      <div class="orbit-10 turn ticks"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8 turn numbers" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"></div>
      <!-- Fixed parts: the pointer at the top and the readout in the middle. -->
      <div class="orbit-11"><div class="satellite"><div class="capsule pointer"></div></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 7">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout hub"><strong class="left">0:15</strong><span>left</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" class="play">Start</button>
    <button type="button" class="reset">Reset</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.timer { touch-action: none; cursor: grab; user-select: none; }
.timer:focus-visible { outline: none; }
.timer:focus-visible .wheel { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--accent); }
.wheel { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #1a222c, #0e1318 72%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #26313d; }
.sector { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 30%, transparent); }
.ticks .vector { background: var(--faint); }
.ticks .vector.major { height: 2px; background: var(--text); }
.numbers .capsule { font-size: 50cqmin; color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.pointer { width: 70%; aspect-ratio: 1; background: var(--accent); clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 50% 100%); }
.hub { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; place-content: center; background: var(--panel); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--line); }
.hub strong { font-size: clamp(18px, 26cqmin, 40px); }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const timer = $('.timer');

// Twelve numbers along the radius and sixty ticks.
$('.numbers').innerHTML = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) =>
  `<div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="capsule flip">${i * 5}</div></div>`).join('');
$('.ticks').innerHTML = Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) =>
  `<div class="vector inner-orbit ${i % 5 ? '' : 'major'}" style="--o-size-ratio: ${i % 5 ? 0.5 : 1}"></div>`).join('');

// left: degrees of time on the wheel, 6 per second, so a full turn is a minute.
let left = 90, running = null;
function render() {
  const from = (360 - left) % 360;
  document.querySelectorAll('.turn').forEach((ring) => ring.style.setProperty('--o-from', `${from}deg`));
  $('.sector').setAttribute('value', left);
  const s = Math.ceil(left / 6);
  $('.left').textContent = `0:${String(s).padStart(2, '0')}`;
  timer.setAttribute('aria-valuenow', s);
  $('.play').textContent = running ? 'Pause' : 'Start';
}
const set = (deg) => { left = Math.max(0, Math.min(359, Math.round(deg))); render(); };
const stop = () => { clearInterval(running); running = null; render(); };
function start() {
  if (!left) return;
  running = setInterval(() => { left -= 1; if (left <= 0) { left = 0; stop(); } else render(); }, 1000 / 6);
  render();
}
$('.play').addEventListener('click', () => (running ? stop() : start()));
$('.reset').addEventListener('click', () => { stop(); set(0); });

// Drag: the wheel follows the change in the pointer's angle around the center.
const angle = (e) => {
  const r = timer.getBoundingClientRect();
  return Math.atan2(e.clientY - r.top - r.height / 2, e.clientX - r.left - r.width / 2) * 180 / Math.PI;
};
let grab = null;
timer.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => { stop(); timer.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); grab = { at: angle(e), left }; });
timer.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  if (!grab) return;
  const turned = ((angle(e) - grab.at + 540) % 360) - 180;
  set(grab.left - turned);
  grab = { at: angle(e), left };
});
timer.addEventListener('pointerup', () => { grab = null; });

// Keys: arrows for a second, Page Up and Down for ten.
timer.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  const step = { ArrowUp: 1, ArrowRight: 1, ArrowDown: -1, ArrowLeft: -1, PageUp: 10, PageDown: -10 }[e.key];
  if (step) { e.preventDefault(); stop(); set(left + step * 6); }
  if (e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); running ? stop() : start(); }
});
render();
```

## How it's built

- The numbers, the ticks and the sector are on three rings with the class `turn`. The script sets one `--o-from` on all three, and Orbit places their children from that angle. See [rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/orbit.html).
- The sector is an [`<o-progress max="360">`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html) whose `value` is the angle set. On `orbit-5` with `--o-size-ratio: 10` the band reaches from the center to lane 10.
- The numbers stand along the radius with `spin-lock` on the satellite and `flip` on the capsule.
- The pointer and the readout are on rings that never get the new `--o-from`, so they stay put.
- The whole universe is the slider: drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Space starts and pauses.

After a [SwiftUI original](https://github.com/harfyzz/CircularTimer). Thanks to [Andriy Tyurnikov](https://github.com/andriytyurnikov), who proposed the challenge.

- [Watches and clocks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/index.html)
- [Progress with handle](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-handle.html)
- [Knob demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/05-knob.html): another dial you drag
- [Orbit Kit timer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/timer.html)

# Circular year calendar

A year on one dial: seasons, months and the days of the month on three rings. Step through the days and the day ring re-spaces itself for 28, 30 or 31 days.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang calendar" role="group" aria-label="Year calendar">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"><div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule face"></div></div></div>
      <!-- Days of the month: one satellite per day, spaced by Orbit. -->
      <div class="orbit-11 days" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.3"></div>
      <!-- How far into the year: a thin progress band. -->
      <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: .3"><o-progress class="year" max="365"></o-progress></div>
      <!-- Twelve months: arcs without value share the ring. -->
      <div class="orbit-9 months" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"></div>
      <!-- Seasons start on 21 December: 350° on a ring where January starts at 0°. -->
      <div class="orbit-7 from-350 seasons" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.4">
        <o-arc class="winter">Winter</o-arc>
        <o-arc class="spring" flip>Spring</o-arc>
        <o-arc class="summer" flip>Summer</o-arc>
        <o-arc class="autumn">Autumn</o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 9">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout" aria-live="polite"><strong class="date"></strong><span class="weekday"></span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" data-step="-1" aria-label="Previous day">‹</button>
    <button type="button" data-step="0">Today</button>
    <button type="button" data-step="1" aria-label="Next day">›</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.face { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #1a222c, #0e1318 72%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px #26313d; }
.days .capsule { width: 70%; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; place-content: center; font-size: 55cqmin; color: var(--muted); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.days .today .capsule { background: var(--accent); color: var(--bg); font-weight: 650; }
.year { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: var(--accent); --o-back-fill: var(--line); }
.months o-arc { --o-fill: transparent; --o-stroke: none; color: var(--muted); font-size: 13px; }
.months o-arc.current { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, transparent); color: var(--text); }
.seasons o-arc { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 16%, transparent); color: var(--c); font-size: 12px; }
.winter { --c: var(--blue); }
.spring { --c: var(--lime); }
.summer { --c: var(--amber); }
.autumn { --c: var(--coral); }
.readout strong { font-size: clamp(18px, 20cqmin, 36px); }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const names = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
// Labels in the lower half (April to September) are flipped to read left to right.
$('.months').innerHTML = names.map((m, i) => `<o-arc ${i >= 3 && i <= 8 ? 'flip' : ''}>${m}</o-arc>`).join('');

let day = new Date();
function show() {
  const y = day.getFullYear(), m = day.getMonth(), d = day.getDate();
  const length = new Date(y, m + 1, 0).getDate();
  // Rewrite the day ring only when the month changes; Orbit spreads 28 to 31 days evenly.
  const days = $('.days');
  if (days.children.length !== length || days.dataset.month !== `${y}-${m}`) {
    days.dataset.month = `${y}-${m}`;
    days.innerHTML = Array.from({ length }, (_, i) => `<div class="satellite"><div class="capsule">${i + 1}</div></div>`).join('');
  }
  [...days.children].forEach((s, i) => s.classList.toggle('today', i + 1 === d));
  [...$('.months').children].forEach((arc, i) => arc.classList.toggle('current', i === m));
  const dayOfYear = Math.round((new Date(y, m, d) - new Date(y, 0, 1)) / 864e5) + 1;
  $('.year').setAttribute('value', dayOfYear);
  $('.date').textContent = `${d} ${names[m]}`;
  $('.weekday').textContent = `${day.toLocaleDateString('en', { weekday: 'long' })}, ${y}`;
}
document.querySelectorAll('[data-step]').forEach((button) => button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const step = Number(button.dataset.step);
  day = step ? new Date(day.getFullYear(), day.getMonth(), day.getDate() + step) : new Date();
  show();
}));
show();
```

## How it's built

- The days are satellites on `orbit-11`. The script writes as many as the month has, and Orbit spaces them evenly, so the ring is always full. See [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html).
- Months and seasons are [`<o-arc>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) elements without a `value`: sibling arcs share their ring equally. Text inside an arc is drawn along it, and `flip` keeps the lower half readable.
- `from-350` turns the season ring so winter starts on 21 December, ten days before January.
- The thin band between the months and the days is an [`<o-progress max="365">`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html) set to the day of the year.

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/

# Calendars

Time goes around, so a circle suits it: a year as a dial of months, a day as wedges of hours.

- [Circular year calendar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/circular-year-calendar.html): Seasons, months and days on one dial; step through the year.
- [Chronodex day planner](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/index.html#chronodex): A day as wedges; click one to plan that hour.

## Chronodex day planner

A Chronodex is a radial day planner from paper journaling: each hour is a wedge, and you fill the wedge to plan that hour. Here every wedge is an `<o-arc>` you can click.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang planner" role="group" aria-label="Day planner">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- Twelve hours, 10am to 9pm. Each wedge starts on lane 4 and grows outward. -->
      <div class="orbit-4 hours"></div>
      <!-- The morning, 7am to 9am, on an inner quarter. -->
      <div class="orbit-1 from-210 range-90 morning"></div>
      <!-- Hour labels just past the tip of their wedge: see the JS tab. -->
      <div class="labels"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="controls"><output class="count"></output></p>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 4px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 64px); }
.controls { margin: 0; }
.planner o-arc { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 7%, transparent); --o-gap: 2; }
.planner o-arc:hover { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text) 14%, transparent); }
.planner o-arc[aria-pressed="true"] { --o-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 70%, transparent); }
.planner o-arc:focus-visible { outline: none; --o-stroke: var(--accent); --o-stroke-width: 2; }
.label { pointer-events: none; }
.label .capsule { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.morning-label .capsule { font-size: 11px; }
```

```js
const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const hourName = (h) => `${h % 12 || 12}${h < 12 ? 'am' : 'pm'}`;
const wedge = (h, lanes) => `<o-arc interactive tabindex="0" role="button" aria-label="${hourName(h)}" aria-pressed="false"
  class="outer-orbit" style="--o-size-ratio: ${lanes}" data-hour="${h}"></o-arc>`;

// Wedge k covers the hour from k to k+1 on the clock face. Thickness cycles 3, 4, 5 lanes.
const outer = Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, k) => (k >= 10 ? k : k + 12));
$('.hours').innerHTML = outer.map((h, k) => wedge(h, 3 + (k % 3))).join('');
$('.morning').innerHTML = [7, 8, 9].map((h) => wedge(h, 3)).join('');

// One ring of labels per thickness, centered on the wedges (from 15° + 30° per step).
$('.labels').outerHTML = [0, 1, 2].map((t) => `
  <div class="orbit-${8 + t} from-${15 + 30 * t}" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6">
    ${[0, 3, 6, 9].map((k) => `<div class="satellite label"><div class="capsule">${hourName(outer[k + t])}</div></div>`).join('')}
  </div>`).join('') + `
  <div class="orbit-3 shrink-50 from-225 range-60 fit-range morning-label" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.2">
    ${[7, 8, 9].map((h) => `<div class="satellite label"><div class="capsule">${h}</div></div>`).join('')}
  </div>`;

// Click, Enter or Space to plan an hour.
const count = () => { $('.count').value = `${document.querySelectorAll('[aria-pressed="true"]').length} hours planned`; };
const toggle = (arc) => { arc.setAttribute('aria-pressed', arc.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true'); count(); };
document.querySelectorAll('.planner o-arc').forEach((arc) => {
  arc.addEventListener('click', () => toggle(arc));
  arc.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); toggle(arc); } });
});
[8, 13, 14, 18].forEach((h) => toggle($(`[data-hour="${h}"]`)));
```

### How it's built

- Twelve [`<o-arc>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) elements without a `value` share `orbit-4`, 30° each. `outer-orbit` makes every wedge start on the ring and grow outward, and its own `--o-size-ratio` sets how far: 3, 4 or 5 lanes.
- The morning is three more arcs on `orbit-1`, three lanes long, limited to a quarter with `from-210 range-90`.
- `interactive` makes an arc take clicks; `role="button"`, `tabindex` and `aria-pressed` make it a toggle for the keyboard and screen readers.
- The labels are satellites on three rings, one per wedge length, each turned with `from-N` to the middle of its wedges.

- [Watches and clocks](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/index.html)
- [Radial menu demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/03-radial-menu.html): arcs that respond to hover and keys
- [Arcs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html)

# Geometric square mandala

One pattern of nested squares, copied and turned. The copies sit on one ring, and Orbit spreads them over a quarter turn: pick the number of folds and the angles follow.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang mandala" role="img" aria-label="Square mandala">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- The copies: centered satellites on one ring. range-90 spreads their angles over 90°. -->
      <div class="orbit-0 range-90 folds" style="--o-size-ratio: 24"></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: .6"><div class="satellite at-center dot"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls" role="group" aria-label="Folds">
    <span>Folds</span>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">1</button>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">2</button>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">4</button>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">8</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.square { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 75%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--c) 4%, transparent); }
.outer { --c: var(--violet); }
.inner { --c: var(--accent); }
.diamond { --c: var(--amber); }
.dot { background: var(--amber); }
.controls button[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
```

```js
// One copy of the pattern: a satellite as big as the universe, with its own system inside.
// spin-lock turns a satellite, and everything in it, by its angle on the ring.
const pattern = `
  <div class="satellite at-center spin-lock">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center box square outer" style="--o-size-ratio: 15"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center box square outer" style="--o-size-ratio: 11"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center box square inner" style="--o-size-ratio: 7"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center box square diamond spin-lock angle-45" style="--o-size-ratio: 7"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center box square inner spin-lock angle-45" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.4"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>`;

const mandala = document.querySelector('.mandala');
const buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.controls button');
function folds(n) {
  document.querySelector('.folds').innerHTML = pattern.repeat(n);
  mandala.setAttribute('aria-label', `Square mandala, ${n} ${n === 1 ? 'fold' : 'folds'}`);
  buttons.forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.textContent === String(n)));
}
buttons.forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => folds(Number(b.textContent))));
folds(4);
```

## How it's built

- Each copy is an `at-center` satellite with `--o-size-ratio: 24`, as wide as the universe. The `.gravity-spot` inside it has the same lanes as the main system. See [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html).
- All copies sit on one `orbit-0` with `range-90`. Orbit gives each one an angle, 90° divided by the number of copies, and `spin-lock` turns the copy by that angle.
- A square is a satellite with the `box` class. `at-center` keeps it on the center, so only `--o-size-ratio` sets its size, in lanes.
- The diamonds are squares with `spin-lock angle-45`: the same turn, for a single satellite.

- [Radial symmetry mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/radial-symmetry-mandala.html)
- [Starter patterns](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/index.html#starters)
- [Chemical structure](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/chemical_structures.html): systems inside satellites again
- [Capsules](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/capsule.html): `spin-lock`

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/radial-symmetry-mandala.html

# Radial symmetry mandala

Symmetry for free: put copies of a satellite on a ring and Orbit spaces them evenly. Change the number of copies and the whole pattern redraws with six, eight or twelve folds.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang mandala" role="img" aria-label="Mandala">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- Three rings of copies, written by the JS tab, and a target in the middle. -->
      <div class="orbit-8 triangles" style="--o-size-ratio: 8"></div>
      <div class="orbit-8 stacks" style="--o-size-ratio: 6"></div>
      <div class="orbit-4 stacks small" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.8"></div>
      <div class="orbit-0">
        <div class="satellite at-center circle" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.2"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center circle" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center circle" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"></div>
        <div class="satellite at-center dot" style="--o-size-ratio: .6"></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls" role="group" aria-label="Symmetry">
    <span>Folds</span>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">6</button>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">8</button>
    <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">12</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 12px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 84px); }
.circle { border: 1px solid var(--c, var(--accent)); background: var(--panel); }
.stacks .circle:nth-child(even) { --c: var(--violet); }
.triangles .side { background: var(--amber); }
.dot { background: var(--amber); }
.controls button[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); }
```

```js
// A copy: a satellite with its own system inside, so its circles are counted in its own lanes.
const stack = (sizes) => `
  <div class="satellite"><div class="gravity-spot"><div class="orbit-0">
    ${sizes.map((s) => `<div class="satellite at-center circle" style="--o-size-ratio: ${s}"></div>`).join('')}
  </div></div></div>`;
// A triangle: three sides on the outer ring of a nested system. spin-lock turns it with its place.
const triangle = `
  <div class="satellite spin-lock"><div class="gravity-spot"><div class="orbit-12">
    <div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div><div class="side"></div>
  </div></div></div>`;

const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
const buttons = document.querySelectorAll('.controls button');
function folds(n) {
  $('.stacks').innerHTML = stack([24, 18, 12, 6]).repeat(n);
  $('.stacks.small').innerHTML = stack([24, 14]).repeat(n);
  $('.triangles').innerHTML = triangle.repeat(n);
  // Half a step round, so the triangles show between the stacks.
  $('.triangles').style.setProperty('--o-from', `${180 / n}deg`);
  $('.mandala').setAttribute('aria-label', `Mandala with ${n}-fold symmetry`);
  buttons.forEach((b) => b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', b.textContent === String(n)));
}
buttons.forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => folds(Number(b.textContent))));
folds(8);
```

## How it's built

- Copies of a satellite on one ring are spread evenly, so the symmetry needs no angles: the buttons only change how many copies the script writes.
- Each copy holds its own `.gravity-spot`, which reaches the edge of the satellite. Its circles are `at-center` satellites sized in the copy's own lanes: 24 is as wide as the copy. See [gravity spot](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html).
- The triangles are three [`.side`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html) elements on `orbit-12` of the nested system. `spin-lock` turns each copy with its place on the ring, so all of them point outward.
- `--o-from` on the triangle ring turns it half a step, so the corners show between the stacks. The stacks have a background and sit above it, hiding the rest.

## Related

- [Geometric square mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/geometric-square-mandala.html)
- [Starter patterns](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/index.html#starters)
- [Team map demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/07-satellites.html): satellites spread on three rings
- [Sides](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html)

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/

# Mandalas

Mandalas are repetition and nesting, which is what Orbit does: put copies of a satellite on a ring and they spread evenly; put a system inside a satellite and it gets its own center. Everything here is `<div>` elements with borders.

- [Geometric square mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/geometric-square-mandala.html): Nested squares, copied and turned; one to eight folds.
- [Radial symmetry mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/radial-symmetry-mandala.html): Rings of circles with six, eight or twelve folds.
- [Starter patterns](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/index.html#starters): A hexagonal flower and a rosette.

## Starter patterns

### Hexagonal flower

Six circles around a hexagon. The hexagon is six `.side` elements on the outer ring of a system nested in the center satellite.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang" role="img" aria-label="Hexagon surrounded by six circles">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- Six circles, 60° apart, each as wide as the distance to the center. -->
      <div class="orbit-5 petals" style="--o-size-ratio: 10"></div>
      <!-- The hexagon: a system in a satellite, with six sides on its orbit-12. -->
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 10">
        <div class="satellite at-center">
          <div class="gravity-spot"><div class="orbit-12 hexagon"></div></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.petals .satellite { border: 1px solid var(--accent); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, transparent); }
.hexagon .side { height: 2px; background: var(--amber); }
```

```js
document.querySelector('.petals').innerHTML = '<div class="satellite"></div>'.repeat(6);
document.querySelector('.hexagon').innerHTML = '<div class="side"></div>'.repeat(6);
```

- Circles on `orbit-5` with `--o-size-ratio: 10` pass through the center and touch their neighbors' centers: the flower of life.
- Sides connect the places of neighbors on a ring, so six of them on `orbit-12` of the nested system draw a hexagon that fits its satellite. See [sides](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html).

### Rosette

Large circles on one small ring overlap into a rosette. Drag the slider: Orbit respaces them as their number changes.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang rosette" role="img" aria-label="Rosette of 18 circles">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-5 circles" style="--o-size-ratio: 12"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <label class="controls">Circles <input type="range" min="3" max="36" value="18"> <output>18</output></label>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 10px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 76px); }
.circles .satellite { border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--violet) 70%, transparent); }
.circles .satellite:nth-child(odd) { border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 70%, transparent); }
```

```js
const input = document.querySelector('input'), output = document.querySelector('output');
function draw() {
  const n = Number(input.value);
  document.querySelector('.circles').innerHTML = '<div class="satellite"></div>'.repeat(n);
  document.querySelector('.rosette').setAttribute('aria-label', `Rosette of ${n} circles`);
  output.value = n;
}
input.addEventListener('input', draw);
draw();
```

- Every circle is twelve lanes wide on a ring of radius five, so each one reaches past the center to the other side. The count only changes the angle between them.

# Car dashboard

A dashboard screen made of nested systems: a clock and two pods, each a satellite with its own rings inside.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <!-- A 2:1 universe: lanes count from the height, pods sit past orbit-12. -->
  <div class="bigbang dash" role="group" aria-label="Dashboard">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <!-- The clock: one satellite 19 lanes wide, with a seconds ring of its own. -->
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 19">
        <div class="satellite at-center face">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-11 seconds" id="seconds" style="--o-size-ratio: .8"></div>
            <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 18">
              <div class="satellite at-center">
                <div class="capsule readout clock"><span id="date">Sun 11 Apr</span><strong id="time">6:59</strong><span>12° outside</span></div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!-- Two satellites alone on a ring sit opposite each other: right and left. -->
      <div class="orbit-17" style="--o-from: 90deg; --o-size-ratio: 11">
        <div class="satellite pod" role="meter" aria-label="Battery" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="63">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><o-progress class="battery" value="63" shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
            <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 14">
              <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>63%</strong><span>214 km</span></div></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="satellite pod">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-10 range-270 from-225" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><o-progress class="heat" value="0" shape="rounded"></o-progress></div>
            <!-- Two buttons alone on a ring: one on top, one at the bottom. -->
            <div class="orbit-7" style="--o-size-ratio: 4">
              <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><button data-step=".5" aria-label="Warmer">+</button></div></div>
              <div class="satellite"><div class="capsule"><button data-step="-.5" aria-label="Cooler">−</button></div></div>
            </div>
            <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 8">
              <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong id="temp" aria-live="polite">21.5°</strong></div></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage > .dash { width: min(100%, (100vh - 32px) * 2); aspect-ratio: 2 / 1; }

.face, .pod { border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 35%, #18202a, var(--panel) 70%); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line), 0 20px 50px -24px #000; }
.seconds .vector { background: var(--faint); height: 2px; transition: background .3s; }
.seconds .vector.past { background: var(--accent); }
.clock { gap: 4px; }
.clock strong { font-size: clamp(30px, 24cqmin, 92px); font-weight: 300; letter-spacing: -.04em; }
.clock span { font-size: clamp(11px, 5cqmin, 16px); }
.pod .readout strong { font-size: clamp(14px, 16cqmin, 30px); }
.pod .readout span { font-size: clamp(10px, 8cqmin, 13px); }

.pod o-progress { --o-stroke: none; --o-back-fill: #1d2630; }
.battery { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
.heat { --o-fill: var(--amber); }
.pod button { width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 1; padding: 0; border-radius: 50%; font-size: clamp(13px, 9cqmin, 20px); line-height: 1; }
```

```js
// Sixty ticks; the ones up to the current second light up.
const seconds = document.getElementById('seconds');
seconds.innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(60);
const tick = () => {
  const now = new Date();
  [...seconds.children].forEach((v, i) => v.classList.toggle('past', i <= now.getSeconds()));
  document.getElementById('time').textContent = now.toLocaleTimeString('en-GB', { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' });
  document.getElementById('date').textContent = now.toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { weekday: 'short', day: 'numeric', month: 'short' });
};
tick();
setInterval(tick, 1000);

// Climate: 16° to 28°, drawn on the pod's 270° ring.
let temp = 21.5;
const setTemp = t => {
  temp = Math.max(16, Math.min(28, t));
  document.querySelector('.heat').setAttribute('value', (temp - 16) / 12 * 100);
  document.getElementById('temp').textContent = temp.toFixed(1) + '°';
};
document.querySelectorAll('[data-step]').forEach(b => b.addEventListener('click', () => setTemp(temp + Number(b.dataset.step))));
setTemp(temp);
```

## How it's built

- The [universe](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/bigbang.html) is 2:1, so the reach is its height. The clock fills the middle, and the pods sit on `orbit-17`, past the edge of the circle but inside the wide box.
- Two [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html) alone on a ring are spread half a turn apart. `--o-from: 90deg` on the ring turns that pair to right and left.
- The clock and each pod are satellites with a [`.gravity-spot`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html) inside. Every system starts from the defaults, so their rings are counted from their own edge: the seconds ticks, the battery ring and the climate arc.
- The climate buttons are two satellites on one ring of the pod, so they land at the top and the bottom with no angles.
- The clock ticks with a one-second timer that lights the [`.vector`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html)s up to the current second.

Inspired by a design found on [Pinterest](https://pin.it/dP9PlNjFc); an earlier version is on [CodePen](https://codepen.io/zircle/pen/eYqwYPB).

# Layered status rings

Several channels on one radial object, stacked in depth: the one in front is the one you read, and an alert moves its channel to the front.

A home, a car or a server has channels that compete for attention: climate, lights, security. As separate widgets they split the user's focus. Here they share one object, and the order says what matters now.

```html
<main class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang home" role="group" aria-label="Home status">
    <!-- depth turns the rings of this system into layers, front to back. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot depth" style="--o-depth-grow: .42; --o-back-opacity: .4">
      <div class="orbit-6 layer-front" data-depth="0" data-name="Climate" data-value="21.5°">
        <o-progress variant="stroke" value="82"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-6 segments" data-depth="1" data-name="Lights" data-value="5 of 6 on" id="lights"></div>
      <div class="orbit-6 segments" data-depth="2" data-name="Security" data-value="6 of 6 closed" id="security"></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 10">
        <div class="satellite at-center">
          <div class="capsule readout" aria-live="polite"><strong id="value">21.5°</strong><span id="name">Climate</span></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls"><button id="alert">Open a window</button></div>
</main>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 4px; align-content: center; }
.stage > .home { width: min(100%, 100vh - 70px); }

.home o-progress { --o-stroke: var(--text); --o-back-stroke: var(--line); }
.segments o-arc { --o-fill: var(--line); --o-stroke: none; --o-gap: 24; --o-size-ratio: .16; }
.segments o-arc.on { --o-fill: var(--text); }
.segments o-arc.fail { --o-fill: var(--coral); }

/* The alert ripple: only on the ring in front. */
.alert.layer-front::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  border-radius: 50%;
  border: 2px solid var(--coral);
  animation: ripple .9s ease-out infinite;
}
@keyframes ripple {
  from { scale: 1; opacity: .8; }
  to { scale: 1.45; opacity: 0; }
}
.home .readout strong { font-size: clamp(18px, 13cqmin, 30px); }
.home.alerting .readout strong { color: var(--coral); }
```

```js
// Six segments per channel: lights that are on, windows that are closed.
const segments = (ring, on) => {
  ring.innerHTML = Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => `<o-arc value="16.66" class="${i < on ? 'on' : ''}"></o-arc>`).join('');
};
segments(document.getElementById('lights'), 5);
segments(document.getElementById('security'), 6);

const home = document.querySelector('.home');
const layers = [...home.querySelectorAll('.depth > [data-depth]')];
const security = document.getElementById('security');
const windowArc = security.children[2];
const button = document.getElementById('alert');

// Order layers front to back and give each its depth.
const order = list => {
  list.forEach((layer, depth) => {
    layer.dataset.depth = depth;
    layer.classList.toggle('layer-front', depth === 0);
  });
  document.getElementById('name').textContent = list[0].dataset.name;
  document.getElementById('value').textContent = list[0].dataset.value;
};

button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const alerting = security.classList.toggle('alert');
  home.classList.toggle('alerting', alerting);
  windowArc.classList.toggle('fail', alerting);
  windowArc.classList.toggle('on', !alerting);
  security.dataset.value = alerting ? 'Window open' : '6 of 6 closed';
  button.textContent = alerting ? 'Close the window' : 'Open a window';
  // An alert goes in front; resolving it restores the base order.
  order(alerting ? [security, ...layers.filter(l => l !== security)] : layers);
});
```

## How it's built

- `.depth` on the [`.gravity-spot`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html) turns its rings into layers. Each ring gets a `data-depth`, and `.layer-front` marks the one in front.
- All three channels use `orbit-6`. `--o-depth-grow: .42` makes each step back 42% larger (1×, 1.42×, 1.84×), so no two rings share a radius, and the perspective compensation keeps those sizes.
- Climate is a single [`<o-progress variant="stroke">`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html). Lights and Security are six [`<o-arc>`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) segments each, spaced with `--o-gap` and thinned with `--o-size-ratio`.
- Color belongs to the alert: the failing segment, the ripple and the value in the center turn coral, and nothing else is painted.
- Order is data. The script keeps the base order, puts the alerting channel first, and writes `data-depth` from that list. The depth transition is Orbit's own.

## Customization

- `--o-depth-step` (default `-110`) changes the spacing in z, and `--o-perspective` (default `900`) the perspective.
- `--o-depth-compensate: 0` lets farther layers look smaller.
- To hide layers past the third, set `opacity: 0` on `[data-depth="3"]` and above, and show a count instead. Three visible layers is about what people read at a glance.

# Sci-fi interface

A HUD made of loose pieces: partial arcs and rows of dashes, each ring at its own distance from the eye. Tilt it and the rings slide past each other. Move the pointer over the frame.

```html
<div class="stage tilt">
  <div class="bigbang hud" role="img" aria-label="Shields at 87 percent">
    <!-- depth: each ring is a layer; --o-z sets its distance, negative is farther. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot depth outer-perspective">
      <div class="orbit-12 rim" style="--o-z: 40"></div>
      <div class="orbit-11 from-120 range-240 dashes spin-slow" style="--o-z: -20; --o-size-ratio: .5" data-count="48"></div>
      <div class="orbit-10" style="--o-z: 10; --o-size-ratio: .4">
        <o-arc value="22" class="from-215 coral"></o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-9" style="--o-z: -60; --o-size-ratio: .25">
        <o-arc value="35" class="from-320 teal"></o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-8 from-30 spin-back" style="--o-z: -110; --o-size-ratio: .6">
        <o-arc class="teal faint"></o-arc><o-arc class="none"></o-arc><o-arc class="teal faint"></o-arc><o-arc class="none"></o-arc>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-7 from-180 range-100 dashes" style="--o-z: -80; --o-size-ratio: .7" data-count="16"></div>
      <div class="orbit-6" style="--o-z: -150; --o-size-ratio: .35">
        <o-progress class="shields" value="87" shape="rounded"></o-progress>
      </div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-z: 20; --o-size-ratio: 6">
        <div class="satellite at-center"><div class="capsule readout"><strong>87%</strong><span>Shields</span></div></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls"><button type="button" class="pause" aria-pressed="false">Pause</button></div>
</div>
```

```css
/* The perspective lives on the stage; --o-perspective on the system matches it. */
.tilt { perspective: 700px; gap: 10px; }
.tilt > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 80px); }
.hud .depth { --o-perspective: 700; }
.hud { rotate: x var(--rx, 0deg); transform: rotateY(var(--ry, 0deg)); }
.rim { border-color: var(--line); }
.dashes .vector { height: 3px; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 55%, transparent); }
.hud o-arc { --o-stroke: none; }
.teal { --o-fill: var(--accent); }
.coral { --o-fill: var(--coral); }
.faint { opacity: .45; }
.none { --o-fill: none; }
.shields { --o-stroke: none; --o-fill: var(--accent); --o-back-fill: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, transparent); }
.readout strong { font-size: clamp(20px, 24cqmin, 40px); color: var(--accent); }
/* Rings turn with rotate; depth uses transform, so the two add up. */
.spin-slow { animation: spin 60s linear infinite; }
.spin-back { animation: spin 40s linear infinite reverse; }
.paused .spin-slow, .paused .spin-back { animation-play-state: paused; }
@keyframes spin { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
```

```js
// The dashes: data-count vectors per ring.
document.querySelectorAll('[data-count]').forEach((ring) => {
  ring.innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(Number(ring.dataset.count));
});

// Tilt toward the pointer, up to 25°. Without a pointer, sway slowly.
const stage = document.querySelector('.tilt'), hud = document.querySelector('.hud');
const still = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
let pointer = null, rx = 0, ry = 0, paused = false;
const pause = document.querySelector('.pause');
pause.addEventListener('click', () => {
  paused = hud.classList.toggle('paused');
  pause.setAttribute('aria-pressed', paused);
  pause.textContent = paused ? 'Play' : 'Pause';
});
stage.addEventListener('pointermove', (e) => {
  const r = stage.getBoundingClientRect();
  pointer = [(e.clientX - r.left) / r.width - 0.5, (e.clientY - r.top) / r.height - 0.5];
});
stage.addEventListener('pointerleave', () => { pointer = null; });
function frame(t) {
  const [x, y] = pointer || (still || paused ? [0, 0] : [Math.sin(t / 2400) * 0.3, Math.cos(t / 3100) * 0.25]);
  ry += (x * 50 - ry) * 0.08;
  rx += (-y * 50 - rx) * 0.08;
  hud.style.setProperty('--rx', `${rx}deg`);
  hud.style.setProperty('--ry', `${ry}deg`);
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}
requestAnimationFrame(frame);
```

## How it's built

- Arcs with a `value` and a `from-N` draw a partial band anywhere on a ring; arcs without one split the ring, and a transparent one leaves a gap. See [arcs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html).
- The dashes are [vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html) written by the script, 48 on a 240° range and 16 on 100°.
- `depth` on the `.gravity-spot` turns each ring into a layer, and `--o-z` places it in front or behind. Layers keep their apparent size, so the face looks flat until it tilts. See [depth](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html).
- `outer-perspective` leaves the perspective to the stage, so the whole universe can turn with `rotateY` and `rotate: x`.
- Two rings also spin with a CSS animation on `rotate`, which adds to the depth transform instead of replacing it. The button pauses them and the sway.

## Related

- [Abstract orbital map](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/abstract_map.html)
- [Layered status rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/layered-status-rings.html): depth layers that change order
- [Depth layers demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/11-depth-layers.html)
- [Sci-fi and game interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/sci-fi-game-uis.html)

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/abstract_map.html

# Abstract orbital map

A star chart where every planet is a system of its own, with its own rings and moons. Each ring turns at its own speed with a plain CSS animation on `rotate`.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang map" role="img" aria-label="Star chart with two planets and their moons">
    <div class="gravity-spot">
      <div class="orbit-12 line"></div>
      <div class="orbit-12 ticks" style="--o-size-ratio: .35"></div>
      <div class="orbit-9 line dashed"></div>
      <div class="orbit-6 line dashed"></div>
      <div class="orbit-3 line"></div>
      <!-- Meridians: twelve long vectors from the center. -->
      <div class="orbit-6 meridians" style="--o-size-ratio: 12"></div>

      <!-- A planet: a satellite with a system inside. Its ring turns, and the planet with it. -->
      <div class="orbit-9 turn" style="--time: 90s">
        <div class="satellite angle-60" style="--o-size-ratio: 5">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 9"><div class="satellite at-center planet"></div></div>
            <div class="orbit-8 line dashed"></div>
            <div class="orbit-11 turn" style="--time: 12s">
              <div class="satellite moon" style="--o-size-ratio: 2"></div>
            </div>
            <div class="orbit-16 turn" style="--time: 90s; --dir: reverse">
              <div class="satellite angle-135 label"><div class="capsule">Meridian</div></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="orbit-6 turn" style="--time: 50s; --dir: reverse">
        <div class="satellite angle-210" style="--o-size-ratio: 3.4">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 7"><div class="satellite at-center planet small"></div></div>
            <div class="orbit-10 turn" style="--time: 8s">
              <div class="satellite moon" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"></div>
              <div class="satellite moon" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="orbit-3 turn" style="--time: 20s"><div class="satellite moon angle-20" style="--o-size-ratio: .6"></div></div>
      <div class="orbit-0" style="--o-size-ratio: 1.6"><div class="satellite at-center star"></div></div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="controls"><button type="button" class="pause" aria-pressed="false">Pause</button></div>
</div>
```

```css
.stage { gap: 10px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 80px); }
.line { border-color: var(--line); }
.dashed { border-style: dashed; }
.ticks .vector { background: var(--faint); }
.meridians .vector { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--line) 70%, transparent); }
.star { background: var(--amber); box-shadow: 0 0 24px 6px color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber) 45%, transparent); }
.planet { background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, var(--accent), color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 40%, black)); }
.planet.small { background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, var(--violet), #4b3a87); }
.moon { background: var(--text); }
.label .capsule { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted); white-space: nowrap; }
/* Every .turn ring spins; --time and --dir set its speed and way. */
.turn { animation: spin var(--time) linear infinite var(--dir, normal); }
.paused .turn { animation-play-state: paused; }
@keyframes spin { to { rotate: 360deg; } }
```

```js
document.querySelector('.ticks').innerHTML = '<div class="vector inner-orbit"></div>'.repeat(72);
document.querySelector('.meridians').innerHTML = '<div class="vector"></div>'.repeat(12);

// Moving content that runs for long should have a way to stop it.
const pause = document.querySelector('.pause');
pause.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const paused = document.querySelector('.map').classList.toggle('paused');
  pause.setAttribute('aria-pressed', paused);
  pause.textContent = paused ? 'Play' : 'Pause';
});
```

## How it's built

- Each planet is a satellite with its own `.gravity-spot`, so it gets its own twelve lanes for a core, a dashed ring and moons. See [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html).
- Rings are drawn by their border. An empty ring is just a circle, so the chart's guides are rings with nothing on them; the ticks and meridians are [vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html).
- A ring with `rotate` turns everything on it. The `.turn` class animates it, and `--time` and `--dir` on each ring set the speed and the direction.
- The label rides on `orbit-16` of the planet's system, past its edge. That ring turns back as fast as the planet's ring, so the two cancel out and the word stays upright beside the planet.

Inspired by a design found on [Pinterest](https://pin.it/dP9PlNjFc).

- [Sci-fi interface](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/scifi.html)
- [Nested systems demo](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/08-nested-orbits.html)
- [Gravity spot](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html): a satellite is a universe too

# Chemical structure

Caffeine, drawn as two systems side by side: a six-membered ring and a five-membered one that share a bond. Each ring of bonds is a polygon of `.side` elements, each atom a satellite.

```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="bigbang molecule" role="img" aria-label="Structure of caffeine">
    <!-- A reach of 150cqmin draws everything half again as large. -->
    <div class="gravity-spot" style="--o-force: 150cqmin">
      <!-- The six-membered ring: a system as wide as the universe, two lanes left of center. -->
      <div class="orbit-2" style="--o-size-ratio: 24">
        <div class="satellite angle-270">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-3 bonds"></div>
            <!-- Bonds to the outside, and the second line of the double bond at the top. -->
            <div class="orbit-3" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.6">
              <div class="vector outer-orbit angle-0"></div>
              <div class="vector outer-orbit angle-180"></div>
              <div class="vector outer-orbit angle-240"></div>
              <div class="vector outer-orbit angle-300"></div>
            </div>
            <div class="orbit-3" style="--o-size-ratio: .5">
              <div class="satellite angle-180 atom n"><div class="capsule">N</div></div>
              <div class="satellite angle-300 atom n"><div class="capsule">N</div></div>
            </div>
            <!-- Groups on the outside, spread over half the circle, counterclockwise. -->
            <div class="orbit-6 range-180 ccw fit-range" style="--o-size-ratio: .5">
              <div class="satellite inner-orbit atom o"><div class="capsule">O</div></div>
              <div class="satellite atom"><div class="capsule">H<sub>3</sub>C</div></div>
              <div class="satellite atom o"><div class="capsule">O</div></div>
              <div class="satellite atom"><div class="capsule">CH<sub>3</sub></div></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
      <!-- The five-membered ring, its center placed so the two rings share a bond. -->
      <div class="orbit-3 shrink-35" style="--o-size-ratio: 24">
        <div class="satellite angle-90">
          <div class="gravity-spot">
            <div class="orbit-3 shrink-25 from-36 bonds"></div>
            <div class="orbit-3 shrink-75 from-36 double"></div>
            <div class="orbit-3 shrink-25" style="--o-size-ratio: 2.4"><div class="vector outer-orbit angle-18"></div></div>
            <div class="orbit-3 shrink-25" style="--o-size-ratio: .6">
              <div class="satellite angle-18 atom n"><div class="capsule">N</div></div>
              <div class="satellite angle-165 atom n"><div class="capsule">N</div></div>
            </div>
            <div class="orbit-6 shrink-5" style="--o-size-ratio: .6">
              <div class="satellite angle-18 atom"><div class="capsule">CH<sub>3</sub></div></div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="readout"><strong>C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>10</sub>N<sub>4</sub>O<sub>2</sub></strong><span>Caffeine</span></p>
</div>
```

```css
body { background: var(--bg); }
.stage { gap: 4px; }
.stage > .bigbang { width: min(100%, 100vh - 90px); }
.molecule { color: #c3ccd6; }
.vector, .side { height: 2px; }
/* An atom hides the bonds behind its letter with the page color. */
.atom { background: var(--bg); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text); }
.atom sub { font-size: .7em; }
.n { color: var(--blue); }
.o { color: var(--coral); }
.readout { margin: 0; }
.readout strong { font-size: 20px; letter-spacing: 0; }
```

```js
// Six sides make the hexagon. The pentagon is drawn twice: once whole, once with
// every other side left out, slightly inside, for the double bonds.
document.querySelector('.molecule .bonds').innerHTML = '<div class="side"></div>'.repeat(6);
document.querySelectorAll('.molecule .bonds')[1].innerHTML = '<div class="side"></div>'.repeat(5);
document.querySelector('.molecule .double').innerHTML =
  ['hidden', '', 'hidden', '', 'hidden'].map((c) => `<div class="side" ${c}></div>`).join('');
```

## How it's built

- Sides connect neighboring places on a ring, so six [`.side`](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html) elements make a hexagon and five a pentagon. The double bonds of the pentagon are a second, smaller pentagon with every other side hidden.
- Each ring of atoms is its own `.gravity-spot` inside a satellite as wide as the universe, so both use lanes of the same size. See [gravity spot](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/gravity-spot.html).
- The hexagon's satellite sits two lanes left of the center, the pentagon's on `orbit-3 shrink-35` to the right: the distance at which the two rings share a bond. `--o-force: 150cqmin` makes the reach larger than the universe, so the molecule fills the frame.
- Atoms are satellites at fixed angles. Their background is the page color, which hides the bonds behind each letter.
- Single bonds to the outside are [vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html) at `angle-N`; methyls and oxygens ride on `orbit-6`, spread over half the circle with `range-180 ccw fit-range`.

Benzene, pyridine or furan use the same parts with a different number of sides.

## Related

- [Geometric square mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/geometric-square-mandala.html): systems inside satellites
- [Hexagonal flower](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/index.html#starters): a hexagon of sides
- [Sides](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/side.html)

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/

# Gauges

A gauge is an arc, some labels and something that points. In Orbit the arc is a ring of `<o-arc>` bands, the labels are curved text or satellites, and the needle is a `.vector` on a ring turned with `rotate`. All of it is HTML you can style and inspect.

- [180° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/180-degree-gauge.html): Five named zones and a needle on a half circle.
- [240° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/240-degree-gauge.html): A stepped speedometer: bands light up with the speed.
- [Fuel gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/fuel-gauge.html): A 90° dial with E, F and a reserve, in a box cut to fit.

For a gauge with ticks, ranges and a value API already wired, see the [Orbit Kit gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/gauge.html).

## Related

- [Progress rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/index.html): a value without a needle
- [Knobs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/index.html): gauges you can turn
- [Arcs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html) and [vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html)

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/

# Progress rings

A circular progress bar in Orbit is one element, `<o-progress value="60">`, inside a ring. Its color, track, ends and thickness are CSS. These four cover the usual patterns.

- [Progress with background](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-background.html): A fill over its track, number in the middle.
- [Dashed progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/dashed-circular-progress-bar.html): Ten segments for progress counted in steps.
- [Progress with handle](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-handle.html): A circular slider you can drag.
- [Stacked progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/stacked-circular-progress-bars.html): Three live metrics, labeled in the open quarter.

## Related

- [Progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/progress.html)
- [Orbit Kit rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/rings.html)
- [Gauges](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/index.html): when you want a needle
- [Fitness and health apps](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html)

# Knobs and menus

Controls that live on a circle. A knob is a body, ticks and an indicator that turns; a pie menu is a ring of clickable arcs. Use a continuous arc for values like gain, LEDs for discrete steps, and a pie menu when the choices fit around a point.

- [Knob with progress bar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/knob-with-progress-bar.html): A gain knob whose arc grows from the center.
- [LED knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/led-knob.html): Eleven LEDs and a knob that snaps between them.
- [Pie menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/piemenu.html): Wedges that open their options on an outer ring.

All three work with the pointer and the keyboard. [Build a knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/guide.html) explains that part step by step, and the [Kit knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html) and [Kit menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/menu.html) come with it built in.

## Related

- [Progress rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/index.html)
- [Audio app interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/audio-app-ui.html)

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/

# Charts

Pies, donuts and sunbursts are arcs with values. Put `<o-arc value="…">` elements in a ring and they follow each other around it, each taking its share. Orbit draws the paths; you bring the data.

- [Donut chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/donut-chart.html): Five arcs with values, and two weeks to switch.
- [Pie chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/pie-chart.html): Slices that slide out on hover and focus.
- [Sunburst chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/sunburst-chart.html): Two levels of nested data that line up on their own.
- A donut leaves room in the middle for a total.
- A pie is denser, and pairs well with a legend outside it.
- A sunburst shows nested categories, one ring per level.

## Related

- [Arcs](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/arc.html)
- [Orbit Kit donut](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/donut.html)
- [Dashboards](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/dashboards.html)

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/

# Watches and clocks

A watch face is many things around one center: a bezel, sixty ticks, twelve numbers, hands and sometimes whole sub-dials. In Orbit the ticks are vectors, the numbers are satellites, each hand is a vector on a ring that turns, and a sub-dial is a satellite with its own system. All of them tell the real time.

- [Minimalist analog clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/minimalist-analog-clock.html): Ticks, numbers and three hands, on the real time.
- [Chronograph](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/chronograph-watch-face.html): Three sub-dials, each its own system, and a working stopwatch.
- [Roman numeral clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/roman-numeral-clock-face.html): Numerals along the radius, with spin-lock and flip.
- [Smartwatch face](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/smartwatch-face.html): Time and date as curved text along the bezel.
- [Circular timer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/circular_time.html): Turn the wheel to set it; three rings share one angle.

## Related

- [Orbit Kit clock](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/clock.html)
- [Calendars](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/calendar/index.html)
- [Vectors](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/vector.html) and [satellites](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/reference/satellite.html)

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/dashboards.html

# Dashboards

A single headline number, a part of a whole, progress toward a goal: these read best on a circle. Orbit builds gauges, rings and donuts from HTML and CSS, so they take your design tokens, dark mode and transitions like the rest of the page, and you can inspect them in DevTools.

## Where it fits

- A design system that needs its own gauge, donut and progress components instead of a chart library's defaults.
- Small pages where a chart library would be most of the JavaScript.
- Values that change: set `value` on an `<o-progress>` or `<o-arc>` and it redraws on the next frame.

## Where it does not

- Time series and multi-series charts. Use a charting library.
- Thousands of data points. Canvas handles that better than the DOM.

## Start from

- [Speedometer](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/04-arrow-gauge.html): Ticks, zones and a needle on one 270° dial.
- [240° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/240-degree-gauge.html): A headline KPI on a dial.
- [Stacked progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/stacked-circular-progress-bars.html): Three related metrics around one center.
- [Donut chart](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/charts/donut-chart.html): A breakdown with room for a total.
- [Car dashboard](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/dashboard.html): A whole panel built from nested systems.

A monitoring view could pair a 240° gauge for CPU with three small rings for memory, disk and network, and a donut for traffic by region. Each one is a `.bigbang` as big as its card. The [Orbit Kit](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/index.html) has gauge, donut and rings components ready to use.

## Related

- [Audio app interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/audio-app-ui.html)
- [Fitness and health apps](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html)
- [IoT and hardware interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/iot-and-hardware-ui.html)
- [Sci-fi and game interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/sci-fi-game-uis.html)
- [All examples](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/index.html)
