Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/iot-and-hardware-ui.html

# IoT and hardware interfaces

Devices are full of dials: thermostats, fan speeds, fuel and battery levels, valve positions. The quantities are continuous and bounded, so a radial control matches how people think of the thing. Orbit gives you those controls as HTML that any framework, or none, can update from a WebSocket or MQTT message.

## Where it fits

- Smart-home panels and cards that should look the same across platforms.
- Companion apps for devices with a knob or a gauge of their own: e-bikes, printers, brewing controllers.
- Device screens prototyped in HTML, then shipped in a web view.
- Live telemetry: one attribute or custom property per message, redrawn on the next frame.

## Where it does not

- Old embedded browsers. Orbit needs container query units and CSS `sin()` and `cos()`.
- Illustrated, branded controls. Draw the illustration and put an Orbit gauge on top for the values.

## Start from

- [Half gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/06-semicircle.html): A battery in 20 cells on a half circle.
- [Fuel gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/fuel-gauge.html): A compact level instrument.
- [Knob with progress bar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/knob-with-progress-bar.html): A setpoint control.
- [Layered status rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/layered-status-rings.html): Several channels in one object; alerts come to the front.
- [Progress with background](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/circular-progress-with-background.html): Battery, fill level, filter life.

A thermostat screen could be a large temperature gauge, a knob for the setpoint and two small rings for humidity and filter life. The [Kit instrument](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/instrument.html) and [gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/gauge.html) are good starting points.

## Related

- [Audio app interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/audio-app-ui.html)
- [Dashboards](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/dashboards.html)
- [Fitness and health apps](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html)
- [Sci-fi and game interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/sci-fi-game-uis.html)
- [All examples](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/index.html)

---

Source: https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html

# Fitness and health apps

Activity rings made the circle the way to show a daily goal: you see how close you are without reading a number. With Orbit, rings, gauges and watch faces are a handful of HTML elements, updated by setting a value.

## Where it fits

- Goal rings for steps, calories, exercise, water or sleep.
- Live readouts during a workout, like heart rate from a Bluetooth sensor.
- Summary screens with several radial figures.
- Web and PWA versions of an app, without a chart library. Give each ring `role="meter"` or `progressbar` and its value, and screen readers announce it.

## Where it does not

- Trends over days, like weight or sleep history. Use a charting library.
- Route maps and heatmaps.

## Start from

- [Progress rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/01-minimal-gauge.html): Three goals with rounded ends.
- [Stacked progress](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/progress/stacked-circular-progress-bars.html): Three goals around one center.
- [180° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/180-degree-gauge.html): A zone readout, like heart rate.
- [Smartwatch face](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/watches/smartwatch-face.html): Live time with complications.

A daily summary could be three rings at the top, a heart-rate gauge under them and a row of small dials for water, sleep and steps. The [Kit rings](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/rings.html) component does the first part.

# Audio app interfaces

Audio software never gave up the knob. It maps a wide range to a small gesture, and your hand remembers where it was. Orbit gives you the knob, its ticks, its arc and the meters around it as HTML, so the only script you write maps a drag to a value.

## Where it fits

- Web audio tools and plugins built on Web Audio or AudioWorklet.
- Synth and effect layouts you want to try with users before building them natively.
- Companion apps for controllers, interfaces and MIDI gear.
- Controls that need to be accessible: a knob is a DOM element, so it can be a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuenow` and arrow keys.

## Where it does not

- A large mixer with hundreds of meters moving at audio rate. Draw those on a canvas.
- Photographic knobs. Use an image for the texture and Orbit for the value around it.

## Start from

- [Knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/05-knob.html): Drag, scroll or use the keys.
- [Knob with progress bar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/knob-with-progress-bar.html): A continuous value with ticks and an arc.
- [LED knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/knobs/led-knob.html): Stepped values, one light per step.
- [240° gauge](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/gauges/240-degree-gauge.html): A level meter with zones.

An EQ, for example, is four knobs in a row with their values in the middle, an input and an output meter, and a ring around the bypass button. [Build a knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/guide.html) covers drag, wheel and keyboard. The [Kit knob](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/kit/knob.html) has all of it ready.

## Related

- [Dashboards](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/dashboards.html)
- [Fitness and health apps](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/fitness-and-health-apps.html)
- [IoT and hardware interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/iot-and-hardware-ui.html)
- [Sci-fi and game interfaces](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/use-cases/sci-fi-game-uis.html)
- [All examples](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/index.html)

# Sci-fi and game interfaces

Sci-fi interfaces live on circles: concentric rings, turning bezels, curved labels, geometry in the background. Orbit builds those from HTML and CSS, and animates them with ordinary keyframes on `rotate` and `opacity`, which the browser composites without your script.

## Where it fits

- HUDs and menus over a web game, as a DOM layer on top of the canvas.
- Game interfaces prototyped in HTML before they move to an engine.
- Game websites that should speak the game's visual language.
- Decorative backgrounds: mandalas, turning bezels, rings behind content.

## Where it does not

- The game itself. Orbit is for the interface around it.
- Pixel art. Orbit draws smooth geometry.

## Start from

- [Radar](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/demos/10-radar.html): A sweeping beam and contacts that flash in time.
- [Sci-fi interface](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/scifi.html): Arcs and dashes at different depths, tilting with the pointer.
- [Abstract orbital map](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/abstract_map.html): Planets that are systems of their own, each ring turning.
- [Pie menu](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/piemenu.html): A radial menu with submenus.
- [Radial symmetry mandala](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/examples/mandalas/radial-symmetry-mandala.html): Geometry for backgrounds and emblems.

A cockpit could be a slow mandala behind everything, gauges for shields and hull, a cluster of sub-dials for cooldowns and the target's name in curved text around the bezel. For layers that move in z, see [depth layers](https://zumerlab.github.io/orbit/craft/depth.html).
